title: Senior Facilities Mechanical Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

As a Facilities Mechanical Engineer, you will play a critical role in ensuring the availability, reliability, and maintenance of essential mechanical and HVAC systems that support manufacturing, clean room, and research and development activities. You will design, analyze, and troubleshoot mechanical systems to deliver innovative solutions, drive system reliability, and support operational excellence on a day-to-day basis. This role requires regular onsite presence to fulfill key responsibilities and make a tangible impact on Intel's operations and infrastructure.

Business group

Intel Corporation's Facilities Operations team is dedicated to maintaining and optimizing the mechanical infrastructure that supports Intel's global manufacturing and research efforts. The team ensures that mechanical systems operate safely, reliably, and efficiently, enabling Intel to meet its business objectives and deliver cutting-edge products to customers. Joining this group means contributing to Intel's success by providing world-class engineering solutions and supporting sustainability and innovation across facilities.

Key Responsibilities

  • Ensure the reliability, availability, and maintenance of mechanical and HVAC systems such as chilled water plants, boilers, environmental abatement systems, and clean room equipment.
  • Design, analyze, and troubleshoot mechanical systems to identify and resolve systematic issues.
  • Develop engineering scopes of work for mechanical projects and conduct design reviews and evaluations.
  • Partner with internal customers and operations teams to implement engineering solutions that support equipment and systems needs.
  • Conduct feasibility studies and testing on new and modified designs, and oversee prototype fabrication and design testing.
  • Collaborate with maintenance service providers to ensure mechanical systems are operated and maintained within specified limits.
  • Create mechanical systems roadmaps and asset replacement strategies to ensure reliability, redundancy, and capacity for facility expansions and renovations.
  • Support Intel's safety, reliability, and environmental objectives through daily tactical efforts in mechanical systems management.

Behavioral traits

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to drive innovative solutions.
  • Effective communication skills to collaborate across teams and with stakeholders.
  • Enthusiasm for contributing to sustainability initiatives and operational excellence.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum qualifications and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.  This position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, or a related field, with 10+ years of experience in designing, maintaining, and optimizing mechanical systems OR Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering with 6+ years of relevant experience OR PhD in Mechanical Engineering with 3+ years of relevant experience.
  • Experience mentioned above should be a combination of the following areas:
    • Mechanical system design, analysis, and troubleshooting methodologies.
    • Knowledge of HVAC systems or environmental compliance exhaust systems or mechanical process equipment.
    • Engineering tools for system evaluation and design documentation.
    • Familiarity with safety and environmental regulations related to facilities management.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Prior experience working in manufacturing or clean room facilities.
  • Develop long-term strategies for system reliability and capacity planning.

Joining Intel's Facilities team offers an exciting opportunity to shape the foundation of a company known for innovation and excellence. Be part of an environment where your expertise drives impactful solutions and supports Intel's growth.

Your day-to-day work will involve collaborating across engineering disciplines to design and validate photonic integrated circuits (PICs) components such as modulators, detectors, lasers, and passive devices, ensuring they meet performance, reliability, and manufacturability requirements. This role offers a unique opportunity to push the boundaries of photonics technology and drive innovation in data center and AI applications.

About the Team

Intel's Integrated Photonics Solutions (IPS) team is a global leader in silicon photonics integration, pioneering high-performance optical solutions that enable transformative scalability in data center bandwidth and speeds. The team focuses on research, development, and commercialization of advanced photonic technologies that drive Intel's vision of delivering cutting-edge innovations in optical communications and AI-driven systems. Joining IPS means becoming part of an innovative team dedicated to redefining the future of high-volume photonic integration.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, simulate, and optimize photonic components such as modulators, passive devices, lasers, and detectors for PICs
  • Conduct tolerance analysis to ensure components maintain reliability and performance under various operating conditions
  • Lead test chip development, including design, layout, tapeout, testing, and validation processes
  • Analyze characterization data, identify performance gaps, and develop strategies for optimization and improvement
  • Develop and refine modeling methodologies for photonic components and propose innovative test approaches
  • Research emerging photonics technologies to define next-generation architectures and drive intellectual property development
  • Collaborate with cross-disciplinary engineering teams to align component designs with system-level requirements

To Be Successful in This Role, You Should Demonstrate

  • Strong collaboration skills with the ability to work effectively across engineering disciplines
  • A proactive approach to problem-solving with a drive to push the boundaries of photonics technology
  • Strong communication skills to effectively present designs and findings to cross-functional teams


Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's or BS degree in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Optical Science, or a related field, and 6+ years of relevant experience; or Master's degree with 4+ years of relevant experience; or Ph.D. with 2+ years of relevant experience in photonic device design and simulation


The experience must include:

  • Proficiency in optical and RF design and simulation tools such as Lumerical (FDTD, MODE, DEVICE, Interconnect), RSoft, or Tidy3D
  • Hands-on experience in photonic integrated circuit design, from concept through high-volume manufacturing
  • Familiarity with photonic test methodologies and equipment, including optical spectrum analyzers, tunable lasers, and optical vector analyzers
  • Experience managing statistical analysis of photonic test data using tools like JMP or programming languages such as Python or Matlab

Preferred Qualifications

  • Proficiency in layout tools such as Cadence or KLayout for component design and PIC tapeouts
  • Experience with advanced passive or active silicon photonic components such as ring modulators, Mach-Zehnder interferometers, EAM's/EML's
  • Knowledge of system-level link modeling, Monte Carlo analysis, and optical coupling solutions
  • Familiarity with inverse design methodologies and circuit-level simulations
  • Understanding of advanced electronic ICs and integration with photonic systems, including drivers, TIAs, DSPs, and modulators

Join Intel's Integrated Photonics Solutions team and be at the forefront of innovation in optical communication technologies. Shape the future of photonic integration and contribute to groundbreaking advancements in data centers and AI-driven solutions.

title: Senior DFT Logic Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Group

Intel Foundry is a systems foundry dedicated to transforming the global semiconductor industry by delivering cutting-edge silicon process and packaging technology leadership for the AI era. With a focus on scalability, AI advancement, and shaping the future, we provide an unparalleled blend of an industry-leading technology, a rich IP portfolio, a world-class design ecosystem, and an operationally resilient global manufacturing supply chain.


Intel Foundry will be differentiated from other foundries with a combination of leading-edge packaging and process technology, committed capacity in the US and Europe, and a world-class IP portfolio that customers can choose from, including x86 cores, graphics, media, display, AI, interconnect, fabric and other critical foundational IP's, along with Arm and RISC-V ecosystem IP's. Foundry Services will also provide access to silicon design services to help our customers seamlessly turn silicon into solutions, using industry standard design packages. Come join us and do something wonderful.


The Aerospace, Defense, Government (ADG) - The Senior DFT Logic Design Engineer provides technical support to Intel Foundry Services customers on our PDKs, DFT/DFM insertion, ATPG validation methodology and flows.

The successful candidate will:

  • Collaborate with internal teams across Intel and external stakeholders such as foundry customers' design teams, IP providers, and EDA vendors on issue resolution.
  • Create content, application notes and deliver technical training/presentations.
  • Drive quality of ASIC DFT/DFM and ATPG validation methodology, capability/flow and documentation for block level and SOC level.
  • Support and provide Tool/Flow/Methodology on customer issues and challenges for successful customer tape-outs, and to increase customer satisfaction.

Core Competencies

  • Customer-oriented attitude and mindset.
  • Self-driven and results-oriented, capable of effectively working multiple tasks.
  • Team player - effective team-work skillset to drive and find solutions for customer design implementation issues/challenges.
  • Analytical problem-solving skills.
  • Effective communication skills, as well as experience in collaboration, listening and providing feedback.

The Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position.  Minimum qualifications listed below would be obtained through a combination of industry relevant job experience, internship experience and / or schoolwork/classes/research. The preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

Minimum Qualifications

  • US Citizenship required.
  • Ability to obtain a US Government Security Clearance.
  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical / Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or in a STEM related field of study.
  • 3+ years of experience with advanced CMOS processes (16nm and below).
  • 3+ years of experience in implementing ASIC DFT/DFM insertion (MBIST, LBIST, SCAN, JTAG, ...) at ASIC design block level and at full chip level. Performing ATPG validation and DFT timing and DFT signoff at SOC level.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Active US Government Security Clearance with a minimum of Secret level.

  • Experience in working with RTL and Hard IP designers on DFT/DFM implementation methodology.

  • Experience with providing technical direction to engineering teams, including but not limited to customer support, driving methodologies to streamline design work
  • Customer facing experience.
  • Semiconductor foundry experience.

  • Direct customer engagement and technical leadership in advanced semiconductor design
  • Access to Intel's most advanced foundry technologies and comprehensive EDA tool suites
  • Competitive compensation
  • Professional development in DFT methodologies and foundry services

title: Senior Analog Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The world is transforming - and so is Intel. Intel is a company of bold and curious inventors and problem solvers who create some of the most astounding technology advancements and experiences in the world. With a legacy of relentless innovation and a commitment to bring smart, connected devices to every person on Earth, our diverse and brilliant teams are continually searching for tomorrow's technology and revel in the challenge that changing the world for the better brings. We work every single day to design and manufacture silicon products that empower people's digital lives. Come join us and do something wonderful.

Business group

Intel Integrated Photonics Solutions (IPS), part of the Data Center Group, is a leader in silicon photonics integration. Our team drives innovation through advanced technology and scalable, high-volume manufacturing of silicon photonics products. We are committed to developing next-generation optical connectivity solutions that enable continued data center bandwidth growth through smaller form factors, co-packaged optics, and data rates scaling from 400G today to 3.2T and beyond.
 

The Role and Impact

We are seeking a highly motivated Senior Analog Design Engineer to join our growing team and help accelerate the development of industry-leading silicon photonics solutions. As a Senior Analog Design Engineer, you will contribute to the Silicon Photonics Solutions Group's mission of transforming data center connectivity and strengthening Intel's leadership in networking technologies.

In this role, you will be responsible for:

  • The architecture, design, implementation, and validation of high-speed analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits used in advanced optical interconnect products.
  • You will collaborate closely with cross-functional design teams to deliver innovative solutions from concept through production.
  • Define circuit architectures and develop designs that meet power, performance, and functionality requirements for next-generation optical interconnects.
  • Lead block-level design and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to deliver key integrated circuit components.
  • Architect, design, and validate high-speed, low-voltage, low-power analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits.
  • Work closely with digital design teams to ensure successful integration and product execution.
  • Plan and execute design activities while balancing performance, schedule, and quality objectives.
  • Guide to the development of post-silicon test and characterization plans.
  • Create and maintain comprehensive design documentation, including design specifications, reviews, and technical reports.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Experience listed below would be obtained through a combination of your degree, research and or relevant previous job and or internship experiences. 


Minimum Qualifications:
M.S. degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field with 3+ years of industry experience or PhD & 0 years in the following:

  • Hands-on experience designing high-speed circuit blocks such as amplifiers, drivers, equalizers, PLLs, phase interpolators, and clock and data recovery (CDR) circuits for data rates of 32 Gbps and above.
  • Experience designing inductors, transmission lines, transimpedance amplifiers (TIAs), and optical modulator drivers.
  • Strong expertise in high-speed serial link design and analog CMOS/BiCMOS circuit design using deep-submicron process technologies.
  • Experience with full-chip integration, ESD design considerations, and verification methodologies.



Preferred Qualifications:

  • Familiarity with optical communication systems.
  • Experience developing 400G, 800G, and 1.6T optical links.
  • Experience with package design and test setup development.
  • Experience designing precision analog circuits such as ADCs and DACs.
  • Experience with PAM4 and NRZ link architectures.
  • Strong understanding of mixed-signal design methodologies and flows.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

title: Packaging Module Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:

Job Description: 

Intel is one of the world's most iconic and innovative technology companies, dedicated to designing and manufacturing the foundational semiconductor technologies that power the modern world. From the devices in your pocket to the data centers running the internet, Intel's innovations are everywhere. With a bold vision for the future of computing — spanning artificial intelligence, advanced packaging, and next-generation chip architectures — Intel is transforming what's possible. Our Arizona campuses are among the most advanced semiconductor research, development, and manufacturing facilities on the planet, and they're growing. Join us and be part of something truly world-changing.

Are you ready to shape the future of semiconductor technology? We're looking for a talented and driven Packaging Module Development Engineer to join our Advanced Packaging Technology & Manufacturing (APTM) team in Chandler, Arizona.

In this role, you'll be at the cutting edge of semiconductor packaging innovation — designing, optimizing, and qualifying the assembly processes and equipment that make Intel's most advanced products possible. You'll work on technologies that power mobile devices, edge computing platforms, and high-performance computing systems used by millions of people around the world.   • Establish and maintain specifications for materials and equipment, partnering with suppliers to meet performance and quality standards.

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

APTD LYA is a Foundry Labs Network organization that supports back-end package assembly and wafer level assembly sort and test fails to help root cause yield loss and in-line failures. Job Details:

As a Manufacturing Quality and Reliability Engineer, you will play a key role in ensuring Intel's manufacturing ramps transition seamlessly to high-volume production while maintaining exceptional product quality and reliability standards. You will evaluate materials, processes, and testing mechanisms, conduct quality audits, and implement improvements that directly enhance Intel's ability to deliver cutting-edge technology solutions. descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel Foundry Construction and Sourcing (FCS) is at the heart of building the world's most advanced semiconductor manufacturing facilities. We are a team of passionate engineers, project managers, and construction professionals dedicated to delivering cutting-edge factories that power Intel's global technology operations. At Intel, we believe in pushing boundaries, fostering innovation, and creating a culture where safety, collaboration, and excellence are at the forefront of everything we do. Join us and be part of a team that is literally building the future of technology.

We are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Construction Tool Equipment Install Engineer to join our Project Execution Team at our Hillsboro, Oregon campus. In this role, you will serve as the primary Intel equipment owner from pre-design through SL2 Signoff, working closely with factory owners, suppliers, trade contractors, and cross-functional stakeholders to ensure the seamless installation of semiconductor manufacturing tools and equipment. This is a hands-on, high-impact role that sits at the intersection of engineering, project management, and construction execution.

This is a fixed-term opportunity lasting approximately 12 months, with the potential for extension subject to the approval of both parties.

Key Responsibilities

  • Equipment & Delivery Management: Collaborate with factory owners and stakeholders to ensure tools, equipment, and kits are ordered and delivered in alignment with the Tool Install schedule. Track and resolve issues in a timely manner, escalating where required.

  • Stakeholder Representation: Represent the local FCS site in CTI and VF forums, acting as the primary point of contact for all equipment-related matters.

  • Financial Planning & Forecasting: Work with stakeholders to forecast equipment workload and funding requirements, ensuring alignment with FCS Financial Planning and Reporting Cycles. Ensure purchase orders and commitments are in place to meet program goals.

  • Project Planning: Translate business and technical requirements into high-quality project plans that enable accurate and cost-effective delivery of scope.

  • Problem Resolution: Act as the primary Intel equipment owner from pre-design through SL2 Signoff, driving troubleshooting efforts to lean, decisive resolution to mitigate delays on assigned projects.

  • Innovation Mindset: You continuously look for ways to improve processes, challenge traditional practices, and bring fresh ideas to the table.

  • Planning & Organization: You are meticulous in your planning, ensuring all moving parts are aligned and that nothing falls through the cracks.

title: Install Qualification Operations Specialist (contract)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Install Qualification Operation Specialist is responsible for driving key milestones enabling tool installation, readiness, and qualification within Intel Foundry Construction and Sourcing (FCS). The role is responsible for equipment install execution from pre-design through design finish and set to SL2 signoff, ensuring safe delivery, accurate scope definition, efficient construction, and prompt vendor qualification.

This position requires five days per week of onsite presence and close coordination with manufacturing, design, construction, OEMs, trade contractors, and supplier partners.


Please consider that this is an Intel contract position (3 years).

Responsibilities will include but are not limited to:


Safety and Compliance:

  • Champion Intel's Culture of Caring and ensure safe behaviors across design and construction activities.
  • Enforce cleanroom, IP protection, and site protocols to maintain compliance with all applicable regulations and agency audits.

Install and Qualification Execution:

  • Own key tool installs milestones including set, rigging, placement, hook up, energization, and qual.
  • Support troubleshooting for Supplier Qual and Intel Qual to quickly resolve issues.
  • Drive micro schedule and pull plan development to support tool install milestones.
  • Manage decoupled construction paths SET/SL2 to accelerate readiness.
  • Coordinate testing and facility readiness (LSS, eFIT, TAB, networking, ESOPN).

Design and Scope Alignment:

  • Load complete tool install scope in DAC prior to design engagement.
  • Participate in cross functional design reviews with CIT, TICE, Layout, OEMs, and module teams.
  • Validate OEM data and ensure alignment with Intel standards (SEED/EDS/UDS).
  • Support LSP creation, routing validation, POC assignments, and space management.
  • Reduce changes by minimizing DCNs, DCRs, and late-stage modifications.

Execution Planning and Stakeholder Coordination:

  • Lead multi supplier coordination meetings and execution planning sessions.
  • Translate technical/business requirements into actionable plans and schedules.
  • Forecast equipment and resource needs.
  • Ensure readiness and prompt delivery of tools, prefac kits, globals, and parts.
  • Coordinate equipment decon and demo activities.

Supplier and Vendor Management:

  • Manage OEMs and third-party vendors to achieve best-in-class qual durations.
  • Drive early vendor enablement and facility readiness using ESOPN. (Equipment sign- off
  • per need).
  • Ensure clean handoff from construction completion to vendor qual finish.
  • Manage contracts, KPIs, and supplier scorecards in partnership with Procurement.

Operations and Continuous Improvement:

  • Oversee contractor and supplier activities in accordance with SLAs.
  • Monitor site operational budget and maximize efficiency.
  • Apply Lean principles to eliminate waste, reduce install durations, and improve quality.
  • Document and share lessons learned across modules and sites.
  • Influence tools install methods through innovation and best-known methods (BKMs).

In addition to the qualifications a successful candidate will demonstrate:

  • Project management skills (planning, scheduling, risk mitigation).
  • Adaptability in fast-paced, changing environments.
  • Organizational discipline and time management.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications, you must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position.

The candidate must have at least one of the following:

  • Bachelor's degree in engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, Business, or related field with 3+ years of experience in Project Management, as Equipment/Engineering Tool Owner, or equivalent installation/qualification/demo/maintenance technician experience.

OR

  • Associate’s degree related to semiconductor manufacturing and 5+ years of experience in Project Management, as Equipment/Engineering Tool Owner, or equivalent installation/qualification/demo/maintenance technician experience.

 OR

  • 7+ years of experience in Project Management, as Equipment/Engineering Tool Owner, or equivalent installation/qualification/demo/maintenance technician experience will be considered in lieu of a degree.

• Willing to working onsite in a cleanroom/construction environment.

 This position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship.



Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.


  • Experience in navigating construction areas when needed.
  • PMP certification.
  • Experience with medium or large-scale construction or tool install programs.
  • Knowledge of Intel systems: EMS, SIRFIS, Fuzion, QUEST, IMCS, Capacity Planning, SLS, 6D.
  • Demo experience (6D trained and certified).
  • Experience with station controller setup / automation.
  • Panel shutdowns, FPOCs, eFITs.
  • Tool crating/de crating, AIO.
  • Tool install/qual specifications and maintenance.
  • Managing daily third-party supplier operation.

title: Defect Metrology Tool Install Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Join Intel Foundry Construction and Sourcing (FCS), a team dedicated to building and optimizing world-class semiconductor manufacturing facilities. FCS drives the construction, equipment installation, and startup of advanced factories that enable Intel's technology roadmap. As part of this team, you will contribute to the deployment of cutting-edge manufacturing equipment that powers the future of semiconductor innovation.

As a Defect Metrology Tool Install Engineer, you will be responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing installation projects for advanced inspection and metrology equipment used to support process control, yield improvement, and manufacturing excellence. You will work closely with engineering, construction, manufacturing, and supplier partners to deliver successful tool installation projects supporting Intel's leading-edge factories.

This is an onsite position located in Hillsboro, Oregon.

What You'll Do

Core Responsibilities

  • Coordinate and execute semiconductor tool installation activities supporting factory construction and manufacturing ramp milestones.
  • Collaborate with factory owners, suppliers, contractors, and engineering teams to ensure equipment, materials, and resources are available to support project schedules.
  • Lead planning and coordination activities across multiple stakeholders to support successful tool installation execution.
  • Monitor equipment readiness, procurement status, funding approvals, and project milestones.
  • Develop and maintain installation plans, schedules, and risk mitigation strategies.
  • Act as the primary Intel equipment owner from planning through installation and turnover.
  • Resolve project constraints, escalate risks, and drive issue resolution to maintain schedule commitments.
  • Ensure all work is performed in accordance with Intel safety, quality, and operational standards.

Defect Metrology-Specific Responsibilities

  • Support installation, relocation, startup, and qualification activities for defect inspection and metrology equipment.
  • Partner with yield engineering, process engineering, manufacturing, and supplier teams to support equipment deployment and operational readiness.
  • Coordinate readiness activities required for metrology equipment installation and turnover.
  • Drive issue resolution related to equipment integration, facilities interfaces, startup activities, and installation challenges.
  • Support deployment of advanced metrology and inspection technologies that enable process control and yield improvement.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders to ensure successful qualification of equipment supporting manufacturing operations.

The Successful Candidate Will Demonstrate:

  • Strong project planning, coordination, and execution skills with a focus on delivering results.
  • Effective communication and collaboration skills across technical and business teams.
  • Ability to make sound decisions, solve problems, and drive timely resolution of issues.
  • Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills in a highly matrixed environment.
  • Ownership, accountability, and attention to detail.
  • Commitment to safety, quality, and operational excellence.
  • Continuous improvement mindset with the ability to identify and implement process improvements.
  • Adaptability and resilience in a fast-paced semiconductor manufacturing environment.

Intel invests in our people and offers a complete and competitive package of benefits employees and their families through every stage of life.

title: Install Qualification Operations Sr Specialist (Contract)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

oin Intel Foundry Construction and Sourcing (FCS) in building the world's largest semiconductor manufacturing factories across the globe. The future is what we build.

The scope of our work includes but is not limited to Advanced Packaging Factories, New Wafer Fabrication factories (Fabs), Fab Conversions, Process Tools Install, Infrastructure, and Progressive Build. We are looking for world-class technical talent to join our team. If you enjoy working with the latest technology in a rewarding, fast-paced environment, this is the right place for you.

Everywhere you go, you'll find an opportunity to make a difference. In any given workday, you will be given the responsibility to innovate and create an impact on our business.

The Install Qualification Operation Sr Specialist is responsible for driving key milestones enabling tool installation, readiness, and qualification within Intel Foundry Construction and Sourcing (FCS). The role is responsible for equipment install execution from pre-design through design finish and set to SL2 signoff, ensuring safe delivery, accurate scope definition, efficient construction, and prompt vendor qualification.

This position requires five days per week of onsite presence and close coordination with manufacturing, design, construction, OEMs, trade contractors, and supplier partners.

Please consider that this is an Intel Contract position (3 years).

Responsibilities will include but are not limited to:


Safety and Compliance:

  • Champion Intel's Culture of Caring and ensure safe behaviors across design and construction activities.
  • Enforce cleanroom, IP protection, and site protocols to maintain compliance with all applicable regulations and agency audits.

Install and Qualification Execution:

  • Own key tool installs milestones including set, rigging, placement, hook up, energization, and qual.
  • Support troubleshooting for Supplier Qual and Intel Qual to quickly resolve issues.
  • Drive micro schedule and pull plan development to support tool install milestones.
  • Manage decoupled construction paths SET/SL2 to accelerate readiness.
  • Coordinate testing and facility readiness (LSS, eFIT, TAB, networking, ESOPN).

Design and Scope Alignment:

  • Load complete tool install scope in DAC prior to design engagement.
  • Participate in cross functional design reviews with CIT, TICE, Layout, OEMs, and module teams.
  • Validate OEM data and ensure alignment with Intel standards (SEED/EDS/UDS).
  • Support LSP creation, routing validation, POC assignments, and space management.
  • Reduce changes by minimizing DCNs, DCRs, and late-stage modifications.

Execution Planning and Stakeholder Coordination:

  • Lead multi supplier coordination meetings and execution planning sessions.
  • Translate technical/business requirements into actionable plans and schedules.
  • Forecast equipment and resource needs.
  • Ensure readiness and prompt delivery of tools, prefac kits, globals, and parts.
  • Coordinate equipment decon and demo activities.

Supplier and Vendor Management:


  • Manage OEMs and third-party vendors to achieve best-in-class qual durations.
  • Drive early vendor enablement and facility readiness using ESOPN. (Equipment sign- off per need).

  • Manage contracts, KPIs, and supplier scorecards in partnership with Procurement.

Operations and Continuous Improvement:


  • Oversee contractor and supplier activities in accordance with SLAs.
  • Monitor site operational budget and maximize efficiency.
  • Apply Lean principles to eliminate waste, reduce install durations, and improve quality.
  • Document and share lessons learned across modules and sites.

In addition to the qualifications a successful candidate will demonstrate:


  • Project management skills (planning, scheduling, risk mitigation).

  • Organizational discipline and time management.

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, Business, or related field with 5+ years of experience in Project Management, as Equipment/Engineering Tool Owner, or equivalent installation/qualification/demo/maintenance technician experience.

title: Module Development Engineer - LTD Dry Etch
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Business Group
Intel Foundry Technology Development is committed to delivering world-class manufacturing solutions that power Intel's product roadmap. The team leads advancements in semiconductor process engineering, enabling innovative device architectures and high-volume production. Joining this team means contributing to Intel's pursuit of excellence and maintaining its leadership in a dynamic, competitive market.

About the Role

Join Intel Logic Technology Development and help advance the next generation of patterning.

You will operate in a high impact space, partnering closely with cross functional teams (Process Integration, Manufacturing, Equipment Engineering, Yield/Defect Engineering, and suppliers) to solve complex technical challenges and establish long term systems that sustain performance. This role requires regular onsite presence to fulfill essential job responsibilities.

  • Drive technology development for future technology and high-volume manufacturing, provide process integration and equipment solutions, and perform feasibility studies to meet desired device specifications.

  • Own and drive development of the next generation patterning processes, including process architecture, optimization strategies, and qualification methodologies.

  • Perform pathfinding activities in support of process and hardware development on existing and first of kind equipment, enabling manufacturing of innovative device architectures and developing roadmaps for technologies enabling future roadmap.

  • Provide technical leadership for cross functional problem solving to resolve complex process and defect issues; drive structured root cause, containment, and permanent corrective actions.

  • Design and execute comprehensive characterization plans; plan and conduct experiments (DOE/response surface/robustness studies) across the development cycle.

  • Establish and mature control systems to optimize and sustain production performance (SPC, control plans, alarms, response plans, recipe governance, sustaining systems).

  • Develop strategies and infrastructure to resolve difficult problems and implement systems to manage these problems in the future (standard work, monitoring, dashboards/analytics, knowledge capture).

  • Drive improvements in yield, reliability, cost, productivity, and process capability, ensuring scalable transfer to manufacturing and ongoing sustainment.

  • Influence technical direction, mentor engineers (as appropriate for grade), and communicate status/risks clearly to stakeholders.

  • Recommend and implement modifications for operating equipment to improve production efficiency, manufacturing techniques, and optimizing production output for existing products.

  • Partner with key equipment and material suppliers to develop and implement enabling elements of the technology. Perform process technology feasibility studies through theoretical simulations and/or practical engineering methods.

Core Competencies

  • Strong collaboration and problem-solving skills to work effectively in cross-disciplinary teams.

  • Ability to communicate technical data and concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Qualifications:

The Minimum qualifications listed below are required to be initially considered for this position.  Minimum qualifications listed below would be obtained through a combination of industry relevant job experience, internship experience, academic projects, and / or schoolwork/classes/research. The preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • PhD in Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, Electrical Engineering, or a semiconductor related STEM field with relevant industry or graduate school research experience.
    -Or-

  • Master's degree in Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, Electrical Engineering, or a semiconductor related STEM field with 2 years of relevant industry or graduate school research experience.
    -Or-

  • Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, Electrical Engineering, or a semiconductor related STEM field with 4+ years of industry experience at a leading foundry or dry etch equipment supplier.

  • Hands-on experience in dry etch semiconductor manufacturing, including ownership of process development and optimization.

  • Experience with plasma etch fundamentals, including plasma generation, plasma-surface interactions, selectivity, profile control, and defect mechanisms.

  • Experience delivering dry etch process solutions that improved yield, reliability, performance, or manufacturability.

  • Expertise in statistical analysis and DOE methodologies, using tools such as JMP, Python, or MATLAB to drive data-based decisions.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of direct industry experience developing and deploying dry etch processes for advanced logic, foundry technologies or dry etch equipment suppliers.

  • Experience with advanced dry etch technologies such as: ICP / CCP plasma etch, High aspect ratio etch (HARC), Atomic Layer Etch (ALE), Radical and Vapor phase isotropic etching, Ash and surface treatments, EUV patterned layer etch integration.

  • Experience in managing complex process challenges and provide solutions such as pattern fidelity, CD control, defectivity, variability reduction, or process window expansion.

  • Experience with materials and device characterization techniques, including SEM, TEM, CD SEM, AFM, XPS, or electrical correlation.

  • Expertise in APC development and variability reduction in a manufacturing environment.

  • Expertise in etch driven defect reduction and metrology in a manufacturing environment.

  • Proven ability to lead technical problem solving across projects, influencing peers and stakeholders without formal people management responsibility.


Join Intel's passionate and innovative team to help define the future of semiconductor technology. Your expertise and dedication will contribute to groundbreaking advancements in manufacturing processes and device development, making a meaningful impact on Intel's technology roadmap.

title: Facilities Electrician
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

As a Facilities Electrician, you will play an essential role in ensuring the functionality, safety, and reliability of electrical systems across Intel's facilities. You will be responsible for assembling, maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing electrical equipment, wiring, and systems that are critical to daily operations. Your expertise will help maintain the seamless flow of operations, minimize downtime, and ensure compliance with performance standards, making a tangible impact on Intel's operational success.

Business group Intel Corporation's Facilities Operations team enables the smooth functioning of Intel's cutting-edge facilities. The group is dedicated to maintaining the infrastructure that supports Intel's leadership in technology innovation, ensuring operational excellence and environmental compliance. By providing essential services and technical expertise, the Facilities Operations team drives efficiency and reliability, fueling Intel's broader organizational goals.

The primary responsibilities for this role will include, but are not limited to:

  • Assemble, test, and maintain electrical or electronic wiring, equipment, appliances, and apparatus.
  • Troubleshoot and repair malfunctioning equipment and systems using appropriate spare parts and servicing techniques.
  • Inspect electrical systems regularly to identify faults or hazards and ensure adherence to safety protocols.
  • Operate and maintain medium voltage electrical systems while implementing reliability improvements.
  • Review wiring blueprints and interpret technical drawings for system layout and diagnostics.
  • Run tests on generators, backup systems, and other electrical components, ensuring upgrades and repairs are performed as needed.
  • Install and preserve the functionality of wires, plugs, panel boards, switchgear, and related equipment.
  • Document and escalate issues to management while providing reliability suggestions and commissioning new electrical facilities equipment.
  • Operate and maintain environmentally compliant equipment to support sustainability efforts.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position.

  • Bachelor's degree in a relevant field with 0-4 years of hands-on experience in electrical systems maintenance and troubleshooting OR an Associate's degree in a relevant field with 3-6 years of hands-on experience OR 8-10 years of relevant experience with a High School diploma.
  • Journeyman Electrician must have an active Oregon journeyman license or Oregon reciprocal agreement journeyman license from the states of Arkansas, Idaho, Maine, Montana, Utah, Wyoming.
  • Intermediate knowledge in operating medium voltage electrical systems.
  • Intermediate experience to assemble, maintain, and troubleshoot electrical wiring, appliances, and equipment.
  • Intermediate knowledge of electrical safety codes and regulations.
  • Intermediate experience with testing tools such as voltmeters and ohmmeters.

Preferred Qualifications:

Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

  • Strong diagnostic and problem-solving skills to identify and resolve electrical system issues effectively.

title: Senior Core Design Verification Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
As a CPU Design Verification Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring the functionality and reliability of cutting-edge CPU designs. Your day-to-day responsibilities will include developing and executing verification plans to thoroughly test CPU microarchitectures, identifying and resolving design bugs, and collaborating with cross-functional teams to ensure performance, power, and efficiency goals are met. Your efforts will directly contribute to the delivery of innovative and high-quality products, reinforcing Intel's position as a leader in the semiconductor industry.


Business Group
The Silicon and Platform Engineering Group (SPE) leads the development of silicon and platform solutions that drive Intel's technological advancements. This team focuses on designing, verifying, and delivering high-performance CPUs and platforms to meet evolving market demands. By joining this group, you will be part of a collaborative and dynamic environment that supports Intel's mission to create world-changing innovations.


Key Responsibilities


  • Perform functional verification of CPU logic to ensure designs meet specification requirements.
  • Develop and execute IP verification plans, test benches, and environments to ensure comprehensive coverage of CPU microarchitecture specifications.
  • Define and run system simulation models to verify design functionality, analyze power and timing, and uncover bugs.
  • Debug issues in the presilicon environment, replicate failures, and implement corrective measures.
  • Collaborate with CPU architects, RTL developers, and physical design teams to optimize the verification process and achieve functional, performance, and power targets.
  • Document verification plans and lead technical reviews with design and architecture teams.
  • Maintain and enhance existing verification infrastructure and methodologies.
  • Actively contribute to the definition of CPU architecture and microarchitecture features.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.
  • At least 4 years of experience in ASIC or FPGA design verification, preferably with CPU or E-Core designs.

Life at Intel


The Role and Impact
As a SoC Power Thermal Performance Validation and Optimization Engineer, you will play an essential role in ensuring Intel's products achieve optimal power, thermal, and performance benchmarks at the system-on-chip (SoC) level. In this position, you will develop and execute validation methodologies, optimize hardware/software solutions, and perform SoC-level debugging to address power, thermal, and performance challenges. Your contribution will directly impact Intel's ability to deliver competitive, high-performing products to market.

Business Group
This role is part of Intel's Data Center Group (DCG), which focuses on designing innovative solutions to power the next generation of computing platforms for data centers. As a member of the PTP PreSi Correlation Solution team, you will contribute to shaping the development and validation processes for cutting-edge technologies, ensuring Intel meets and exceeds industry standards for performance and efficiency.

Key Responsibilities:

title: AI Software Development Engineer - Neuromorphic Computing
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

What if you could help define how developers program an entirely new class of AI hardware?

For nearly a decade, Intel's Neuromorphic Computing Lab, together with a global ecosystem of more than 250 research groups, has advanced architectures, algorithms, and software inspired by the brain's remarkable efficiency, scalability, and adaptability. Our Loihi research chips pioneered event-driven, sparse, and massively parallel neuro-inspired computing, contributing to more than 100 peer-reviewed publications and establishing the potential of this new approach.

Now we are taking the next step: transforming those breakthroughs into technologies for physical AI systems, such as robots and intelligent edge devices that must sense, decide, and act under tight latency and power constraints. This is an opportunity to join at a formative stage and help create the kernels, programming abstractions, and performance models for a new hardware architecture built around sparse, event-driven, and massively parallel computation. Your work will directly influence both the hardware and how developers use it. You will also help shape a software stack designed for an era in which engineers and AI agents build and optimize applications together.

Position Overview

As an AI Software Engineer in Neuromorphic Computing, you will turn new neuromorphic hardware capabilities into working, high-performance AI software and contribute to critical technical areas from design through delivery. You will build specialized kernels for current and next-generation neuromorphic hardware, explore optimization strategies that conventional processors cannot offer, and help shape the programming abstractions that expose those capabilities to developers.

Working alongside hardware architects, compiler engineers, and AI researchers, you will use performance and power models to influence design decisions before silicon is available and then validate those decisions using simulators, emulators, and hardware. Your work will span the full hardware-software lifecycle, from modeling a hardware feature to implementing the kernel that unlocks it and demonstrating measurable gains on real AI workloads. You will contribute to the training, porting, and optimization of end-to-end applications for Loihi-based systems while helping improve engineering quality across the team.

As part of Intel's CTO Office, you will join a vertically integrated incubation effort dedicated to bringing Intel's neuromorphic technology innovations to market. Our diverse team of engineers and researchers has pioneered sparse, event-based neuromorphic architectures across multiple generations and is now focused on commercializing the technology in future Intel and partner products.

The primary responsibilities for this role will include, but are not limited to:

  • Design and implement specialized AI kernels for neuromorphic hardware using custom DSLs and accelerator programming models such as CUDA and SYCL and help shape the programming abstractions for Intel's next-generation neuromorphic architecture.
  • Develop and optimize operations for convolutional networks, transformers, and generative AI workloads by applying techniques such as tiling, fusion, vectorization, parallelization, layout transformation, buffering, sparsity, and quantization.
  • Develop performance methodologies and improve kernel behavior in areas such as compute utilization, latency, throughput, memory bandwidth, data movement, synchronization, and scaling, turning architectural insights into measurable workload gains.
  • Build reference models, numerical validation tools, benchmarks, and analytical or simulation-based performance, power, and area models that guide hardware-software co-design; reconcile discrepancies across models, simulators, emulators, and hardware.
  • Collaborate with hardware, compiler, runtime, and application engineers to deliver maintainable code, tests, documentation, benchmarks, and performance-regression infrastructure.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position.

  • A PhD with no prior professional experience, a master's degree with 2+ years of relevant experience, or a bachelor's degree with 4+ years of relevant experience in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Physics, or a related technical field.
  • 4+ years of experience developing, debugging, and delivering maintainable software in Python and either C or C++, including performance-critical or systems-level code.
  • 2+ years of experience implementing and optimizing numerical, machine-learning, or high-performance computing kernels using parallel programming and either an accelerator programming model, such as CUDA, SYCL, or OpenCL, or a domain-specific language, such as Triton.
  • 2+ years of experience developing, training, or evaluating AI algorithms and machine-learning models using a framework such as PyTorch, JAX, or TensorFlow.
  • 2+ years of experience establishing numerical correctness and measuring performance using reference implementations, automated testing, benchmarking, profiling, or performance-regression infrastructure.

Preferred Qualifications:

Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

  • Experience developing or optimizing workloads based on convolutional networks, transformers, generative AI, or other models relevant to edge and physical AI systems.
  • Experience with compiler technologies or domain-specific language development, such as MLIR, LLVM, TVM, Triton, or related toolchains.
  • Experience with hardware performance modeling, architecture simulators, performance, power, and area (PPA) analysis, or hardware-software co-design.
  • Advanced experience with optimization techniques including kernel fusion, tiling, vectorization, quantization, sparsity, layout optimization, or double buffering.
  • Experience developing software for spatial, dataflow, neuromorphic, or other emerging AI accelerator architectures.
  • Experience contributing to collaborative or open-source software projects using code review, continuous integration, documentation, and testing practices.

We are excited to welcome passionate and driven individuals who want to shape the future of AI technology. Your expertise will be invaluable in driving Intel's success and delivering transformative solutions to the world.

descriptionHtml:

  • Drive resolution of supply chain process gaps, planning system limitations, and cross-functional execution challenges.

title: Quality and Reliability Engineer (Advance Packaging & Assembly)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact:
We are seeking a Manufacturing Quality and Reliability Engineer to join the Foundry QnR team at our Penang site, supporting Intel's advanced packaging programs (EMIB, Foveros).


This role spans silicon processing and wafer-level assembly (WLA) flows, and key interfaces with packaging substrates and 2.5D EMIB technology. You will help ensure that products and processes meet rigorous quality and reliability standards from wafer fabrication through packaging and assembly. The position directly influences manufacturing performance, yield, reliability, and customer satisfaction by driving robust quality control, disciplined excursion management, and continuous process improvement. You will also have the opportunity to represent Quality and Reliability in development forums, Silicon and Advanced Packaging factory operations, and Substrate suppliers.


Key Responsibilities

  • Apply Advanced Packaging expertise to assess inline process health, excursion impact, yield risk, defect mechanisms, and downstream packaging implications.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to drive effective root cause analysis, systemic corrective and prevention actions using 8D and related problem-solving methodologies.
  • Partner with fab manufacturing, substrates assembly, test, process engineering, and quality teams to strengthen early excursion detection, process controls, in-line screens, and outgoing quality.
  • Drive quality control improvements devising incoming/ outgoing quality controls, using statistical process control, defect pareto analysis, control plans, audit learnings, and excursion prevention indicators across fab, substrate manufacturing, and assembly manufacturing steps.
  • Support manufacturing excursion management, including MRB facilitation, containment strategies, rapid product risk assessment, discrepant material disposition decisions, and clear communication with Foundry partners and Intel customers.
  • Provide technical input on thermomechanical interactions between wafer, die, and package to support risk assessment and technical decision-making.
  • Own and continuously improve material disposition RFCs, Rel monitors (QTM, ORM), and Quality and Reliability best known methods.
  • Support technology certification and transfer activities in collaboration with technology development and ramp partners.
  • Use data extraction and statistical analysis tools, and custom scripting to flag product, process, or customer risks.
  • Represent the Quality and Reliability function as the voice of the customer in internal forums, providing recommendations to improve system, process, product quality, and reliability outcomes.

Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor or Master's degree in Materials Science, Physics, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field with relevant experience in semiconductor manufacturing (wafer-level assembly WLA, Die prep, packaging Substrates).
  • at least 3 years of relevant work experience in semiconductor manufacturing (wafer-level assembly WLA, Die prep, packaging Substrates) with a bachelor's degree.
  • Experience in quality and reliability methodologies, excursion management, and failure mode analysis.
  • Proficiency in statistics and data analytics tools for quality and reliability assessments.
  • Familiar with QnR Quality Systems and tools.
  • Effective verbal and written communication, and effective meetings skills.
  • Motivated self-starter and self-driven learner to develop skills in various semiconductor and assembly processes.
  • Demonstrate strong Quality and Zero-defect mindset, and Intel values of Velocity, Efficiency, and Customer 1st.
  • Be comfortable working in a diverse environment and across geographies.
  • Travel might be required.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Influencing skills to drive a quality-focused mindset across the organization.
  • Proven ability to manage impactful quality events

Join us to help shape the future of manufacturing quality and reliability at Intel. In this role, you will make a lasting impact on product quality, process robustness, and customer experience while advancing next-generation semiconductor manufacturing technologies.

title: Senior Lithography and Photomask Process Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Key Responsibilities:


• Photomask and Reticle Operations: Oversee photomask incoming quality control, pellicle integrity, reticle qualification protocols, and reticle lifecycle management across advanced EUV and DUV toolsets.

• Advanced Pellicle Development: Drive next gen EUV pellicle development, material optimization for enhanced transmission, stability, defect mitigation and overall yield improvement. Optimize reticle usage, inspection and disposition strategies over life cycle.

• Cross-Functional Process Integration: Partner closely with Scanner/Litho teams, Reticle Design, Thin Films, Etch, and Yield Enhancement engineering teams to diagnose patterning excursions and accelerate technology transitions.

• Yield Ramp and Excursion Containment: Lead root cause failure analysis (RCFA) for yield-limiting lithography and reticle-related defects during new process node development and high-volume manufacturing (HVM).

• Technical Mentorship and Industry Engagement: Provide technical leadership to junior and mid-level process engineers, establish standard operating procedures (SOPs), and collaborate directly with leading lithography and mask equipment suppliers.

Qualifications:

Education: M.S. with 8+ years of foundry experience or Ph.D. of Foundry experience in Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, Optics, Microelectronics, or a related semiconductor engineering discipline.


• Experience: 8+ years of hands-on process engineering experience in advanced semiconductor lithography and photomask/reticle technologies within high-volume manufacturing (HVM) or advanced technology development fabs.


• Photomask and Reticle Expertise: In-depth knowledge of mask fabrication, mask metrology, aerial image modeling, pellicle technology, reticle degradation mechanisms, and mask defect inspection platforms.


• Lithography Toolset and Process Knowledge: Proven proficiency across DUV (ArFi / 193nm immersion) and EUV exposure systems (ASML Twinscan / NXE platforms), track integration, and advanced CD metrology.


• Analytical and Statistical Mastery: Advanced proficiency with Statistical Process Control (SPC), Design of Experiments (DOE), yield analytics platforms, JMP, Python, or MATLAB for complex data modeling and multivariate analysis.


• Leadership and Communication: Track record of driving cross-functional taskforces, writing comprehensive technical documentation, and delivering executive briefings on process yield, tool performance, and quality enhancements.


We invite you to bring your technical expertise and innovative vision to Intel Foundry, where your work will drive the next generation of semiconductor technology. Join us to make an impact and advance your career in a dynamic, collaborative environment.

About the Team

Logic Technology Development (LTD) develops and delivers Intel's leading-edge silicon process technologies for both Intel products and Intel Foundry customers. LTD is responsible for creating process technologies that meet targets for performance, power, area, yield, reliability, cost, and schedule while ensuring they can be successfully transferred into high-volume manufacturing.

This position is in the Logic Technology Development (LTD) team working in one of the most advanced semiconductor cleanroom facilities in the world. You will be designing, executing, and analyzing experiments necessary to meet engineering specifications for their process.

The Advanced Device Development Engineering Manager is responsible for leading scientific research device group enabling the manufacture of innovative device architectures

Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead a team of device engineers to develop a high-volume capable process technology that meets performance, yield, and reliability requirements for both internal and foundry products. This includes both physical and electrical data analysis, as well as extensive interaction with other technology development teams (integration, module, design/modeling and reliability)
  • Set priorities of a team embedded in programs targeted for foundry offerings to get results across boundaries, ensure an inclusive work environment, develop employee careers and manage team performance.
  • Work closely with LTD core program integration and device organization to ensure the high-quality Process-Design Kit (PDK) is delivered to design enablement team. It includes extensive Silicon-to-Simulation (or model-hardware correlation) analysis/target projection, layout effect validation and electrical monitors to product parametric correlation.
  • Collaborate closely with LTD foundry technology engineering group to ensure the customer achieves leadership product performance and derives maximum value from Intel's advanced manufacturing technologies.
  • Define robust test structures and test programs to validate advanced design rules and reliably extract key device parameters.
  • Use Statistics, Data Mining, and other data analysis techniques to collect, explore, and extract insights from Electrical-test, yield, and fab data to define future development direction.

Required Skills and Experience

    • Semiconductor materials
    • Fabrication

Preferred Skills and Experience

  • Advanced Transistor Device Structures and Device Physics.
  • Process monitoring Test structures design and layout experience.

  • Statistical Process Control (SPC) or Design of Experiments (DOE) principles and engineering analysis tools.

  • Expertise in agentic AI and orchestrated LLM workflows, machine learning, deep learning, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), knowledge engineering, and dataflow pipeline architectures.

title: E-core CPU Physical Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

We created the Intel Atom Processor (E-Core), a disruptive technology that enables a broad range of devices including entry PC's, smartphones, modems, 2 in 1 laptops, micro-servers, and other Internet-of-Things IoT devices. You will be part of a team, participating in the design of a future generation high performance Intel Atom microprocessor. This role requires a engineer with strong analytic and problem solving skill, an ability to communicate well, and willing to share and discuss issues. You will work on implementation of CPU Core blocks from synthesis through post-layout verification and tapeout. You will develop the custom constraints for driving synthesis and Auto-Place and Route APR tools to implement and optimize the design to meet aggressive timing and power goals. You will work closely with micro-architecture, RTL, and custom circuit teams to converge the design to project targets.


The responsibilities will be tailored to the candidate's skills and expertise and will include several of the following, but not be limited to

  • Logic synthesis and place and route for CORE IP blocks.
  • Performing floor-planning and routing studies and implementation
    Block/sub-system level timing analysis.
  • Work on low power techniques and power reduction in sub-system.
  • Physical verification closure of block/sub-system.
  • Scripts writing for data analysis and recipe creation.
  • Strong analytical ability, problem solving and communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently and at various levels of abstraction.
  • Strong communication and team work skills.
  • Capable of working in a high performing team to deliver the results required from the organization.
  • Ability to work well in at team and be productive under aggressive schedules.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Must have either BS or MS in Electrical Engineering or Computer Engineering.

Minimum 5 year of experience in:

  • CPU physical design and timing verification.
  • Synthesis/APR flows on multi voltage high frequency designs including custom polygon editing.
  • Tcl scripting.
  • Noise, cross-talk, OCV analysis.
  • Floorplanning and physical design and timing closure.
  • Formal equivalence, DRC/LVS, IR and electro-migration checks.

Preferred qualifications:

  • 6+ years of experience with the above skill sets.
  • Experience with Fusion Compiler, DCT, DCE, ICC2, RedHawk, ICV, Conformal, Calibre, PrimeTime, StarRCXT.
  • Cadence Tools Experience Not a Must But Preferred.

The Role and Impact
As a Semiconductor Manufacturing Engineer, you will play a vital role in supporting and enhancing manufacturing operations for Intel's cutting-edge fabrication facilities. You will analyze, optimize, and sustain manufacturing processes, ensuring operational excellence and efficiency. Through your contributions to process improvements, equipment performance, and data-driven decision-making, you will directly impact product quality and factory performance, supporting Intel's leadership in semiconductor innovation.

Business group
Intel Corporation is a global leader in semiconductor manufacturing, developing advanced technologies that power progress across industries. The PGAT MFG MSE group focuses on delivering operational solutions for technology development and high-volume fabrication facilities, ensuring seamless product introduction, optimized processes, and sustained manufacturing excellence. This team's efforts are foundational to Intel's ability to meet customer demands, drive innovation, and maintain its competitive edge.

Key Responsibilities

  • Analyze and sustain manufacturing processes to identify areas for improvement and drive corrective actions for process deviations.
  • Provide technical support for new product introduction (NPI) builds and optimize manufacturing workflows throughout the product lifecycle.
  • Monitor the performance of machinery, equipment, and tools to ensure their efficiency and troubleshoot issues as needed.

title: Advanced Packaging Module Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel Corporation is one of the world's leading semiconductor companies, driving innovation that shapes the future of computing, connectivity, and human progress. With decades of pioneering research and development, Intel is at the forefront of designing and manufacturing the world's most advanced chips and technologies. Our Oregon campus in Hillsboro is one of Intel's largest and most strategically important sites globally, serving as a hub for cutting-edge semiconductor research, development, and high-volume manufacturing. At Intel, we believe in the power of human ingenuity and are committed to creating an inclusive, collaborative environment where brilliant minds come together to solve the world's most complex technological challenges.

We are seeking a highly motivated and technically skilled Process Integration Engineer to join our dynamic team in Hillsboro, Oregon. In this critical role, you will be at the intersection of innovation and manufacturing, driving technology development and enablement for both high-volume manufacturing and next-generation semiconductor technologies. You will lead the design and development of sophisticated manufacturing processes, perform pathfinding activities for future device architectures, and collaborate with world-class suppliers and internal teams to push the boundaries of what's possible in semiconductor technology. This is a unique opportunity to make a meaningful impact on Intel's strategic roadmap and the broader semiconductor industry.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Technology Development & Enablement: Drive technology development for high-volume manufacturing and future technology nodes, providing process integration and equipment solutions to meet desired device specifications.
  • Process Design & Development: Lead the design and development of technically sophisticated manufacturing processes, including material selection, parameter optimization, equipment metrology, and system design to enable new product designs and functional requirements.
  • Pathfinding & Roadmap Development: Perform pathfinding activities in support of process and hardware development, enabling the manufacturing of innovative device architectures, and develop technology roadmaps for future product generations.
  • Manufacturing Optimization: Recommend and implement modifications to operating equipment to improve production efficiency, refine manufacturing techniques, and optimize production output for existing products.
  • Supplier Collaboration: Partner with key equipment and materials suppliers to develop and implement enabling elements of technology, building cost-sensitive roadmaps in collaboration with the vendor ecosystem.
  • Feasibility Studies: Perform process technology feasibility studies through theoretical simulations and practical engineering methods to validate new approaches and technologies.
  • Industry Awareness: Remain current on relevant industrial process and material manufacturing technical trends, developing a forward-looking view of Intel's future process technology needs to push the industry forward.
  • Statistical Analysis & Experimentation: Apply Statistical Process Control (SPC) and Design of Experiments (DOE) principles to drive data-informed decisions and process improvements.
  • Automation & Systems Development: Leverage hands-on experience with robotics, automation systems, vision systems, and image processing to advance manufacturing capabilities.

As a Successful Candidate, You Will Bring:

  • A Natural Problem-Solver: You thrive when faced with complex challenges and approach them with creativity, curiosity, and a structured mindset.
  • Adaptable & Resilient: You embrace change and ambiguity, pivoting quickly when priorities shift without losing momentum or focus.
  • A Collaborative Team Player: You build strong relationships across teams, functions, and supplier ecosystems, knowing that the best outcomes come from working together.
  • An Effective Communicator: You can translate complex technical concepts into clear, actionable insights for diverse audiences, from engineers to leadership.
  • Self-Motivated & Driven: You take ownership of your work, proactively seek out opportunities to improve processes, and are passionate about making a meaningful impact.
  • Detail-Oriented: You bring precision and rigor to everything you do, understanding that in semiconductor manufacturing, the smallest details can make the biggest difference.
  • Innovative & Forward-Thinking: You are passionate about staying ahead of industry trends and are energized by the opportunity to shape the future of semiconductor technology.

Are you ready to be part of a team that is literally building the future? At Intel's Hillsboro, Oregon campus, you'll have the resources, the talent, and the mission to do work that truly matters — not just for Intel, but for the world.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.


Minimum Qualifications:

  • Master's degree in Materials Science and Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Chemistry, or a related field with 4+ years of relevant industry experience; or a PhD degree in the same fields with 3+ years of relevant experience.
  • Relevant experience will be any of the following:
    • Technical expertise in semiconductor processing, system controls, opto-mechanics, or mechanical systems.
    • Hands-on experience with robotics, automation systems, vision systems, or image processing.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of experience in:
    • Statistical Process Control (SPC) and Design of Experiments (DOE) principles.
    • Programming experience in Python or MATLAB.
    • Troubleshoot complex manufacturing processes and equipment.
    • Packaging processes, equipment automation development, or project management.

The Role and Impact
As a Sr Deep Learning Hardware Verification Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the future of AI hardware by validating and optimizing next-generation NPU silicon solutions. In this role you will join the NPU Hardware Pre-Silicon Validation team working closely with design engineers, model engineers and AI architects to validate components of the next generation NPU IP portfolio, your contributions will directly shape Intel's advancements in AI technologies.

Business group

With a focus on building state-of-the-art hardware that supports cutting-edge AI models, the team collaborates across Intel to enable breakthroughs in efficiency, scalability, and performance for AI workloads on devices and in the cloud. Join us to be part of a group that defines the future of AI hardware engineering.

title: Senior CPU Architecture and Benchmarking Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Role

Join Intel's architecture team as a Senior CPU Architecture and Benchmarking Engineer. You will drive rigorous, low-level investigations into CPU designs, crafting targeted microbenchmarks that expose microarchitectural behavior at fine granularity and translating those findings into actionable architectural guidance. Your work will bridge the gap between silicon measurement, software behavior, and architectural definition, playing a key role in shaping Intel's future CPU roadmap.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, implement, and analyze pinpointed microbenchmarks to explore and characterize low-level microarchitectural behavior including branch prediction, instruction fetch/decode, execution units, memory subsystem, prefetchers, and power delivery interactions
  • Investigate and document microarchitectural details of CPU designs through systematic benchmarking and analysis
  • Evaluate the impact of system software layers — including OS schedulers, runtime libraries, compilers, and firmware — on end-product CPU performance and power efficiency
  • Identify power/performance gaps and propose concrete architectural solutions and mitigations
  • Collaborate with silicon lab, simulation, backend, and RTL teams to correlate benchmarking findings with pre-silicon models and post-silicon measurements
  • Explore and evaluate proposed microarchitectural ideas in CPU performance simulators, providing quantitative measure of value
  • Develop and maintain tooling, test infrastructure, and analysis frameworks to support repeatable and scalable benchmarking workflows
  • Communicate technical findings clearly and persuasively in written reports and presentations to senior engineering and product teams

To Be Successful in This Role, You Should Demonstrate

  • Intellectual curiosity and a systematic mindset when investigating complex microarchitectural behavior, with the rigor to design experiments that yield clear, reproducible conclusions
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across silicon, simulation, and software teams to align findings and drive architectural decisions

  • Demonstrated experience designing and interpreting low-level microbenchmarks for CPU characterization
  • Proficiency in assembly programming and low-level performance tooling (e.g., EMON/PMU counters, VTune, or equivalent)
