title: HPC System Architecture
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The HPC System Architect is the senior technical lead responsible for defining the next generation of Intel's leading-edge high-performance computing systems. Reporting directly to Nic Dube, Corporate Vice President and General Manager of Data Center Systems and Solutions, this position owns forward-looking HPC system architecture from concept through committed definition.

You will work directly with Intel's CPU and GPU teams to architect the systems that follow today's products - shaping silicon requirements, and defining system-level architecture for the large-scale, scale-out clusters that characterize production HPC. The role spans full-system definition: compute node design, memory and I/O balance, scale-out fabric and topology, and the software stack that determines delivered application performance at scale.

You will engage directly with the customers that set the leading edge of HPC - DOE national laboratories and their exascale and post-exascale programs, financial services institutions, oil and gas operators, and major academic and government research computing centers - translating their workload and facility requirements into system architectures Intel can build, and Intel's roadmap into system concepts they can commit to.

Responsibilities

  • Own system-level architecture for next-generation HPC clusters: node definition, CPU and GPU configuration, memory bandwidth-to-capacity balance, I/O and parallel storage architecture, and scale-out fabric and topology.
  • Define scale-out interconnect architecture - fabric selection, network topology, bisection bandwidth and blocking ratios, collective and communication performance, and resilience at thousands-of-node scale.
  • Partner with the CPU and GPU teams to define product requirements for future HPC systems, bringing system-level and workload evidence into silicon definition while requirements remain open.
  • Build performance models that project delivered application throughput at scale on unreleased silicon and use them to drive configuration and roadmap decisions.
  • Lead architecture co-design and benchmark definition with leadership HPC customers, including acceptance criteria for standard and customer-proprietary application suites.
  • Drive HPC requirements into Intel's CPU, GPU, platform, and software roadmaps across DCG and the product and design organizations.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies for next-generation HPC systems, including advanced memory, Ultra Ethernet and other scale-out fabric standards, optical interconnect, and heterogeneous accelerator integration.
  • Produce reference architectures and system specifications that platform teams, OEM and ODM partners, and system integrators can build to.
  • Grow and lead HPC architecture capability within the team, providing technical direction and mentorship to architects and engineers.

Successful Candidate Profile

  • Deep expertise in HPC system architecture at cluster scale, spanning CPU and GPU configuration, memory subsystem design, scale-out interconnect, and parallel storage.
  • Demonstrated experience defining systems around unreleased silicon and influencing CPU or accelerator requirements from a system and workload perspective.
  • Fluency with HPC workload characteristics and performance analysis, including quantitative reasoning about scaling behavior, communication patterns, and bottlenecks at scale.
  • Working knowledge of the HPC software stack - MPI, OpenMP, GPU programming models, schedulers, and math and communication libraries.
  • Proven credibility with sophisticated technical customers in high-stakes procurement and co-design settings.
  • Strong understanding of the competitive HPC landscape, including alternative CPU and accelerator architectures, fabric options, and system vendor positioning.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills, effective with both deep technical audiences and executive stakeholders.
  • Comfort with high ambiguity and a track record of driving clarity in undefined technical areas.
  • Willingness to travel domestically and internationally for customer engagements and technical conferences.

Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related technical field.
10+ years of experience in HPC, data center, or server system architecture, design, or engineering.
5+ years of experience in a customer-facing or externally-facing technical role.
Demonstrated experience defining or deploying large-scale compute clusters.

Preferred Qualifications
Master's degree or PhD in a relevant technical discipline.
Experience defining next-generation systems in partnership with CPU or GPU product and design teams.
Experience supporting DOE national laboratory or comparable large-scale public-sector HPC procurements.
Domain experience in a definitional HPC vertical: financial services, oil and gas and seismic processing, weather and climate, computational chemistry or biology, or manufacturing and CAE.
Hands-on experience with scale-out fabrics including InfiniBand, Ultra Ethernet, or other high-performance interconnect.
Experience with system-level performance modeling and workload characterization at scale.
Experience with converged HPC and AI system design.

title: GPU Logic Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 


As a GPU Logic Design Engineer, you will play a vital role in developing cutting-edge graphics IPs required for next-generation GPU designs. By leveraging your expertise in logic design and RTL coding, you will contribute to the creation of functional units, GPU IP blocks, and their integration into system-on-chip (SoC) designs.

You will collaborate with diverse teams to define architecture and microarchitecture features, optimizing logic to meet power, performance, area, and timing targets. Your work will directly impact Intel's leadership in graphics technology, enabling innovative solutions for a wide range of applications and products.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop RTL code and implement optimized logic designs for GPU IPs, ensuring alignment with architecture and microarchitecture specifications.
  • Perform power, performance, area, and timing optimization to meet design goals during physical implementation.
  • Participate in defining architecture and microarchitecture features for GPU blocks, contributing to innovation and technology leadership.
  • Execute unit-level verification, debug failing RTL tests, and resolve design issues to achieve correctness, functionality, and robustness at all verification hierarchies.
  • Utilize formal equivalence verification (FEV) techniques to ensure design accuracy and fidelity across development stages.
  • Collaborate with SoC customers to ensure seamless and high-quality integration of GPU blocks into full chip designs.
  • Drive microarchitecture-level enhancements and provide technical documentation to support design and development activities.

Qualifications:


Minimum Qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position.

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field with 4+ or more years of experience in RTL design and logic development with expertise in System Verilog.

OR

  • Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field with 3+ or more years of experience in RTL design and logic development with expertise in System Verilog.

OR

  • PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field with 6+ or more months of experience in RTL design and logic development with expertise in System Verilog.


Preferred Qualifications, are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates:

  • Proficiency in low-power design techniques, including UPF coding and debugging.
  • Experience with static timing analysis and formal equivalence verification (FEV).
  • Understanding of GPU architecture fundamentals and digital design principles.
  • Technical proficiency in TCL scripting for design automation tasks.
  • Demonstrated ability to debug microarchitecture and hardware simulations effectively.
  • Advanced knowledge of microarchitecture fundamentals and GPU validation methodologies.
  • Experience with power and performance validation and debugging in large-scale GPU designs.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with a track record of working in cross-functional teams to solve complex problems.

Requirements listed would be obtained through a combination of industry relevant job experience, internship experiences and or schoolwork/classes/research.

title: Senior Advanced Packaging Defect Inspection Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Advanced Packaging Technology Development (APTD) Metrology Group at Intel sits at the heart of our most critical technology development and pathfinding programs. As packaging architectures grow increasingly complex, the role of metrology has evolved far beyond traditional inspection and measurement — it has become a strategic enabler of technology progress, yield learning, and program decision-making confidence.


We are seeking a Senior Module Development Engineer who combines deep hands-on expertise in next-generation metrology equipment with a broad, current awareness of where the semiconductor metrology industry is heading.


The ideal candidate brings the technical credibility to work at the equipment level and the strategic clarity to translate industry knowledge into a forward-looking roadmap that keeps our capabilities ahead of program demand. This requires genuine engagement with the global metrology landscape — staying current with advances in measurement science, emerging equipment capabilities, and evolving industry standards — and applying that knowledge with sound judgment and determine which capabilities are worth pursuing and when.


This engineer will be embedded in our most advanced development and pathfinding programs from their earliest stages — ensuring that measurement strategies are defined, equipment is ready, and metrology coverage is in place before process flows are locked and before gaps can become program risks. A critical dimension of this role is the end-to-end qualification of new metrology equipment — taking ownership from initial tool installation and acceptance testing through process validation and full fab readiness — ensuring every new tool meets the performance and capability standards our programs require.


This engineer will also serve as a key technical resource for fab support, and ensuring the metrology tool fleet consistently operates at the highest level of performance and availability. The ability to move fluidly between strategic roadmap work and hands-on fab problem solving is essential — and is what makes this role both uniquely challenging and uniquely rewarding.


This is a role that demands technical depth, industry awareness, and the ability to lead with influence across a wide range of partners — from process integration and module engineering to advanced process control, AI and automation, and senior program leadership. The ideal candidate resolves complex process challenges with the same confidence and credibility they bring to presenting a technology investment case to senior leadership.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Drive technology development and enablement across both high-volume manufacturing and future technology nodes — delivering process integration and equipment solutions that meet desired device specifications and performance targets
  • Lead the design and development of technically sophisticated metrology and inspection processes  including material selection, parameter optimization, equipment configuration, and system design to enable new product architectures and functional requirements
  • Define and own the metrology group's long-range technology roadmap translating a deep understanding of industry trends, emerging measurement technologies, and program requirements into a clear, prioritized strategy that keeps our capabilities ahead of demand
  • Perform pathfinding activities in support of process and hardware development enabling the manufacturing of innovative device architectures and developing roadmaps for technologies that support future program needs.
  • Conduct process technology feasibility studies through theoretical simulations and practical engineering methods providing early, evidence-based assessments of new measurement approaches before committing to full qualification Evaluate and qualify next-generation metrology and inspection equipment end-to-end — from installation and acceptance testing through process validation and full fab readiness — ensuring every new tool meets the performance and capability standards our programs require.
  • Serve as the primary technical resource for fab support — providing engineering disposition on process excursions, driving resolution of metrology-related program holds, and maintaining the tool fleet at the highest level of performance and availability.
  • Recommend and implement equipment and process modifications that improve production efficiency, optimize output, and enhance manufacturing techniques for both existing and next-generation products.
  • Partner with key equipment and materials suppliers to develop and implement enabling elements of the technology — building direct technical relationships that go beyond standard supplier engagement to actively co-shape next-generation tool capabilities and roadmaps.
  • Remain current on relevant industry process, materials, and metrology trends — developing a forward-looking view of future technology needs and partnering with the vendor ecosystem to build a cost-sensitive, capability-driven roadmap that pushes the industry forward.
  • Lead metrology module development across multiple concurrent advanced packaging programs — taking full ownership from first wafer through process sign-off, including recipe development, specification setting, SPC strategy, and sampling plan definition.
  • Design and implement rapid inline feedback mechanisms that compress the time between experiment execution and actionable insight — directly accelerating cycles of learning across TD and pathfinding programs.
  • Collaborate with AI, machine learning, and advanced process control teams to develop intelligent monitoring and excursion detection strategies — evolving from threshold-based alarms toward predictive, context-aware process control.
  • Represent the metrology group in cross-functional program reviews — communicating metrology readiness, capability status, and risk with clarity and credibility to integration, process, and senior program leadership teams

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Experience would be obtained through a combination of prior education level classes, and current level school classes, projects, research and relevant previous job and/or internship experience.


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in materials science, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, chemical engineering, physics, chemistry, or related STEM field with 4+ years of relevant experience.
  • OR master’s degree in the same fields with 2+ years of relevant experience.
  • OR PhD in the same fields.
  • Relevant experience in any of the following:
    • Expertise in semiconductor processing, wafer-level assembly, or cleanroom environments.
    • Proficiency in process development methodologies, statistical process control, and manufacturing process improvement.
    • Technical expertise in module engineering or fab process/hardware technology development.

Preferred Qualifications

  • PhD and 3+ years of experience in relevant field and any of the below:
    • Strong metrology fundamental understanding and development experience.
    • Strong collaboration skills with cross-functional teams, including yield and operations.
    • Demonstrated skills to leverage data analysis tools for process optimization and continuous improvement.
    • Experience with packaging processes, equipment automation development, or project management.
    • Passionate about advancing Intel's strategic goals and driving meaningful industry advancements.
    • Experience in Python, Dashboard Creation, and Scripting
    • Direct experience engaging with metrology equipment vendors at a technical roadmap level as a co-development partner

descriptionHtml:

title: Senior Signal Integrity Engineer (Hands-on)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel Central Engineering Group (CEG) team delivers best-in-class Ethernet products and is at the heart of Intel's transformation from a PC company to a company that powers the cloud and billions of smart, connected computing devices. CEG's compelling Ethernet products move the world's data and are the foundations of cloud service and telecommunications data centers. You will be exposed to High-Speed I/O protocols such as PCIeGen6-7, DDR5-6, and PAM4 Ethernet 224Gb, which are a part of our Ethernet Infrastructure Processing Unit (Intel IPU) and Foundation NIC (FNIC) Ethernet product lines. We propose a dynamic and flexible workplace position, working directly with highly capable design, system, and pre/post-silicon teams within the organization. Most of the team's engineers have 10+ years of experience, and we are looking for a highly skilled multidisciplinary engineer with proven experience in Signal Integrity engineering to lead the hardware design of our next division projects' challenges and be part of Ethernet networking's accelerated growth. In this position, as a signal integrity engineer, you will be responsible for modeling channel elements in 3D and 2D EM simulation tools for pre- and post-layout stages of package and platform design for PCIe, Ethernet, and memory interfaces. You are expected to have a thorough understanding of RF circuits and electromagnetic wave propagation; the role includes learning the specifications of each interface and the required design limitations that should be verified. You will be expected to lead all signal integrity activities related to multiple projects for various high-speed and low-speed interfaces utilizing traditional and automated tools. You will work closely with silicon design teams and Hard IP vendors and will be responsible for the model's correlation based on cross-section and electrical measurements at the post-manufacturing stage and modeling manufacturing variation impact on the channels. You will be responsible for running the sign-off simulation flows for various designs, providing feedback to the design teams, and being hands-on in the lab for experiments when required. You would also be responsible for identifying/qualifying new AI-based automation techniques and solutions and providing technical leadership to working groups/task forces through debugging and reviews.

Qualifications:

Required Skills and Experience
• B.Sc./M.Sc. Electrical Engineer with over 7 years of relevant experience in Signal Integrity
• Proven design experience in the semiconductor ASIC development industry is a MUST
• Proven planning and design flow buildup
• Proven experience with PCB technology and layout techniques (Analog and Digital) including stack-up, routing, and advance SI/PI consideration
• Proven hands-on experience with EDA tools: HFSS, CST, ADS, Simbeor, or equivalent
• Knowledge of CAD tools: Cadence Allegro or Mentor Expedition, or equivalent
• Proven experience with modeling and simulation one of the Ethernet, PCIe, DDR interfaces
• Familiar with layout technics
• Working experience with AI-based tools
• Lab hands-on experience in high-speed, low-speed, and clocks circuitry signals measurement such as high-end Oscilloscopes, VNA, TDR, BERT's, etc.
• Excellent debugging skills, ability to analyze problems, diagnose the root cause and apply corrective actions
• Ability to work as a team player and contribute in a cross-functional product team on a daily basis
• Strong verbal and written communication skills in English for interacting with design, evaluation and production engineers; customers; technical marketing engineers; and program managers

title: SoC Design Verification Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Team:

You will be joining Intel's cutting-edge product development group, a team focused on designing and verifying advanced semiconductor solutions. This group is at the forefront of innovation, delivering high-quality, scalable products that drive Intel's leadership in technology and performance. By contributing your skills here, you will help shape the future of computing and enable groundbreaking advancements in the industry.


Position Overview:

As a SoC Design Verification Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring that Intel's complex System-on-Chip (SoC) designs meet functional specifications and deliver high-quality performance. You will design scalable and reusable verification plans, develop test environments, and execute tests to uncover issues and improve functionality. Your contributions will directly enhance Intel's product quality and ensure optimal performance in presilicon development.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Create and update UVM-based test bench generation and test case creation
  • Define and develop scalable and reusable block, subsystem, and SoC verification plans
  • Create test benches and verification environments that align with microarchitecture specifications
  • Execute verification plans, including emulation and system simulation models, to ensure design functionality and uncover bugs
  • Debug and root cause issues in presilicon environments, implementing corrective measures to address failures
  • Collaborate with architects, RTL developers, postsilicon teams, and physical design teams to improve verification of complex architectural features
  • Document and maintain test plans, driving technical reviews with design and architecture teams
  • Integrate security coverage activities within test plans, including regression and debug tests
  • Maintain and improve existing functional verification infrastructure and methodologies
  • Absorb learnings from postsilicon development and incorporate feedback into improved verification strategies.

To Be Successful, You Should Demonstrate the Following:

  • Ability to work collaboratively across interdisciplinary teams
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to work across interdisciplinary teams
  • Passion for tackling complex problems and delivering innovative solutions.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, with 7+ years of hands-on experience in SoC design verification, including demonstrated expertise in OVM/UVM methodologies, debugging, and test planningOR
  • Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, with 6+ years of hands-on experience in SoC design verification, including demonstrated expertise in OVM/UVM methodologies, debugging, and test planning.

The experience must include:

  • AMBA protocols such as CHI, AXI, AHB, and APB with industry-standard VIP from various EDA vendors
  • Creation and updating of UVM-based test benches and test case creation

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with postsilicon validation and incorporating feedback into presilicon test plans
  • Familiarity with emulation models and system simulation tools for performance analysis

We invite you to bring your expertise and creativity to Intel, where your contributions will make a lasting impact on future technology. Join us and shape the future of computing with your skills and dedication.

title: AI Hardware Engineering Intern
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Job

Intel is seeking exceptional Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, and AI/ML students to join an AI Hardware Engineering internship focused on the future of AI inference and AI infrastructure with hardware/software co-design expertise. 


This internship approaches AI infrastructure as a hardware/software co-design challenge. The intern will analyze how model architecture, inference behavior, memory movement, data-center constraints, and software stacks influence end-to-end customer outcomes, including throughput, latency, time-to-first-token, tokens per second, power consumption, utilization, total cost of ownership, and deployability. 


The successful candidate will be technically hands-on, capable of independent research and analysis, and comfortable working within a highly technical team of researchers and engineers addressing complex AI hardware and infrastructure challenges. 


What You Will Do 

  • Conduct technical research on the next generation of AI infrastructure, including CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, ASICs, memory systems, networking, storage, rack-scale architecture, power delivery, cooling, and cluster management. 
  • Analyze GenAI and agentic AI workloads to understand their hardware implications, including transformer architecture based inference, mixture-of-experts architectures, multimodal models, real-time interactive inference, and distributed serving. 
  • Evaluate the hardware behavior of AI inference pipelines, including the distinct demands of prompt processing/prefill and token generation/decode, memory capacity, memory bandwidth, KV-cache management, compute utilization, interconnect bandwidth, and latency. For example, cluster architecture around optimizing both prefill and decode through hardware, memory, and system co-design. 
  • Identify product and system gaps that may limit Intel's ability to serve AI customers effectively, including hardware capabilities, developer tooling, performance libraries, reference architectures, deployment models, observability, and ecosystem enablement.  

- Expertise in modern high-performance CPU, GPU, or AI accelerator architecture and hardware/software interactions. 

- Support Silicon HW programs through multiple phases of the silicon lifecycle, with end-to-end chip execution from concept to silicon. 

- Good understanding with firmware codebases, compilers, kernels, serving stacks and model architectures.    

- Familiar with driving silicon design for subsystems and/or top-level functions with ASICs and SOCs from an architecture specification to production silicon including memory subsystems and interconnects: scale up, scale out, scale across, power management , liquid cooling at rack scale level, deep system level observability & telemetry and dependent impact into Gen AI and LLM level performance/tco/execution KPIs 

  • Develop technical recommendations for what Intel should build, optimize, enable, partner on to meet AI customer requirements based on deep understanding of customer use cases, workload performance, and ML systems research. 
  • Benchmark and compare relevant AI hardware and infrastructure approaches across performance, power efficiency, cost, programmability, memory hierarchy, scalability, ecosystem maturity, and workload fit. 
  • Develop technical models, simulations, prototypes, or analysis tools to evaluate hardware/software trade offs for AI workloads. 
  • Investigate system bottlenecks across compute, memory, networking, storage, and software orchestration, and propose methods to improve end-to-end AI workload performance. 
  • Work with Intel technical teams and external ISVs to collect data on model requirements, inference bottlenecks, deployment challenges, hardware optimization opportunities, and customer priorities. 
  • Engage with AI software ecosystem partners, including model providers, inference-engine developers, cloud providers, framework teams, and ISVs, to understand how their stacks interact with underlying hardware. 
  • Good understanding of modern AI software layers, including PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, SGLang, model serving, TensorRT-LLM, Triton, Kubernetes, and Neocloud design efficiencies.  
  • Present findings through architecture diagrams, benchmark analyses, technical reports, design recommendations, and executive-ready presentations. 

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

  • Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, AI/ML, Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • Strong foundation in computer architecture, operating systems, distributed systems, parallel computing, AI/ML systems, high-performance computing, or systems software.
  • Familiarity with generative AI models and inference concepts, including transformers, attention, token generation, model serving, quantization, batching, KV cache, long-context workloads, and latency-throughput trade-offs.
  • Experience programming in one or more of the languages - C, C++, Rust, CUDA, SYCL, OpenCL, or a comparable low-level or performance-oriented language.
  • Strong academic performance with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher required.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Coursework, research, or project experience in computer architecture, VLSI, digital design, ASIC/FPGA systems, compilers, kernel development, GPU programming, distributed systems, high-performance computing, or AI systems.
  • Experience using profiling, tracing, or benchmarking tools to evaluate CPU, GPU, accelerator, network, memory, storage, or software performance.
  • Familiarity with AI hardware platforms such as Intel Xeon processors, Intel GPUs, NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, TPUs, custom AI accelerators, FPGAs, or domain-specific inference ASICs.
  • Understanding of memory hierarchies and performance concepts, including cache behavior, DRAM, HBM, memory bandwidth, memory capacity, latency, data locality, DMA, and data movement.
  • Experience with inference frameworks or runtimes such as vLLM, SGLang, Hugging Face Transformers, PyTorch, Triton, or Ray.
  • Familiarity with AI systems infrastructure such as Linux, containers, Kubernetes, distributed storage, RDMA over Ethernet, InfiniBand, CXL, PCIe, NVMe, UALink/eSUN based interconnects, silicon photonics and cluster-management software.
  • Some experience with simulation, modeling, emulation, RTL, FPGA prototyping, firmware, driver development, or low-level debugging.
  • Some experience contributing to open-source systems, ML infrastructure, compiler, kernel, framework, or performance-engineering projects.

title: Yield Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Embark with us on a journey of growth and transformation as we create exceptionally engineered technology and bring AI everywhere. As a valued team member, your adaptability and attention to detail will contribute to our drive for results and relentless pursuit of quality, ensuring we meet our customers' needs with precision.


Join us and build on our legacy of innovation and collaboration as we deliver world‑changing technology that improves the life of every person on the planet.


Life at Intel: https://jobs.intel.com/en/life-at-intel


As a Yield Development Engineer, you will play a critical role in advancing Intel's cutting-edge semiconductor technologies. You will be part of a team responsible for driving yield improvement strategies that span the entire lifecycle of a technology node, from research and development through high-volume manufacturing. Your contributions will directly influence Intel's ability to maintain its leadership in the semiconductor industry, ensuring the success of innovative silicon solutions that shape the future of computing. Collaborating with cross-functional teams, you will develop methods and tools to analyze vast data sets, identify yield limiters, and implement process changes that enable Intel to achieve its yield milestones. This role promises an opportunity to shape groundbreaking technologies and generate impactful advancements for the industry and beyond. 


Responsibilities will include but will not be limited to:

  • Perform statistical analysis to construct accurate process development roadmaps and drive technology yield milestones. 
  • Analyze and consolidate diverse data sources to identify defect modes and create yield models. 
  • Develop multivariate algorithms for high-volume data analysis to identify root cause yield limiters. 
  • Extract insights from structured and unstructured data using machine learning, coding techniques, and advanced statistical methods. 
  • Collaborate with process integration, defect engineering, and electrical fault isolation teams to debug yield detractors and propose solutions. 
  • Conduct fault isolation and failure analysis to determine the root cause of yield-impacting issues. 
  • Develop tools and systems that transform manufacturing data into actionable yield improvement strategies. 
  • Work closely with design teams to resolve product-related yield issues and improve manufacturability. 
  • Execute new product introductions and participate in factory task forces to ensure process optimization.

Manufacturing Development Customer Engineering (MDCE) is a new organization within Intel Foundry Technology Manufacturing focused on improving process capability for Intel's technology nodes from initial product qualification to high volume manufacturing with the vision of making technology ramp a competitive advantage for Intel foundry. This team is responsible for transferring new technologies into high-volume manufacturing, driving process optimization and continuous improvement, resolving complex yield and manufacturing issues, partnering closely with technology development and factory teams to ensure robust, predictable silicon delivery.

About the Role

MDCE Metals Deposition Engineer is responsible for enabling best-in-class process performance and manufacturability for advanced metals deposition modules across Intel 18A, Intel 3, and Intel 12nm technology nodes. This role sits at the intersection of Technology Development (TD), High Volume Manufacturing (HVM), and Customer Engineering, driving module readiness from early development through full HVM ramp and sustaining.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

  • Leadership and Trust: Strong leadership, resourcefulness, and the ability to manage extremely sensitive information.

Demonstrated ability to understand and interpret industry trends, create and drive strategies, work independently, simultaneously manage diverse and extensive assignments while remaining organized and productive.

Job Responsibilities Include but Are Not Limited To:

  • Problem Solving: Own the resolution of technical challenges and integrate solutions across multiple groups (including technology development and high volume manufacturing) Demonstrated ability to perform data driven root cause analysis using structured problem-solving methods and common data/analytics tools.

title: Director of Supply Planning - Assembly, Test, and Materials
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Role We are seeking a Director of Supply Planning for Assembly, Test and Materials to lead supply planning across our global semiconductor back-end manufacturing network. This leader is responsible for developing and managing the executable supply plan across assembly, test, and associated materials. The role translates end to end supply requirements and business priorities into a capacity, material, qualification, and flow feasible plan for the Assembly and Test network. The Director will lead a planning organization responsible for balancing manufacturing requirements across factories, anticipating constraints, developing recovery scenarios, and ensuring that capacity, materials, and manufacturing capabilities are synchronized to deliver committed supply. This role requires a leader who can operate at both strategic and operational levels. It involves building planning capabilities and processes while also leading the organization through complex supply, capacity, and material constraints. Key Responsibilities Assembly and Test Supply Planning Lead the development and execution of the supply plan across Assembly and Test manufacturing operations. Translate end to end supply requirements into executable stage level plans that optimize manufacturing capacity, cycle time, yield, qualifications, product mix, routing, and other manufacturing constraints. Own planning across the Assembly and Test network, including a worldwide network of internal manufacturing sites Ensure that Assembly and Test plans remain synchronized across with upstream die availability, materials availability, and downstream finished goods requirements. Materials Planning and Readiness Lead materials planning and readiness in support of the Assembly and Test supply plan. Translate manufacturing plans into requirements for materials such as substrates, lead frames, interposers, packaging components, and other critical materials. Partner closely with the procurement team to identify material shortages and supply risks early, quantify their impact to manufacturing and supply commitments, integrate supplier commitments, and develop mitigation and recovery scenarios. Constraint Management and Scenario Planning Identify current and emerging capacity, material, and manufacturing constraints across the Assembly and Test network. Lead scenario analysis to determine the impact of constraints and evaluate alternatives such as product reallocation, alternate manufacturing routes, capacity changes, material prioritization, and changes in production timing. Drive recovery planning when execution deviates from plan, working with the factory to ensure actions are prioritized based on their impact to supply and customer commitments. Stage Planning and Integration Serve as the primary Assembly, Test and Materials planning interface with Central Supply Planning, manufacturing operations, Procurement, engineering, product organizations, and other supply chain functions. Translate end to end requirements and priorities into feasible plans and provide timely feedback when Assembly, Test, or material constraints affect the end to end supply plan. Drive synchronization of capacity and material constraints across multiple manufacturing stages to reduce unnecessary WIP, queue time, expedites, replanning, and other non value added flow. Planning Execution and Performance Establish and manage a disciplined planning cadence that connects long term capacity and materials planning with tactical supply planning and near term manufacturing execution. Maintain clear accountability for planning performance and continuously improve the quality, stability, and executability of the supply plan. Establish and manage key performance indicators including: • Supply and commit performance • Stage plan and schedule performance • Material readiness and commit performance • Inventory and WIP health • Cycle time performance • Plan stability and planning accuracy • Constraint recovery Use performance data to identify systemic planning gaps and drive corrective actions across planning, manufacturing, materials, and business processes. Planning Systems and Capability Development Drive continuous improvement of supply-planning processes, systems, data, and decision-making capabilities. Ensure planning models accurately represent manufacturing capacity, product flows, BOMs, routings, yields, cycle times, lead times, qualifications, and material constraints. Improve advanced planning capabilities, including constraint-based planning, scenario analysis, exception management, and planning automation. Drive adoption and effective utilization of advanced planning platforms, including Blue Yonder or comparable supply planning solutions. Develop a planning organization that increasingly manages by exception and scenario rather than through manual expediting and transactional intervention. Leadership Responsibilities Build, lead, and develop a high-performing team of Assembly, Test, and Materials supply-planning professionals. Create clear accountability across stage planning, Central Supply Planning, manufacturing operations, and Procurement. Develop planning talent capable of understanding both semiconductor manufacturing details and the broader supply chain implications of planning decisions. Create a culture of fact based decision making, early risk identification, cross-functional problem solving, and accountability for results. Communicate complex supply situations and tradeoffs clearly to senior executives and cross functional stakeholders. Influence decisions across organizational boundaries where the Director may not have direct authority but is accountable for driving an executable supply outcome. What Success Looks Like Success in this role means that Assembly, Test, and Materials operate from a single, credible, executable supply plan. Constraints are identified early enough to influence decisions. Material shortages are understood before they disrupt manufacturing. Capacity decisions are made based on end-to-end supply requirements rather than local utilization alone. Planning signals are stable and trusted by manufacturing operations. Most importantly, the organization consistently converts Central Supply Planning requirements into executable manufacturing plans that deliver the intended supply while improving flow, inventory, cycle time, and overall planning effectiveness.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Business, or a related discipline. • 12+ years of experience in supply chain management or semiconductor engineering related field with a Bachelor's degree, 8+ years with a Master's degree, or 6+ years with a PhD. • Demonstrated leadership experience managing complex supply-planning or manufacturing-planning organizations. • Deep understanding of constrained manufacturing environments and the interaction between capacity, materials, product mix, cycle time, inventory, and customer requirements. • Experience developing and executing supply plans across multiple manufacturing stages and locations. • Strong analytical and scenario-planning capabilities with demonstrated ability to make decisions under complex supply constraints. • Proven track record in leading diverse and global teams to achieve measurable outcomes. • Demonstrated ability to lead across organizational boundaries and influence senior stakeholders. Preferred Qualifications • Advanced degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Business, or a related field. • Direct experience with semiconductor Assembly and Test manufacturing and planning. • Experience with semiconductor packaging materials, substrates, and associated material-planning constraints. • Experience with advanced planning systems such as Blue Yonder, SAP IBP, or comparable constraint-based planning platforms. • Experience with multi-stage planning, capacity allocation, scenario planning, and optimization. • Demonstrated experience transforming planning organizations from manual or reactive processes toward integrated, exception-based planning.

The Sr. Director of Product Management serves as the senior product owner for Intel's Infrastructure Processing Unit (IPU) and Ethernet controller and adapter portfolio, with end-to-end responsibility for product vision, strategy, definition, positioning, and lifecycle management across Data Center, Enterprise, Edge, and Embedded markets. Defines and drives long-range product and portfolio strategy based on customer requirements, market dynamics, competitive intelligence, technology trends, and Intel business priorities. title: Analog Circuit Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Role Overview
As an Integrated Voltage Regulator (IVR) Design Engineer, you will be responsible for the architecture, design, and implementation of high-performance power management solutions directly integrated onto advanced processors (CPUs, GPUs, or SoCs). You will work at the intersection of Analog/Mixed-Signal IC design and Power Electronics to improve energy efficiency and performance in next-generation computing systems.

Key Responsibilities
Circuit Architecture and Design: Develop and refine analog topologies such as Operational Amplifiers (Op-Amps), Bandgap References, Data Converters (ADC/DAC), and Phase-Locked Loops (PLLs).
Design and Simulation: Perform transistor-level design using industry-standard tools (like Cadence Virtuoso). Conduct extensive Monte Carlo simulations, corner analysis, and noise analysis to ensure high yield and reliability.
Layout Oversight: Collaborate closely with layout engineers to guide critical placement and routing, focusing on matching, shielding, and minimizing parasitic capacitance/resistance.
Verification: Use SPICE-based simulators to verify circuit functionality against rigorous performance specifications (speed, power, gain, etc.).
Post-Silicon Characterization: Bench-test silicon prototypes in the lab to validate performance against pre-silicon models and debug hardware anomalies

Qualifications:

Required Technical Skills
Transistor Fundamentals: Expert knowledge of MOSFET/BJT device physics, small-signal modeling, and aging effects.
EDA Tool Proficiency: Mastery of Cadence (Spectre/Virtuoso), Mentor Graphics, or Synopsys tool suites.
Signal Integrity: Deep understanding of thermal noise, jitter, crosstalk, and power supply rejection ratio (PSRR).
Mixed-Signal Flow: Familiarity with Verilog-A or Verilog-AMS for behavioral modeling of analog blocks.
Qualifications
Education: BS, MS, or PhD in Electrical Engineering (EE) with a concentration in Analog IC Design.
Experience: 3 - 7 years of experience in analog design (FinFET or planar CMOS nodes).
Analytical Mindset: Strong mathematical background for analyzing feedback systems and stability.

title: Sr AI Runtime Architect - Neuromorphic Computing
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Opportunity:

For nearly a decade, Intel's Neuromorphic Computing Lab, together with a global ecosystem of 250+ research groups, has explored architectures, algorithms, and software inspired by the brain's extraordinary efficiency, scalability, and adaptability. Our Loihi series of research chips pioneered event-driven, sparse, and massively parallel neuro-inspired processing, fueling over 100 peer-reviewed publications that validate the promise of this novel approach.

Now, we're entering an exciting new chapter: transforming these breakthroughs into real-world products that will power the coming era of physical AI systems - beyond the reach of GPUs and mainstream AI accelerators.

If you are passionate about pushing the boundaries of computing, from transistor-level innovation to software abstractions, join us. Help define the next wave of AI technology that harnesses the proven advantages of Intel's neuromorphic computing technology with the versatility demanded by modern AI workloads.

Position Overview:

Join the team building Intel's neuromorphic AI execution stack targeting edge and robotic systems. In this role, you will lead the team and technical direction for our next-generation runtime stack, while remaining hands-on in architecture and implementation. You will set the roadmap from the first product generation onward, on a spatial, event-driven architecture that redraws the boundary between compiler and runtime.

Responsibilities:

- Define and drive the technical vision, architecture, and roadmap for the runtime stack, from firmware to framework integration, while contributing hands-on to critical design and implementation.
- Architect and develop the runtime and performance tooling, and define the execution behavior that the firmware and drivers must implement, whether the device is attached to a host or runs standalone.
- Own the contracts between the runtime stack and the compiler, as well as its integration with industry-standard AI and robotics frameworks.
- Own the measurable performance, real-time behavior, and production quality of the stack across silicon and simulators.
- Collaborate with compiler, hardware, and application teams, as well as customers and partners, to translate workload requirements into runtime capabilities and feed performance insights back into compiler and hardware design.
- Provide technical leadership by establishing engineering practices and mentoring engineers.

About the Organization:

As part of Intel's CTO Office, you will join a vertically integrated incubation effort dedicated to bringing Intel's neuromorphic technology innovations to market. Our diverse team of engineers and researchers has pioneered sparse, event-based, neuromorphic architecture over multiple generations and is now focused on commercializing the technology in future Intel and partner products.

Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications

- BSc, MSc, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.
- 5+ years of experience developing and shipping AI runtime software, such as OpenVINO, TensorRT, ONNX Runtime, Ryzen AI, or comparable runtimes, for accelerators, GPUs, or other complex hardware, with working knowledge of the underlying drivers and firmware.
- 5+ years of experience leading the architecture of complex software systems, including defining technical direction and the interfaces to adjacent components.
- 5+ years of experience owning the performance and production quality of accelerator software, including profiling, benchmarking, and debugging across hardware and software boundaries.
- 5+ years of experience providing technical leadership to engineering teams, including mentoring engineers and leading cross-functional delivery.
- 10+ years of hands-on experience developing production-grade systems software in C/C++, with proficiency in Python, using disciplined engineering practices such as code reviews, automated testing, and CI/CD.
- 1+ years of hands-on experience with agentic software engineering, routinely using AI agents to design, implement, test, and review production code.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience managing engineering teams, including hiring and developing engineers.
- Experience with the internals of OpenVINO, oneAPI Level Zero, or comparable accelerator software stacks.
- Experience with spatial, dataflow, or statically scheduled accelerators where the compiler determines placement and scheduling.
- Experience with robotics or real-time systems, including deterministic execution and ecosystems such as ROS 2 or Holoscan.
- Experience developing or integrating functional or performance simulators into accelerator software stacks.
- Familiarity with device driver and firmware development for embedded Linux or RTOS-based systems.
- Experience with HW/SW co-design or performance modeling.

title: GPU Software Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Role

Join Intel's graphics software team and help deliver high-quality GPU experiences in AI domain.

As a GPU Software Engineer, you will develop, validate, debug, and optimize graphics software and GPU driver solutions across Intel platforms. You will work at the intersection of software and hardware, partnering with engineering teams to bring new graphics capabilities to market and solve complex system-level issues.


This is an opportunity to develop hands-on expertise across GPU architecture, graphics drivers, validation, debugging, performance, compute, and AI workloads.

 What You’ll Do

Key responsibilities will include but not limited to:

  • Develop and execute end-to-end validation solutions for GPU software, graphics drivers, and applications.
  • Debug and resolve complex software, driver, and system-level issues impacting GPU functionality, quality, and performance.
  • Triage defects, perform root-cause analysis, and collaborate with software and hardware engineering teams to drive issues to resolution.
  • Develop and maintain software, automation, and debugging tools that improve validation efficiency and product quality.
  • Analyze cross-component interactions and identify potential quality, performance, and compatibility issues.
  • Perform validation, triage, and debugging of GPU compute drivers, runtime layers, and AI framework integration failures across software and hardware teams.
  • Integrate latest AI features into end-to-end validation flows and analyze cross-component interactions to develop robust test scenarios.
  • Develop and maintain automation tools, benchmarking suites, and frameworks to improve validation and debug efficiency across AI compute and runtime components.
  • Optimize software performance, memory efficiency, and quality for emerging AI workloads, deep learning inference, and agentic applications.
  • Enable and validate forthcoming AI hardware acceleration capabilities for Intel's GPU platforms.
  • Collaborate on cross-OS software development and validation for GPU-accelerated AI and machine learning workloads.

  • Technical curiosity: Motivated to understand how software, GPU hardware, drivers, operating systems, and applications interact.
  • Problem-solving: Uses structured analysis and data to troubleshoot complex technical issues and identify root causes.

title: GPU Software Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact:


As a GPU Software Development Engineer, you will focus on enabling and optimizing Intel's GPUs by developing, backporting, and validating software solutions that span the stack-from firmware and device drivers to APIs and the application layer. You will play a critical role in designing, debugging, and improving GPU kernel drivers and graphics software on Linux platforms across diverse kernel environments and enterprise distributions, ensuring seamless integration and performance. Your contributions will directly support Intel's innovations in graphics and data center technologies.


Business Group:

The Data Center Group (DCG) drives Intel's leadership in computing innovation, with a focus on delivering high-performance solutions for data-centric markets. This group develops technologies that power advanced workloads in cloud computing, AI, and graphics acceleration. By joining DCG, you'll collaborate with experts dedicated to enabling cutting-edge GPU solutions that advance Intel's broader mission to shape the future of technology.


Key Responsibilities:


  • Develop and validate GPU kernel drivers and graphics software solutions, contributing to the full development lifecycle from design and implementation to testing and release across Linux platforms, including contributions to the open-source graphics software community where applicable.
  • Debug, optimize, and enable Linux DRM/KMD drivers - including root cause analysis of kernel panics, regressions, deadlocks, race conditions, and memory corruption across diverse hardware and software environments.
  • Design and implement new driver features, enhancements, and optimizations within the Linux DRM/KMD subsystem, collaborating closely with hardware and firmware teams to enable new GPU capabilities.
  • Adapt and backport upstream Intel GPU drivers (DRM/KMD) to LTS, enterprise, and customized customer kernel environments, designing and maintaining compatibility layers and out-of-tree packaging solutions such as DKMS.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams - spanning firmware, KMD, user-space runtime, and compute/graphics stacks - to ensure robust integration, compatibility, and stability across the full GPU software stack.
  • Partner with validation and DevOps teams to expand multi-kernel test matrices, regression suites, and automated build pipelines that catch compatibility breaks early.
  • Ensure high code quality and adherence to Linux kernel coding standards through active participation in design and code reviews, spanning both upstream driver development and backported driver deliverables.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:


  • Bachelor's degree in Software Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or Electronics/Electrical Engineering.
    5+ years of hands-on experience in large-scale software product development with deep focus on Linux kernel and system software engineering.
  • Expert-level C programming with deep understanding of Linux kernel internals, driver architecture, memory management, concurrency, locking primitives, and interrupt handling.
  • Proven experience developing and debugging Linux DRM/KMD drivers and device driver debugging mechanisms.
  • Hands-on experience backporting Linux kernel patches and drivers across kernel versions, with practical understanding of kernel API/ABI drift and compatibility wrapper construction.
  • Proficiency in Linux kernel debugging tools such as ftrace, perf, kdump/crash, kgdb, GDB, dynamic debug, and interpreting stack traces and lockdep reports.


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master's degree in Software Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or Electronics/Electrical Engineering.
  • Deep experience with Linux DRM/KMS subsystem, GPU memory management (TTM, GEM), DMA-BUF, and modern graphics/compute software stacks.
  • Experience with out-of-tree module frameworks (DKMS, Kbuild backport frameworks) and multi-kernel distribution packaging (RPM, DEB).
  • Experience triaging and resolving kernel regressions caused by upstream changes in core subsystems such as schedulers, memory allocators, power management, and PCIe buses.
  • Experience supporting customer-specific or enterprise Linux distributions such as RHEL, SLES, or Ubuntu LTS, including kernel validation and issue resolution in production environments.
  • Active patch submissions or contributions to the open-source Linux kernel or DRM/graphics community.

Join us to work on impactful projects that shape the future of GPU technology and advance Intel's mission of delivering world-changing innovations.

title: Sr Staff Substrate Yield Lead
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel Corporation is seeking a high-impact Yield Development Engineer to drive yield performance for cutting-edge manufacturing processes within the Substrate Technology and Development (SPTD) organization. In this role, you will own end-to-end yield improvement initiatives, leveraging your expertise in data analysis, defect resolution, and designnd transform the future of technology.

Intel's APTM organization is seeking a highly driven and execution-focused EMIB-T Substrate Yield Lead to lead yield performance for next-generation advanced packaging technologies, including EMIB-T (Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge with TSV), Intel's most advanced platform for heterogeneous integration. This is a high-visibility, high-accountability role with significant responsibility for enabling successful technology development and manufacturing readiness across both Intel Foundry Services (IFS) and Intel Product Groups (IPG).

The ideal candidate is a self-starter who thrives in ambiguous and fast-paced environments, proactively drives issues to closure, and requires minimal supervision. Success in this role requires strong technical depth, urgency in execution, the ability to influence cross-functional teams and suppliers, and a relentless focus on delivering yield and program milestones.

Business group

The SPTD Yield group is part of Intel Corporation and plays a critical role in driving innovation and delivering high-performance yield solutions that enable advanced semiconductor manufacturing. This team focuses on yield ownership, supplier engagement, and defect resolution, ensuring manufacturing excellence for Intel's cutting-edge technologies. By joining this group, you will collaborate across disciplines to support Intel's broader mission of delivering transformative and impactful technology solutions.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead process yield ownership, driving root cause analysis (RCA) and corrective actions for yield excursions.
  • Establish real-time yield monitoring dashboards and actionable performance metrics.
  • Serve as the primary technical interface with substrate suppliers to drive process accountability, defect reduction, and yield enhancement.
  • Partner with design and integration teams to optimize design rules and improve yield robustness through DFM and DFY initiatives.
  • Perform statistical data analysis using tools such as JMP and SQL scripting to identify yield limiters and develop solutions.
  • Apply advanced analytics or machine learning techniques to improve yield prediction and defect classification.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to solve complex technical challenges, supporting Intel's high-visibility manufacturing programs.

title: Yield Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel is looking for highly motivated individuals with strong technical background and capabilities to drive rapid continuous improvements in safety, quality, yield, reliability, cost, process stability/capability, and productivity while maintaining rigorous quality control. Your adaptability and attention to detail will contribute to our drive for results and relentless pursuit of quality, ensuring we meet our customers' needs with precision.

The role of a Defect Reduction Engineer is to deliver high-quality analytical insights and to drive yield improvement activities to minimize defects in BU and BE segments. All improvements and sustaining work are done in close collaboration and partnership with the process to improve the capability of the tools and processes.

Your responsibilities as a Defect Reduction Engineer may include, but are not limited to:

  • Performing detailed analysis to monitor inline yield and identify the root cause of defect and yield issues using various statistical/data mining tools.
  • Identifying excursionary or baseline sources of defects or yield impacts and recommending/leading corrective actions/fixes.
  • Lead/participate continuous improvement projects on products and processes for improved performance.
  • Provide expertise on process flow segments.
  • Lead/participate in multi-area problem solving teams to provide expertise to troubleshoot complex yield problems.

The ideal candidate should exhibit the following behavioral traits:

  • Solid analytical skills and a passion for data analysis and problem solving.
  • Proficiency in translating complex yield data into strategic action plans, establishing clear milestones, accountability, and ownership to drive rapid issue resolution.
  • Effective communication and presentation skills to influence decision-making in a wide variety of groups at all levels.
  • Excellent teamwork, leadership skills, problem solving and prioritization skills, and driving high-performance maintenance goals for the group.
  • Organizational skills with attention to detail.
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment with the flexibility to meet tight product timelines.
  • Strong drive for self-improvement and a passion for independently acquiring new technical skills, mastering emerging data science tools, and staying current with semiconductor industry trends to solve increasingly complex challenges.

Behavioral traits

  • Strong communication skills, proactive problem-solving capabilities, and adaptability in a fast-paced environment.
  • Connect analysis results to process fundamentals, tool behavior, and physics principles.

  • Bachelor's degree in Materials Science and Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or Chemistry, with 4+ years of hands-on experience in yield analysis, OR a Master's degree with 3+ years of experience, OR a Ph.D. with no prior professional experience.

    • Engineering analysis tools and scripting methods, including Python, JMP, and SQL.

title: Logistics Operations Manager
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
As a Logistics Operations Manager, you will oversee and drive logistics operations for inbound, interplant, and outbound materials, equipment, and finished goods. You will play a key role in ensuring operational excellence by managing critical logistics processes, optimizing solutions, and driving compliance across Intel's supply chain. Your contributions will directly enhance cost efficiency, delivery reliability, and performance standards, making a lasting impact on Intel's global logistics operations.

Business group
The Logistics Operations Manager role belongs to Intel Foundry's Logistics organization, which focuses on efficiently moving materials, equipment, and finished goods to support manufacturing processes and global customer delivery. This team is dedicated to driving operational excellence through process optimization, supplier collaboration, and innovative solutions, helping Intel deliver world-class products and meet customer expectations.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage logistics operations for inbound, interplant, and outbound shipments of materials, equipment, and finished goods.
  • Own dock operations to support site start-up, ramp, and steady-state logistics execution.
  • Monitor and drive performance against logistics KPIs, compliance requirements, and operational standards.
  • Analyze logistics processes and data to identify inefficiencies, defects, and opportunities for continuous improvement.
  • Track, escalate, and resolve shipping, warehouse, carrier, and execution exceptions to maintain delivery continuity.
  • Lead critical logistics escalations, minimizing disruptions to operations and ensuring customer satisfaction.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams and external logistics providers to optimize supply chain execution.
  • Leverage analytical tools and digital solutions to enhance cost efficiency, speed, quality, and reliability.
  • Deliver regular updates to senior leaders on logistics performance, risk assessments, and operational readiness.
  • Prepare and support logistics readiness for ongoing capacity growth, customer ramps, and strategic initiatives.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Logistics, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, or a related field.
  • Minimum 4 years of experience in logistics operations or third-party logistics (3PL) management with a Bachelor's degree, or 3 years with a Master's degree.
  • Expertise in warehouse operations, compliance protocols, and supplier governance, with a proven ability to manage execution end-to-end.
  • Strong analytical skills, with experience translating data into actionable decisions and sustained operational improvements.
  • Technical proficiency in monitoring logistics KPIs and driving operational excellence.
  • Experience managing EHS risks within warehouse, logistics, manufacturing, or industrial operations, particularly involving chemical handling, scheduled waste or high-value scrap, hazardous materials,.
  • Working knowledge of warehouse chemical-management requirements, including Safety Data Sheets, chemical compatibility, labeling, segregation, secondary containment, spill response, and emergency preparedness.
  • Demonstrated experience in operational risk assessment, control design, incident investigation, corrective action, and compliance management.
  • Experience developing and governing business processes, SOPs, control plans, and performance-management mechanisms.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Proven ability to thrive in dynamic, fast-paced operational environments.
  • Demonstrated initiative, ownership, and the ability to lead independently through ambiguity.
  • Experience supporting customer ramps, operational transformations, or large-scale logistics readiness initiatives.
  • Strong communication, collaboration, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence outcomes effectively.
  • Proven experience leading logistics quality programs, risk assessments, operational controls, and corrective/preventive action initiatives to ensure compliance, business continuity, and operational excellence.
  • Strong knowledge of logistics security, safety, regulatory compliance, and risk management frameworks, with the ability to identify vulnerabilities and implement sustainable mitigation plans.
  • Professional training or certification in EHS, chemical safety, scheduled-waste management, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, business process management, or risk management would be an advantage.
  • Experience supporting EHS and chemical-management controls in a semiconductor, electronics, manufacturing, or other high-technology environment.
  • Knowledge of Malaysian requirements relevant to warehouse operations, including the Occupational Safety and Health Act, Environmental Quality Regulations, and scheduled-waste management requirements.
  • Familiarity with structured risk and control methods such as HIRARC, FMEA, Management of Change, control self-assessments, and CAPA.
  • Experience managing third-party warehouse, scrap, recycling, waste-disposal, or chemical-handling service providers.

We encourage you to bring your logistics expertise and passion for operational excellence to Intel. Join us and be part of a team driving innovation, efficiency, and world-class solutions in the logistics domain globally.

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
As a Supplier Manager for Tier 2/3 substrate suppliers, you will play a pivotal role in developing and executing cutting-edge strategies that ensure Intel's supply chain remains ahead of industry demands. Industry constraints for t-glass, substrate core, build up film, MLCC, and other substrate ingredients are risking our ability to supply substrates and support Intel revenue. This role will work face to face with these suppliers who sell to our substrate suppliers and ensure we are proactively managing near-term and long term supply to ensure a healthy, competitive supply chain for substrates. The majority of these suppliers are based in Japan, requiring fluent Japanese and the ability to work from Intel's Tokyo office.

Business group
This role is part of Intel's Supply Chain organization, which is dedicated to driving innovation and operational excellence across Intel's global business. The team manages strategic sourcing and procurement activities, ensuring optimal supplier partnerships to support Intel's technology and business goals. With a focus on fostering collaboration and aligning strategies across engineering, finance, and legal teams, the group plays a crucial role in enabling Intel's success in a dynamic and competitive market.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and implement tier 2/3 strategies tailored to Intel's unique substrate needs and technology roadmaps.
  • Drive supplier development and foster collaborative relationships to ensure cost-effective and innovative supply chain solutions.
  • Conduct sourcing strategy reviews to manage market disruptions and ensure business continuity.
  • Influence technical design decisions, negotiate technical contract terms with suppliers, and shape aligned roadmaps.
  • Coordinate purchasing activities with cross-functional teams to acquire materials and services that meet technical specifications and cost requirements.
  • Lead sustainability initiatives and regulatory compliance efforts, ensuring supplier adherence to Intel's procurement policies.
  • Collaborate with engineering teams to define product requirements and optimize technology solutions.
  • Partner with finance and legal teams to resolve disputes and implement risk mitigation strategies.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in a relevant field such as Supply Chain Management, Business, Engineering, or related area.
  • Fluent in Japanese, and local to Intel's Tokyo office.
  • At least 9 years of experience in commodity management, sourcing strategy, supplier management, or related functions.
  • Proven expertise in contract negotiation and supplier relationship management.
  • Strong understanding of industry technology roadmaps, supply chain solutions, and risk mitigation strategies.
  • Demonstrated proficiency in capacity planning, supply-demand analysis, and commercial acumen.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's degree in a relevant field with at least 6 years of experience in commodity management or related areas.
  • Advanced knowledge of sustainable sourcing practices and regulatory compliance management.
