title: Construction Project Design Manager (Contract)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

This is an exceptionally exciting moment to enter the semiconductor manufacturing industry. Global demand for advanced computing - driven by AI, automation, cloud infrastructure, and digital transformation - is fueling the largest period of growth and reinvestment the sector has seen in decades. Semiconductors are now recognized as critical to economic resilience, national security, and technological leadership, leading to unprecedented expansion in manufacturing capacity and innovation. For professionals in the field, this translates to rare opportunities to shape breakthrough technologies, contribute to globally significant projects, and be part of arguably the most rapidly evolving and impactful industry ever.

Intel's Global Construction Engineering (GCE) organization is responsible for the design and engineering of Intel's major manufacturing and cleanroom facilities worldwide. Our organization consists of highly specialized, in-house architects and engineers working in a deeply collaborative environment. Together with our factory, operations, and supply chain partners, we deliver some of the most technically complex construction programs in the industry - projects that demand precision, speed, and disciplined cost management.

Our vision is to be the world leader in semiconductor foundry construction engineering, and we are expanding our team to support the acceleration of Intel Foundry's manufacturing roadmap. We are seeking exceptional technical talent to join our organization who will thrive in a fast-paced environment, enjoy working with leading-edge technology, and be motivated by opportunities to innovate and make meaningful business impact.

This is a hybrid Contract position in Penang, Malaysia.

As a Construction Project Design Manager - Global Construction Engineering, your responsibilities will include but are not limited to:
• Develop discipline scope and engineering solutions for construction projects.
• Interface and coordinate with contract design, construction, scheduling, and estimating resources.
• Interface with facilities staff and project managers, factory partners, particularly the Industrial Engineering team, to determine the optimal facility design scope and engineering solutions that support evolving factory requirements and business needs
• Define design criteria, lead scope definition and justification, develop design concepts, and oversee completion of positioning, programming, and detailed design.
• Lead and coordinate multidisciplinary design activities to ensure alignment with project objectives, schedule, budget, and constructability requirements.
• Work with estimators to ensure costs are captured and project budgets are met.
• Have strong knowledge of Intel's master specifications and standards, while utilizing established change processes to improve standards and drive innovative solutions.
• Collaborate and share learnings with counterparts at other sites across the globe.
• Build and drive a safety culture of caring in every business environment, from offices to construction sites, and from front-end planning through construction execution.
• Candidates with experience as a Design Manager on semiconductor manufacturing or advanced technology facility construction projects are highly encouraged to apply. Such experience may include leading architect-engineer (A/E) firms, managing design execution, coordinating multidisciplinary engineering teams, and driving design quality, cost, and schedule performance through project delivery.

The successful candidate should exhibit the following behavioural traits:
• Strong written, visual, and verbal communication skills for technical and business topics.
• Ability to communicate strategic and tactical concepts across a wide range of employees and management levels.
• Ability to influence and drive alignment in a highly matrixed, cross-functional environment.
• Strong collaboration skills across engineering disciplines, organizations, external architect-engineer (A/E) partners, and global teams.
• Strong orientation toward teamwork, customer service, and quality.
• Excellent organizational, planning, and workload management skills, with the ability to lead multiple projects of varying complexity.
• Strong problem-solving and decision-making capabilities, including the ability to resolve complex technical and project delivery challenges.
• Proficiency in reading, interpreting, and coordinating construction contract documents and engineering deliverables.
• Working knowledge of office productivity and computer applications.
• Commitment to continuous improvement, innovation, and the adoption of new technologies and best practices.
• High attention to detail, accountability, and ownership in delivering commitments.
• Commitment to championing and sustaining a strong safety culture throughout the project lifecycle.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Minimum Qualifications: • Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related technical field. • 5+ years of relevant industry experience in facilities engineering, project engineering, design engineering, or design management roles supporting semiconductor, advanced manufacturing, or similar industrial facility projects. Preferred Qualifications: • Master's degree in Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related technical field and 4+ years of relevant industry experience. • Experience as a Design Manager, Engineering Manager, or Lead Discipline Engineer supporting semiconductor facility design and construction projects. • Demonstrated experience managing external architect-engineer (A/E) firms and coordinating multidisciplinary design deliverables from concept through construction. • Familiarity with AutoCAD, P/IDs PipeFlo (for Mechanical and Chemical Engineering candidates), ETAP/SKM and power system studies (for Electrical Engineering candidates), and BIM. • For Mechanical and Chemical Engineering candidates, experience with utility and process systems commonly used in semiconductor or advanced manufacturing facilities, including HVAC, chilled water, process cooling water, exhaust, vacuum, compressed dry air, specialty gas, chemical distribution, wastewater treatment, and related safety systems. • Working knowledge of process hazard analysis (PHA), HAZOP reviews, pressure relief and piping system design principles, equipment specification and selection, and engineering codes and standards applicable to industrial facilities. • Basic knowledge of control methods for process systems and/or electrical power distribution systems. • Registration as a Professional Engineer • Experience with: - Construction, start-up, and commissioning/turnover of facility systems - Building and fire codes, hazardous occupancies, and related codes and standards to the field of expertise - Semiconductor manufacturing facilities, cleanrooms, and related infrastructure systems.

title: Product Failure Analysis Engineer - SCAN Design for Test
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

At Intel, we create world-changing technology that enriches the lives of every person on earth. As a global leader in semiconductor innovation, we design and manufacture the world's most advanced chips — powering everything from personal computers and smartphones to data centers, AI systems, and autonomous vehicles. Our Oregon campus is one of our most important engineering hubs in the world, home to thousands of brilliant engineers who are shaping the future of technology. We believe that diversity of thought, background, and experience makes us stronger — and we're committed to building a workplace where everyone can do their best work.

We are seeking an experienced Product Failure Analysis Engineer - SCAN Design for Test who is excited by the opportunity to help enable the success of Intel Foundry's leading-edge 18A technology. The ideal candidate brings 6-12 years of semiconductor experience with deep expertise in DFT, ATPG, scan diagnosis, and post-silicon debug, along with a proven track record of solving complex silicon issues in advanced process technologies.

In this role, you will play a critical part in accelerating the ramp and quality of Intel Foundry products by driving root-cause analysis of silicon failures, partnering across design, test, technology development, and manufacturing organizations to quickly identify and resolve product and process issues. Your technical leadership will directly contribute to improving product quality, yield, reliability, and time-to-market for next-generation foundry customers.

The successful candidate will have hands-on experience utilizing both logical diagnosis techniques (ATPG, scan diagnosis, fault isolation) and physical failure analysis methodologies (FIB, SEM, TEM, laser-based techniques, or equivalent) to isolate defects and determine corrective actions. Strong collaboration skills are essential, as you will work closely with DFT architects, design engineers, validation teams, process integration engineers, yield engineers, and high-volume manufacturing organizations.

Beyond issue resolution, we are looking for an engineer who can help shape the future of failure analysis and silicon debug by developing innovative methodologies, automation frameworks, and diagnostic capabilities that improve debug efficiency and accelerate root-cause identification across Intel Foundry's advanced technology portfolio..

Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead Failure Analysis: Utilize state-of-the-art lab equipment — including FIB tools, probe tools, and automated systems — to isolate microscopic silicon circuit failures and identify root causes with precision and speed.
  • Drive Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with test and validation engineers, circuit designers, wafer fabrication process engineers, and high-volume manufacturing teams to resolve quality issues, develop temporary mitigations, and implement permanent remedies.
  • Advance Debug Technologies: Develop new debug tools, methodologies, and technologies that push the boundaries of silicon debug, contributing to breakthrough innovations in semiconductor manufacturing.
  • Ensure Design for Debug: Evaluate and resolve component engineering and physical design issues, ensuring products incorporate the necessary design-for-debug features to enable deep silicon isolation capabilities.
  • Support Continuous Improvement: Provide expert input on failure analysis investigation areas and design process improvements, ensuring products consistently perform to specification.

As a Successful Candidate, You Will Bring:

  • A collaborative spirit — you thrive in cross-functional environments and build strong relationships across teams.
  • Intellectual curiosity — you love diving deep into complex problems and aren't satisfied until you've found the root cause.
  • Resilience and adaptability — you stay focused and effective even when working on the most challenging, ambiguous problems.
  • Clear communication — you can translate highly technical findings into clear, actionable insights for diverse audiences.
  • Ownership mentality — you take pride in your work and hold yourself accountable for delivering results.
  • Innovation mindset — you're always looking for better ways to do things and aren't afraid to challenge the status quo.

Ideal Background:

  • 6+ years of semiconductor industry experience in Product Engineering, Failure Analysis, Silicon Debug, DFT, Yield Engineering, or Post-Silicon Validation.
  • Deep expertise in DFT architectures, ATPG, scan diagnosis, and fault modeling.
  • Experience debugging complex silicon issues on leading-edge technology nodes.
  • Strong understanding of failure analysis workflows and physical debug techniques.
  • Demonstrated success driving cross-functional investigations from problem identification through corrective action.
  • Experience developing automation and debug methodologies that improve diagnosis accuracy and turnaround time.
  • Passion for advancing semiconductor technology and contributing to the successful deployment of Intel Foundry 18A products.

If you're passionate about silicon engineering and want to work on technology that matters, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today and take the next step in your career at Intel.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Experience would be obtained through a combination of prior education level classes, and current level school classes, projects, research and relevant previous job and/or internship experience.


Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or a related STEM discipline with 6+ years of hands-on experience, OR master's degree with 4+ years, OR PhD with 2+ years.
  • Hands – on experience with the following:
    • Expertise in Design for Test (DFT) tools and techniques, SCAN ATPG methodology, and Scan Chain Diagnosis.
    • In fault isolation techniques including ATPG pattern generation, fault modeling (stuck-at, transition, path delay, bridging), and Scan architecture (SSN).
    • Experience with Siemens Tessent, Synopsys TestMAX/TetraMAX, Verdi, DVE, simulation and diagnosis tools
    • Experience developing debug automation and analysis tools using Python, Perl, or TCL

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 6+ years of experience:
    • JTAG and validation/debug research methodologies.
    • Developing innovative debug tools and methodologies in a research-driven environment.
    • In foundry, fabless semiconductor, or high-volume manufacturing environments supporting customer product bring-up, yield ramp, or production qualification.

title: Senior Construction Manager - Site Logistics (Contract Position)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Organization

Join Intel Foundry Construction and Sourcing (FCS) as we deliver some of the world's largest and most advanced semiconductor manufacturing facilities. FCS manages a global portfolio of capital projects that includes new wafer fabrication facilities, fab expansions and conversions, process tool installations, infrastructure upgrades, and progressive-build programs. 


Our projects involve complex stakeholder environments and large contractor workforces consisting of general contractors, architecture and engineering firms, specialty trade partners, and equipment suppliers. Collectively, the portfolio represents billions of dollars in annual capital investment and plays a critical role in enabling Intel's growth and technology roadmap. 


Position Overview

The Senior Construction Manager - Site Logistics is a key leader within the Project Execution organization, responsible for planning, coordinating, and optimizing site-wide construction logistics, labor forecasting, workforce coordination, and operational readiness across multiple capital projects. 


Reporting to the Director of Construction, this role provides leadership and oversight for integrated site logistics activities supporting projects with contractor populations ranging from 100 to 1000 workers. The successful candidate will collaborate across project teams, construction managers, suppliers, operations organizations, and external stakeholders to ensure safe, efficient, and predictable project execution. 


This role serves as a central coordination point for site logistics strategy, trade labor planning, contractor integration, and construction operations while driving innovation, productivity improvements, and best-in-class safety performance. 


Location: Albuquerque, New Mexico (On-site) 


Key Responsibilities 


Site Logistics and Construction Operations 

  • Lead site-wide logistics planning and execution to support multiple concurrent construction and tool installation projects. 
  • Drive safe, efficient, and coordinated construction operations while minimizing operational disruptions. 
  • Develop and implement logistics strategies for workforce access, material flow, laydown areas, site services, transportation, and critical infrastructure coordination. 
  • Partner with construction and project management teams to optimize site utilization and project delivery performance. 

Labor Planning and Workforce Coordination 

  • Own trade labor forecasting, workforce planning, and contractor resource alignment across active projects. 
  • Develop and present labor forecasts and staffing plans to construction leadership, trade organizations, and labor stakeholders. 
  • Monitor trade headcount demand, workforce availability, and project labor requirements to ensure delivery commitments are met. 
  • Coordinate labor requirements across multi-prime, design-build, and general contractor delivery models. 

Program Integration and Stakeholder Management 

  • Serve as a key interface between Construction Management, Tool Install, Facilities Operations, Finance, Design, Procurement, and Supply Chain organizations. 
  • Lead site-wide indirect planning, coordination, tracking, and reporting activities. 
  • Drive alignment among project teams, suppliers, and stakeholders regarding logistics priorities, resource constraints, and schedule requirements. 
  • Facilitate executive-level discussions while maintaining detailed understanding of project execution needs. 

Contractor and Supplier Leadership 

  • Build and maintain strategic partnerships with contractors, suppliers, and service providers. 
  • Drive continuous improvement in contractor performance, safety, schedule reliability, productivity, and cost management. 
  • Identify and implement innovative construction methods, technologies, and operational practices that improve project outcomes. 

Process Excellence and Innovation 

  • Own and drive site logistics governance processes, planning frameworks, and reporting mechanisms. 
  • Champion Lean construction principles and operational excellence initiatives. 
  • Evaluate and implement innovative logistics, planning, and construction solutions to improve efficiency and scalability. 
  • Promote sustainability initiatives and support environmental and certification objectives where applicable. 

Safety and Culture 

  • Lead and reinforce Intel's Culture of Caring across all phases of project execution. 
  • Ensure compliance with safety requirements and foster a proactive safety culture among contractors and project teams.

title: Process Integration and Yield Technician
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

At Intel Foundry, we are driving the future of semiconductor manufacturing through advanced process technologies, innovation, and operational excellence. We are seeking a Process Integration and Yield Technician to support process optimization, defect reduction, yield improvement, and product reliability initiatives within our manufacturing environment. This role plays a critical part in identifying process issues, analyzing failures, conducting technical investigations, and collaborating with engineering teams to improve manufacturing performance and product quality.

The ideal candidate is highly analytical, detail-oriented, and passionate about solving complex technical problems in a fast-paced semiconductor manufacturing environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform physical, electrical, and technical analysis to identify defects contributing to yield loss, performance degradation, or reliability concerns.
  • Conduct failure analysis on semiconductor products and components to determine root causes of electrical or physical failures.
  • Perform electrical validation, fault isolation, and defect characterization on devices that fail manufacturing or reliability testing.
  • Utilize analytical tools and techniques, including Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), to image, inspect, and characterize defects.
  • Prepare and process samples for laboratory analysis and generate detailed reports summarizing findings and recommendations.
  • Document, analyze, and communicate technical results to engineers, technicians, operators, and management teams.
  • Execute engineering experiments, process evaluations, and test runs to support process integration and yield improvement initiatives.
  • Collect, analyze, and interpret inline defect, parametric, reliability, and end-of-line manufacturing data.
  • Create and maintain records, charts, graphs, and reports to identify trends, abnormalities, and opportunities for continuous improvement.
  • Support material disposition activities through database reporting, statistical analysis, and defect assessment.
  • Recommend process, equipment, or operational improvements to enhance product quality, yield, reliability, and manufacturing efficiency.
  • Set up, calibrate, maintain, and troubleshoot analytical and laboratory equipment.
  • Partner with process integration, manufacturing, quality, reliability, and engineering teams to implement corrective and preventive actions.
  • Ensure compliance with manufacturing standards, specifications, and quality procedures.
  • Demonstrate strong quality ownership by supporting Stop the Job (STJ) activities and driving rapid resolution of quality concerns.
  • Provide technical guidance, training, and mentoring to peers to strengthen overall team capability and knowledge sharing.

Behavioral Traits

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Detail-oriented with a commitment to quality and accuracy.
  • Work effectively in a highly collaborative team environment.
  • Demonstrates ownership, accountability, and a continuous improvement mindset.
  • Manage multiple priorities in a dynamic manufacturing environment.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Curious, proactive, and motivated to investigate complex technical issues.
  • Adaptable and comfortable working with ambiguity while driving solutions.
  • Passion for learning and applying new technologies and methodologies.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum qualifications and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. This position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship

Minimum Qualifications

  • Associate degree in Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, Semiconductor Manufacturing, or another STEM-related field and 4+ years of hands-on laboratory or manufacturing experience in a semiconductor, high-tech manufacturing, engineering, or related technical environment. OR Bachelor’s degree in Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, Semiconductor Manufacturing, or another STEM-related field and 2+ years of hands-on laboratory or manufacturing experience in a semiconductor, high-tech manufacturing, engineering, or related technical environment.
  • Candidate must be willing to:
    • Standing and walking for up to 80% of the workday.
    • Perform precision manual activities, including soldering small devices/components and conducting fine polishing tasks.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of experience working in a semiconductor manufacturing facility or lab facility.
  • 1+ years of experience in one or more of the following areas: acoustic imaging, x-rays inspection, electron spectroscopy and imaging (SEM/TEM/EDX), and sample prep techniques is highly desired.
  • Familiarity with laboratory techniques.

Explore this opportunity to grow your career and contribute to Intel's success by applying your skills to world-class innovation and quality.

title: Defect Characterization Low Yield Analysis Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

As a Low Yield Analysis (LYA) Engineer within Intel Foundry's Defect Characterization organization, you will drive root cause identification and yield improvement strategies for advanced packaging assembly and substrate technology development programs. You will lead complex technical investigations, develop innovative characterization methodologies, and collaborate across manufacturing, quality, process integration, design, and module technology development organizations to resolve critical yield challenges.


This role requires a strong sense of ownership, urgency, technical leadership, and customer focus. The successful candidate will independently drive investigations, influence technical decisions, mentor team members, and deliver measurable business impact through yield improvement and defect characterization excellence.

Responsibilities

  • Lead end-to-end investigations to identify and resolve complex yield, defect, and quality issues.
  • Serve as a technical owner for major factory, platform, or technology development programs.
  • Define characterization strategies, learning plans, and root cause methodologies for critical technical challenges.
  • Utilize advanced analytical techniques including Optical Microscopy, SEM/EDS, EBSD, CSAM, FTIR, Raman, FIB, ion milling, and mechanical cross-sectioning to identify failure mechanisms.
  • Correlate characterization results with electrical data, defect inspection data, process history, and manufacturing information to establish root cause.
  • Consolidate and analyze large data sets using statistical methods and coding tools to identify yield limiters and emerging trends.
  • Develop and implement tools, dashboards, automation, and analytical methodologies that improve learning velocity and analysis efficiency.
  • Drive corrective actions and influence process improvements across manufacturing, integration, quality, and technology organizations.
  • Lead cross-functional task forces and technical reviews to address high-priority yield and reliability issues.
  • Present technical findings, recommendations, and risk assessments to engineering and management teams.
  • Mentor engineers and technicians while promoting best-known methods and organizational learning.
  • Support future capability development through equipment strategy, methodology development, and characterization roadmap planning.
  • Effectively manage multiple high-priority investigations while balancing customer commitments, factory priorities, and business needs.

Behavioral traits

  • Demonstrated success managing multiple competing priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing or development environment.
  • Communicate findings verbally and through reports to yield engineers, LYA analysts, and other customers.
  • Work in a collaborative manner with a variety of different individuals in a fast paced, technical environment.
  • Experience independently driving technical investigations and root cause analysis activities.
  • Independently own open-ended technical problems, proactively drive actions across organizations, and deliver measurable business impact through root cause identification and implementation of corrective actions.
  • Problem-solving, analytical, and troubleshooting skills.
  • Verbal and written communication skills to communicate technical findings to diverse audiences.

title: Reliability Lab Shock and Vibration Testing Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Stress Test and Reliability Laboratory organization is looking for a dynamic, hands-on engineer to join their environmental stress tool engineering team in Chandler, AZ. The lab engineering team develops and maintains a fleet of equipment which is used to evaluate Intel's silicon, package, and assembly technologies under simulated field use including heat, humidity, temperature change, and dynamic stresses such as shock and vibration.

This role will focus on supporting our dynamics stress capability. In this role, you will be responsible for developing, executing, and analyzing mechanical reliability and environmental stress testing programs for semiconductor devices, boards, and assemblies. The role requires expertise in shock, vibration, and dynamic mechanical loading methodologies with a strong emphasis on industry-standard test requirements and a deep knowledge of the physics of failure.


Responsibilities will include but are not limited to:

  • Develop, plan, and execute dynamic stress tests, including shock, vibration, and other test methods in compliance with JEDEC, IPC, and/or customer requirements
  • Develop test fixtures, instrumentation strategies, and data acquisition systems to support mechanical reliability evaluations.
  • Working with the operations team, perform testing on devices
  • Analyze test data using statistical and engineering methods to identify failure modes, performance limits, and reliability risks.
  • Correlate test data to mechanical models to validate and improve simulation results
  • Generate detailed test plans, procedures, reports, and qualification documentation.
  • Drive continuous improvement of laboratory capabilities, test automation, and best practices for dynamic stress testing.
  • Ensure laboratory operations comply with applicable safety, quality, and calibration requirements.
  • Provide technical guidance regarding shock and vibration requirements throughout the product development lifecycle.

Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.  Requirements listed would be obtained through a combination of industry relevant job experience, internship experiences and or schoolwork/classes/research. 


Minimum Requirements

Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Materials Engineering, or similar STEM related degree:

  • BS with 4+ years of experience in shock and vibration stress testing/methods
  • -OR- MS with 1+ years of experience in shock and vibration stress testing/methods
  • - OR- PhD with 6 months+ of experience in shock and vibration stress testing/methods

Experience can come from a combination of educational and work experience and may include:

  • Hands-on experience conducting shock and vibration testing using electrodynamic shakers and mechanical shock equipment.
  • Working knowledge of JEDEC and/or IPC standards related to board-level reliability and mechanical stress testing.
  • Experience developing test plans, procedures, and qualification reports.
  • Proficiency with data acquisition systems, accelerometers, strain gauges, and vibration control software.
  • Experience analyzing vibration and shock response data and interpreting failure mechanisms.
  • Understanding of finite element analysis (FEA) results and correlation to physical testing.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Deep expertise with JEDEC standards such as JESD22-B103, JESD22-B110, JESD22-B111, and other relevant mechanical reliability requirements.
  • Experience interpreting and applying IPC standards including IPC-9703 and related solder joint reliability specifications.
  • Familiarity with military, aerospace, or transportation standards such as MIL-STD-810, ASTM, and IEC environmental test methods
  • Advanced knowledge of vibration analysis, modal analysis, frequency response functions (FRFs), and resonance characterization.
  • Proficiency with FEA tools such as Comsol Multiphysics, ANSYS, Abaqus, or Nastran.
  • Experience with standard and high-speed data acquisition systems (including DMM) and automated test scripting using Python, MATLAB, or LabVIEW.
  • Laboratory leadership experience, including test equipment specification, procurement, calibration management, and mentoring junior engineers.
  • Proficiency in electrical measurements, calibration, and troubleshooting programmable DC power supplies, multimeters, and other instrumentation.
  • Experience with data acquisition systems, instrumentation communication protocols (e.g., Ethernet, RS-232, GPIB), and automated test equipment.
  • Knowledge of design of experiments, statistical process control, and measurement system analysis.
  • Strong troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively in cross-functional engineering environments.

Your expertise and enthusiasm for engineering excellence can help shape the future of semiconductor innovation. Join our team and contribute to groundbreaking technological advancements by applying today.

title: E-Core CPU Design Automation Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

E-core (formerly known as ATOM), Intel's most efficient CPU Technology team is looking for a highly motivated and technically savvy experienced individual to join our team as Design Automation Engineer. Intel has a vision to create and extend computing technology to connect and enrich the lives of every person. We are designing future generations of high-performance E-core CPUs using the most advanced and innovative process technologies. If you are looking to grow and develop your skillsets while being surrounded by highly motivated and knowledgeable teammates, then this is the organization for you.


E-Core CPUs are the industry-leading performance-per-watt CPU that helps:

  • Power the latest Intel laptops, desktops, and high-end gaming platforms.
  • Drive 5G communications by serving as the base station that delivers essential data from your electronic devices across the world at maximum bandwidth.
  • Create Artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning devices.
  • Enable a full virtual learning experience for students using the latest Google Chromebooks.

As a CPU Physical Design Automation Engineer in the E-core CPU group, you will be responsible for:

  • Developing, debugging, and supporting tools, flows, and methodologies covering backend physical design methodologies and flow automation for high-performance blocks and full chip level using RTL2GDS standard cell level design techniques.
  • Performing analysis of either synthesis, place and route, floor planning or signoff for static timing analysis on timing paths, formal equivalence verification, power consumption, electrical rule checking, and circuit reliability to identify key issues.
  • Working closely with design teams to understand and debug tool issues and constraints.
  • Working with industry EDA vendors to build and enhance tool capabilities to design a high-speed, low-power synthesizable CPU.
  • Creating documentation and helping with guidelines/specs.
  • Communicating with other team members to solve problems and following solutions through to completion. Excellent verbal and written English communication skills.
  • Leverage AI capabilities to enhance daily operational efficiency and design productivity.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Engineering and/or Electrical/Electronic Engineering and 1+ years of relevant working experience OR Master's Degree in Computer Engineering and/or Electrical/Electronic Engineering

  • Fresh Graduate is welcome to apply.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 1+ years of experience in VLSI, design automation algorithms, and transistor-level design.

  • 1+ years of experience using industry standard Engineering Design Automation (EDA) VLSI tools/flows from vendors such as Synopsys, Cadence and/or Mentor Graphics for performing synthesis, place-and-route, extraction, timing/power analysis and functional verification.

  • 1+ years' experience with Python, Perl, and/or Tcl scripting languages.

  • Experience with timing closure methodology for worst-case corner (static timing analysis / STA, statistical variation analysis, spice circuit simulation, ERC, noise analysis flows, cross talk, OCV effects, budget constraints)

title: Senior CPU Circuit Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
As a Senior CPU Circuit Design Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in designing and developing custom digital circuits for CPUs, including memory. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams to optimize power, performance, area, timing, and yield goals, while ensuring the functionality and reliability of CPU circuits. Your expertise will directly contribute to the creation of cutting-edge processors that shape Intel's technological leadership.


Business Group
The Silicon and Platform Engineering Group (SPE) drives Intel's innovation in silicon technologies, enabling advancements in CPU performance, power efficiency, and scalability. As part of this group, you will join a collaborative team dedicated to developing world-class CPUs that address the needs of diverse computing markets and support Intel's broader mission of technological excellence.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Design custom digital circuits for CPU blocks, including memory, with a focus on optimizing power, performance, area, timing, and yield.

  • Conduct comprehensive design verification using industry-standard methodologies, including timing analysis, noise analysis, and layout rule checks.

  • Characterize memory instances and memory compilers, driving improvements in performance, power efficiency, and area reduction.

  • Proficiency with industry-standard EDA tools for circuit design and verification.
  • Experience in circuit simulation, timing analysis, noise analysis, and reliability evaluations.
  • Strong understanding of advanced CMOS technology and physical layout techniques.
  • Solid understanding of power optimization, timing analysis, and design for manufacturability principles.

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
As a Substrate Capacity Manager, you will lead strategic supplier capacity growth initiatives that are critical to Intel's ability to scale next-generation semiconductor technologies. This role combines project management, supplier engagement, and capacity planning expertise to ensure substrate supply readiness for both development and high-volume manufacturing.

You will drive complex, multi-year capacity expansion programs across a global supplier network, coordinating technical, operational, and commercial workstreams to deliver capacity on time and at scale. By aligning supplier investments, manufacturing roadmaps, and business demand forecasts, you will help secure the infrastructure required to support Intel's future growth and technology leadership.

Your success will directly influence Intel's ability to accelerate product ramps, mitigate supply risks, and enable long-term manufacturing scalability.

Business group
This position is part of Intel Foundry, a dynamic and innovative group that focuses on enabling Intel's technology leadership through robust manufacturing capabilities and supply chain excellence. The team is committed to ensuring a resilient and efficient flow of critical materials and services, supporting Intel's broader mission of delivering world-class products and solutions.


Key Responsibilities

  • Lead end-to-end supplier capacity expansion programs, managing scope, schedules, milestones, risks, and dependencies to ensure capacity is delivered in alignment with Intel's technology and production roadmaps.
  • Drive cross-functional execution of capacity growth initiatives by partnering with engineering, operations, planning, finance, and supplier teams to remove barriers and meet aggressive deployment timelines.

descriptionHtml:

Job Description:

This position is in the Logic Technology Development (LTD) team, working in one of the most advanced semiconductor development facilities in the world.

The LTD Resolution Enhancement Technology (RET) team is extending the limits of feature sizes that are patternable on Intel's devices, using current and future lithography manufacturing tooling. The team works closely with fab integrated lithography process and mask manufacturing teams using computational lithography tooling to optimize mask patterns and maximize manufacturing process capability. The RET team also works closely with the design rule definition teams, using lithography and patterning simulation capabilities to determine design rules for future Intel process nodes.

Intel is seeking a collaborative and community-focused professional to help strengthen relationships with the public and private sector in Ohio, with a primary focus on the Columbus, New Albany, Johnstown, and Licking County region. The Government and Public Affairs, Community Engagement Manager will support Intel's efforts to advance education, workforce development, economic opportunity, and community impact through strategic engagement with schools, nonprofits, civic organizations, neighbors, and other community stakeholders.

title: Senior Verification Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact 

You will be part of a highly skilled, agile design/verification team developing cutting-edge hardware for the NIC, IPU and AI domains. 

As a senior IP Design Verification Engineer, you will play a crucial role in ensuring the functionality and reliability of complex designs. You will technically lead teams in developing verification plans, creating test benches, and building environments to thoroughly validate meaningful parts of the chip — complex IPs and subsystems. 

Your work will directly contribute to identifying and resolving bugs in the pre-silicon environment using simulation and/or Formal Property Verification techniques, ensuring robust designs that meet high-performance standards. 

We are intentional, fast adopters of AI as a working tool. We bring modern AI assistants and automation into every part of the verification flow — planning, stimulus and checker development, coverage analysis, debug and more. 

 
 
Business group  
You will be joining Intel's Central Engineering Group (CEG), a global organization responsible for designing and verifying industry-leading IPs and architectures that power Intel's NIC, IPU and ASIC products. The group produces innovative technologies and solutions for hyperscalers, cloud providers, networking, AI and other specialized workloads. 

As part of this dynamic team, you will contribute to Intel's commitment to advancing silicon and system innovation.  
 
Key Responsibilities 

  • Own verification planning and execution for key IP features across IP and subsystem integration points 
  • Build scalable verification environments and targeted test plans with reusable test benches, checkers, VIPs, and behavioral models 
  • Collaborate closely with architecture, design, and software teams from specification through bringup; contribute across role boundaries when needed to unblock progress and maintain execution quality 
  • Drive ownership of multiple critical blocks and verification components; take full responsibility for functional signoffs and achievement of performance and power metrics 
  • Lead IP delivery to multiple customers while ensuring technical excellence; balance competing requirements, schedules, and resources across teams 
  • Drive convergence of simulation and formal verification into unified bug hunting and coverage closure strategies; evaluate and adopt emerging methodologies including ML-driven verification flows 
  • Mentor and develop verification engineers; establish verification best practices and raise team-level execution quality 
  • Comfortable using AI-assisted development tools as part of everyday workflow; track record of delivering reusable, configurable verification collateral 

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications  

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related field.  
  • 10+ years of experience in functional design verification of ASIC, SOC or FPGA designs with expertise in System Verilog, OVM/UVM, and debugging tools.  
  • Proficiency in creating IP test environments and/or using formal verification methods 
  • Strong knowledge of digital design fundamentals and microarchitecture principles.  

Preferred Qualifications  

  • Master's or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related field with relevant experience in design verification.  
  • Experience with formal property verification, System Verilog Assertions, code and functional coverage implementation and analysis 
  • Experience collaborating across teams to drive architectural improvements.  
  • Use of AI tools would be an advantage. At a minimum, require someone that is passionate about performing Pre-Silicon DV harnessing the power of AI. 
  • Experience with switching/routing and communications protocols such as Ethernet, and Cryptographic Protocols such IPSec, DTLS and MACSec. 
  • Experience with AMBA protocols such as APB and AXI. 
  • Experience with languages such as SystemC, Python, Perl, Shell scripting and how AI can be used to integrate these in verification flows. 

We invite you to bring your leadership, expertise and enthusiasm to a team where your contributions will drive technological progress and create opportunities for impactful learning and growth.

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About Intel's Central Engineering Group

Intel's Central Engineering Group (CEG) focuses on enhancing engineering execution and expanding market opportunities through internal product development and external ASIC design services. Join a team dedicated to revolutionizing engineering methodologies and supporting Intel's industry leadership.

Position Overview

As an IP Design Verification Engineer, you will play a crucial role in ensuring the functional accuracy and reliability of clock generator IPs, such as PLL and FLL, within Intel's innovative product development lifecycle. You will actively develop verification environments, implement tests, and debug pre-silicon issues to meet rigorous specification requirements.

Your contributions will directly impact the seamless integration of IPs into Intel's cutting-edge designs and ensure the highest standards of quality and performance.

  • Perform functional verification for clock generator IPs such as PLL and FLL, ensuring conformance to microarchitecture specifications

  • Document test plans and participate in technical reviews with design teams

title: CPU Power Management and Performance Architect
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel is shaping the future of technology to help create a better future for the entire world. Our work in pushing forward fields like AI, analytics, and cloud-to-edge technology is at the heart of countless innovations. With a career at Intel, you'll have the opportunity to use technology to power major breakthroughs and create enhancements that improve our everyday quality of life. Join us and help make the future more wonderful for everyone. Want to learn more? Visit our YouTube Channel or the link below.


Life at Intel

We are seeking an experienced SoC CPU power-management professional to define and drive the power-management architecture for next-generation mobile and desktop client processors. In this role, you will own end-to-end CPU power and performance requirements within the broader SoC, define differentiated architectural features and control mechanisms, and guide their implementation from early product definition through post-silicon validation. You will work closely with CPU microarchitecture, SoC integration, silicon design, firmware, operating system, validation, thermal, and product teams to deliver industry-leading performance, energy efficiency, and user experiences.


Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Own the power-management and performance architecture for mobile and desktop CPUs as part of the CPU architecture team. Define architectural capabilities, develop innovative techniques, guide implementation, and drive energy efficiency across operating conditions and product segments.
  • Define and analyze CPU power and performance requirements, budgets, and interfaces within the SoC, working across CPU cores, shared caches, interconnects, memory, accelerators, and platform IP.
  • Create and maintain workload-based CPU and SoC power and performance models and targets; correlate predictions with pre- and post-silicon data; and apply the results to improve current implementations and future architectures across idle, sustained, burst, and peak workloads.
  • Partner with firmware and operating system teams to define end-to-end CPU and platform power-management capabilities, including DVFS policies, clock and power gating, idle-state management, telemetry, residency, latency, and quality-of-service tradeoffs.
  • Influence CPU microarchitecture and SoC fabric, memory, and I/O architecture to optimize power efficiency, performance, throughput, latency, and quality of service under representative real-world workloads.
  • Lead cross-functional architecture and design reviews, drive tradeoff decisions across power, performance, area, cost, thermals, and product experience, and align CPU, SoC integration, validation, firmware, operating system, and product teams.
  • Translate product usage models and competitive insights into clear architectural requirements, feature specifications, and measurable success criteria; track execution and communicate risks, decisions, and progress to technical and product leadership.
  • The architect role may involve technical and managerial leadership of a team or group.

A successful candidate will also demonstrate:

  • System-level thinking and the ability to connect detailed design decisions to CPU, SoC, and product-level outcomes.
  • Strong analytical problem-solving skills, with an emphasis on innovation, feasibility assessment, and disciplined exploration of architectural tradeoffs.
  • Technical leadership and communication skills to influence CPU architecture, SoC design, firmware, validation, and product roadmaps across organizational boundaries.
  • Curiosity, initiative, and a willingness to expand deep technical expertise into broader architecture ownership while advancing energy-efficient computing.

Qualifications:

The minimum qualifications below are required for consideration. Preferred qualifications are additional attributes that may help candidates succeed in the role. Relevant experience may be gained through architecture, design, modeling, validation, firmware, or other closely related engineering roles.


What We Need to See (Minimum Qualifications):

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field with 6+ years of relevant experience; master’s degree with 4+ years; or PhD with 2+ years. The specialized experience described below may be included within this overall experience.
  • Within that experience, 4+ years in SoC or IP architecture, CPU or SoC design, microarchitecture, power and performance engineering, or a closely related technical field.

How to Stand Out (Preferred Qualifications):

  • Extensive experience in CPU or SoC design, microarchitecture, architecture, or power and performance engineering; candidates with deep design expertise and demonstrated system-level leadership who are ready to grow into an architecture role are encouraged to apply. 
  • Proven experience designing, integrating, or architecting compute SoCs, CPUs, or complex silicon IP, with an understanding of how local design decisions affect system-level power, performance, and product behavior.
  • Knowledge of CPU or SoC power-management concepts such as DVFS, clock and power gating, idle states, telemetry, thermal constraints, or firmware and operating system interactions; direct ownership in all areas is not required.
  • Advanced knowledge of computer architecture, CPU microarchitecture, system-level design, and the interactions among cores, caches, interconnects, memory, accelerators, and platform IP.
  • Experience with performance or power modeling, benchmarking, workload analysis, functional modeling, statistical analysis, or correlation of model predictions with silicon measurements.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead technical tradeoffs, communicate across design, architecture, firmware, validation, and product teams, and expand from detailed design ownership to broader architectural decision-making.

Bring your technical depth, system-level perspective, and passion for energy-efficient computing to Intel. Join us in developing CPU power-management innovations that shape the performance, efficiency, and user experience of future client products.

title: Packaging Module Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Surface Mount Technology Development (SMTD), part of Intel's Assembly Technology Development (ATD) packaging team, cater to Intel's customer product assembly needs and certify Surface Mount Technology (SMT) manufacturing for new Central Processing Unit (CPU), Chipset, System on Chip (SoC) BGA packages, and Socket Technology. The Surface Mount Technology Development Lab in Kulim, Malaysia, offers SMT manufacturing, provides expertise in technology development, enabling next-generation product roadmaps through innovative solutions in circuit board technology, assembly processes, and materials.


In this role, you will be a Packaging Module Development Engineer focuses on process, equipment, materials technology development for SMT processes and Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs). Your responsibilities will include developing SMT process solutions and recommendations for Intel's integrated circuit (IC) packages and Sockets, as well as advancing new technologies to support Intel's SMT and PCB roadmap.

What you will do:

As a Packaging Module Development Engineer, you will be tasked with developing and validating board assembly process solutions to meet Intel's next-generation product requirements.


Your responsibilities will include creating SMT process solutions for Intel IC packages and sockets, identifying and addressing root causes of defects in SMT process development, and publishing Critical to Function (CTF) parameter recommendations and manufacturability guidelines for Intel's customers to adopt.


You will also be responsible for SMT Process Development. Design and optimize SMT processes, including stencil design, solder paste selection, reflow profiling, and inspection criteria to ensure high yield and reliability.

  • Materials Characterization: Evaluate and select materials such as solder pastes, fluxes, underfills, and adhesives to enhance assembly performance and reliability.
  • Process Integration: Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate new SMT processes into existing manufacturing lines, ensuring compatibility and scalability. Influence IC package and PCB design based on a deeper understanding of SMT, and manufacturing processes in internal and external strategic forums.
  • Failure Analysis: Conduct root cause analysis of assembly defects and implement corrective actions to improve process robustness.
  • Technology Roadmap: Contribute to the development of technology roadmaps for SMT and PCB advancements, focusing on miniaturization, higher interconnect densities, and improved thermal and electrical performance.
  • Prototype Testing: Oversee the assembly and testing of prototype boards, utilizing advanced equipment such as X-ray inspection and automated optical inspection (AOI).
  • Data Analysis: Utilize statistical tools and software to analyse process data, identify trends, and drive continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Documentation and Training: Develop detailed process documentation and provide training technicians to ensure consistent implementation of new technologies.

Qualifications:

  • Possess a Bachelor's degree with 3+ years of experience or Master's degree with 3+ years of experience or Ph.D. degree with 2+ years of experience in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering or Physics or related STEM fields.
  • Experiences required are Semiconductor integrated circuit (IC) assembly OR Printed Circuit Board Assembly (PCBA SMT) in process and equipment related such as reflow, pick and place, dispensing of paste, adhesive with good understanding of material interaction with assembly processes or use condition.
  • Proficiency in statistical tools and methods (e.g., SPC, DOE) for process optimization.


The candidate should exhibit the following behavioral traits and/or skills:

  • Discipline, Experimenters.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across teams.
  • A proactive approach to problem-solving and the ability to excel under tight timelines and schedules.

We invite you to become part of a dynamic team that values innovation, collaboration, and the pursuit of excellence. Your expertise will drive transformative advancements in technology, ensuring Intel continues to lead in delivering exceptional products that shape the future of the semiconductor industry.

Job Description: 

Join Intel and build a better tomorrow as an Intel Contract Employee. Our vision is to extend computing technology to connect and enrich the lives of every person on Earth. At Intel New Mexico, the Wafer Packaging Manufacturing (WPM) Singulation organization plays a critical role in semiconductor wafer processing, testing, and die to wafer assembly.
Beyond traditional product types, Singulation drives Intel's advanced packaging strategy, enabling large scale AI computing and next generation technologies. Working in Singulation offers the opportunity to contribute directly to manufacturing excellence in a collaborative, supportive, and fast paced environment where innovation and continuous improvement are valued.


Job Responsibilities:

The Singulation Module Equipment Technician is responsible for maintaining, troubleshooting, and improving manufacturing equipment performance. Key responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Perform electrical and mechanical troubleshooting to diagnose issues with non functioning manufacturing equipment.

  • Dismantle, adjust, repair, install, and assemble equipment using layout plans, blueprints, operating manuals, and technical documentation.

title: Chassis IP Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
As an IP Logic Design Engineer, you will be instrumental in developing and optimizing logic designs for high-performance IP blocks that drive Intel's cutting-edge SoC solutions. Your day-to-day responsibilities will include writing register transfer level (RTL) code, conducting simulations, and ensuring designs meet stringent power, performance, area, and timing goals. You'll play a pivotal role in delivering quality IPs while collaborating across architecture, verification, and SoC integration teams to ensure seamless handoffs and impactful results.

Business group
The Central Engineering Group (CEG) is Intel's leading innovation hub, focused on designing foundational technologies for integration across Intel's product portfolio. Within this team, the UIC Fabric Design organization specializes in developing reusable IP blocks and subsystems that enhance system-level capabilities. This group contributes to Intel's broader mission of delivering world-class solutions to revolutionize computing across industries.

Key Responsibilities
- Design and develop RTL code for IP blocks, ensuring functionality, quality, and scalability.
- Optimize logic designs to meet power, performance, area, and timing objectives.
- Collaborate with architecture teams to define microarchitecture features of IP designs.
- Participate in verification plan reviews and implement corrective measures for failing RTL tests.
- Support SoC integration teams to ensure high-quality integration and verification of IP blocks.
- Work with physical design teams to address timing and implementation challenges.
- Drive compliance with quality assurance standards for seamless IP-SoC handoff.

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field with 4+ years of experience in state-of-the-art SoC or IP design OR Master's degree with 3+ years of experience.
- Proficiency in Verilog/System Verilog, including Lint/CDC/RDC tools and methodologies.
- Demonstrated ability to optimize designs for power, performance, and area trade-offs (PPA).

- Familiarity with AMBA (CHI, AXI, AHB, APB) and PCIe/CXL protocols.
- Experience in designing IP subsystems, including protocol conversion bridges and debug/trace components.

- Proven ability to collaborate across architecture, verification, and SoC integration teams effectively.
- Familiarity with using AI tools to assist logic design.
- Strong communication skills and experience working with globally distributed teams across time zones.

title: AI Frameworks Engineer - Intern
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact


Intel is building the open software stack that makes large language models run fast on Intel GPUs. As an intern, you will join the engineering team that develops and optimizes LLM inference frameworks. You will work in vLLM and in the GPU kernel libraries beneath it with experienced engineers who will review your code and mentor you. This is a hands-on engineering internship, not a side project. You will write and test kernels, measure where performance goes, and see your changes land in open-source projects used across the AI industry.

Our internships usually last 12-24 months, and you will work with us part-time alongside your university degree. All applicants must be current university students and must remain students for the length of the internship. Candidates must be based in Poland on the internship start date and for its full duration.

Key Responsibilities


- Develop and optimize AI framework software for LLM inference on Intel GPUs, under the guidance of senior engineers, with contributions going upstream to open-source projects such as vLLM.
- Implement, port, and tune compute kernels (e.g., Triton, SYCL) for core transformer building blocks such as attention, sampling, normalization, mixture-of-experts, and quantization.
- Run benchmarks and profile inference workloads to find performance bottlenecks, measure them, and report findings to the team.
- Write and extend unit tests, correctness checks, and performance regression tests so that framework and kernel code stays reliable as upstream moves.
- Investigate and debug failures across the stack, from Python framework code down to kernel behaviour on the hardware.
- Collaborate with framework, compiler, and kernel engineers across global teams, and take part in code review and technical discussion with the open-source community.

Minimum Qualifications


No professional experience is required.

- Currently pursuing a BS or MS degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, AI, Mathematics, Physics, or a related field. Student status is required for the whole internship, preferably for the next two years and for at least 12 months.
- Good Python programming skills.
- Understanding of deep learning and neural networks, including the basics of transformer architecture and LLM inference. 
- Familiarity with Linux environments from a user perspective.
- Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving skills.
- Eagerness to learn, an open mind, and the ability to work in a team.

title: Compiler Engineering Intern
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Join Us in Shaping the Future


At Intel, we are building the next generation of software technologies that unlock the potential of heterogeneous computing. Our compiler technologies help developers harness CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators through high-performance, portable software.


As an intern, you will contribute to an open ecosystem that advances performance, scalability, reliability, and developer productivity for AI, HPC, and other demanding workloads, while supporting Intel's commitment to contributing to and collaborating with open-source communities.


The Team


The Intel Compiler Engineering Team develops LLVM-based C, C++, SYCL, Triton, MLIR, Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), and Fortran compiler technologies for Intel processor platforms, including CPUs and GPUs. The team works across the compiler stack and in close collaboration with hardware architecture teams, covering language front ends, intermediate representations, optimization, code generation, debug information, runtimes, offload support, quality, and developer tooling. This work connects Intel hardware and compiler capabilities with AI frameworks and software ecosystems such as PyTorch, inference engines, and machine-learning models. You will collaborate with experienced engineers and contribute to open-source communities while learning how production compilers are designed, tested, optimized, and delivered.


Position Overview


We are hiring a Compiler Engineer Intern to contribute to Intel's compiler software stack.


You will work with experienced compiler and hardware architecture engineers on a scoped project that may involve compiler features, MLIR-based intermediate representations, Triton or other Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), optimization, code generation, runtime or offload support, debug information, testing infrastructure, performance analysis, or developer tools.


Projects may involve connecting software capabilities to AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning model ecosystems such as DeepSeek, Hugging Face, and Qimi. You will investigate technical problems, implement and test solutions, analyze results, and communicate findings to the team. This opportunity is designed for an undergraduate student who wants to build practical compiler-engineering experience and apply foundational computer science concepts to production software.


Responsibilities


• Contribute to the design, implementation, testing, or analysis of compiler and runtime technologies.
• Develop and debug software in C or C++ within a large, collaborative codebase.
• Create or improve tests, reproduce defects, analyze failures, and help deliver reliable solutions.
• Evaluate functional correctness, compile-time behavior, runtime performance, or code quality, as applicable to the project.
• Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, and project planning with mentors and team members.
• Document designs, experiments, results, and lessons learned, and present project outcomes to the team.
• Contribute to open-source projects when aligned with the assigned work.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications


• Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or a Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Informatics, or a related technical discipline (able to maintain student status for at least 1 year).
• Coursework or project experience in data structures, algorithms, computer architecture, operating systems, programming languages, or compiler construction.
• Experience programming in C or C++ through coursework, research, personal projects, or prior internships.
• Experience using software development and debugging tools in a Linux or similar development environment.


Preferred Qualifications


• Compiler-related coursework or project experience, including parsing, intermediate representations, optimization, code generation, or runtimes.
• Familiarity with LLVM, MLIR, Clang, Flang, SYCL/DPC++, Triton, OpenMP, CUDA, or another compiler or parallel-programming ecosystem.
• Knowledge of CPU or GPU architecture, heterogeneous computing, or systems programming.
• Familiarity with AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning model ecosystems such as DeepSeek, Hugging Face, and Qimi.
• Tile-base programming model knowledge
• GPU Compute kernel writing experience
• Experience with Git, automated testing, continuous integration, performance analysis, or open-source development.
• Technical contributions such as code, patches, reviews, research, publications, or substantial academic projects.


Success in This Role


• Curiosity and willingness to learn unfamiliar technologies.
• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and debugging skills.
• Clear written and verbal communication.
• Ability to work independently on scoped tasks while seeking guidance when needed.
• Collaborative mindset and commitment to high-quality engineering.


Bring your passion, curiosity, and your engineering drive to Intel, and help shape how the next generation of AI workloads runs on Intel hardware.

title: Intel Foundry Principal Engineer Overlay Development Engineer - Lithography
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Team

Logic Technology Development (LTD) is Intel Foundry's advanced technology engine, responsible for inventing, developing, and industrializing the process technologies that power future semiconductor products. From breakthrough device architectures and materials innovation to production-ready manufacturing solutions, LTD transforms research into customer-ready technologies that enable industry-leading performance at scale.

About the Role

The Lithography Overlay Principal Engineer is responsible for overlay control innovation, defining key technology roadmaps, and leading complex technical projects to establish Intel's overlay leadership.

As a lithography overlay expert and technologist, you will be responsible for customization and addition of new features to base technologies to use in high volume manufacturing. Your expertise will focus on all aspects of improving overlay control.

Responsibilities:
LTD Principal Engineers are responsible for leading scientific research enabling the manufacture of innovative device architectures but not limited to:

  • Lead scientific research enabling the manufacture of innovative device architectures coupled with the realization of these architectures.
  • Designing, executing, and analyzing experiments necessary to meet engineering specifications for their process.

title: E-core CPU Physical Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

We created the Intel Atom Processor (E-Core), a disruptive technology that enables a broad range of devices including entry PC's, smartphones, modems, 2 in 1 laptops, micro-servers, and other Internet-of-Things IoT devices. You will be part of a team, participating in the design of a future generation high performance Intel Atom microprocessor.


This role requires an engineer with strong analytic and problem solving skill, an ability to communicate well, and willing to share and discuss issues. You will work on implementation of CPU Core blocks from synthesis through post-layout verification and tapeout. You will develop the custom constraints for driving synthesis and Auto-Place and Route APR tools to implement and optimize the design to meet aggressive timing and power goals. You will work closely with micro-architecture, RTL, and custom circuit teams to converge the design to project targets.

The responsibilities will be tailored to the candidate's skills and expertise and will include several of the following, but not be limited to:

  • Logic synthesis and place and route for CORE IP blocks.
  • Performing floor-planning and routing studies and implementation
    Block/sub-system level timing analysis.
  • Work on low power techniques and power reduction in sub-system.
  • Physical verification closure of block/sub-system.
  • Scripts writing for data analysis and recipe creation.
  • Strong analytical ability, problem solving and communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently and at various levels of abstraction.
  • Strong communication and team work skills.
  • Capable of working in a high performing team to deliver the results required from the organization.
  • Ability to work well in at team and be productive under aggressive schedules.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

Minimum qualifications:
Must have either BS or MS in Electrical Engineering or Computer Engineering.

Minimum 6 year of experience in:

  • CPU physical design and timing verification.
  • Synthesis/APR flows on multi voltage high frequency designs including custom polygon editing.
  • Tcl scripting.
  • Noise, cross-talk, OCV analysis.
  • Floorplanning and physical design and timing closure.
  • Formal equivalence, DRC/LVS, IR and electro-migration checks.

  • 7+ years of experience with the above skill sets.

title: CPU Physical Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel is shaping the future of technology to help create a better future for the entire world. Our work in pushing forward fields like AI, analytics, and cloud-to-edge technology is at the heart of countless innovations. With a career at Intel, you'll have the opportunity to use technology to power major breakthroughs and create enhancements that improve our everyday quality of life. Join us and help make the future more wonderful for everyone.

Life at Intel


As a member of Intel's CPU development team, you will have a front seat in designing the latest core IP to power cutting edge compute processors across client, server, IOTG and AI. We innovate state of the art microprocessor architecture on the most advanced and latest process technologies with a focus on power efficiency. Our core designs are present in nearly all segments of Intel's compute roadmap.

Job responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Performs physical design implementation of custom CPU designs from RTL to GDS to create a design database that is ready for manufacturing.
  • Conducts all aspects of the CPU physical design flow including synthesis, place and route, clock tree synthesis, floor planning, static timing analysis, power/clock distribution, reliability, and power and noise analysis.
  • Conducts verification and signoff including formal equivalence verification, static timing analysis, reliability verification, static and dynamic power integrity, layout verification, electrical rule checking, and structural design checking. Analyzes results and makes recommendations to improve current and future CPU microarchitectures closely collaborating with logic, circuit, architecture, and design automation teams.
  • Possesses CPU specific expertise in various aspects of structural and physical design, including physical clock design, timing closure, coverage analysis, multiple power domain analysis, structured placement, routing, synthesis, and DFT.
  • Works intimately with industry EDA vendors to build and enhance tool capabilities to design a highspeed, low power synthesizable CPU.
  • Optimizes CPU design to improve product level parameters such as power, frequency, and area. Participates in the development and improvement of physical design methodologies and flow automation.


For information on Intel’s immigration sponsorship guidelines, please see

Intel U.S. Immigration Sponsorship Information

Qualifications:


Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Requirements listed would be obtained through a combination of industry relevant job experience, internship experiences and or schoolwork/classes/research.



Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelors in Computer Engineering or Electrical Engineering or related field with 6+ years of relevant work experience or M.S. in Computer Engineering or Electrical Engineering or related field (or higher degree) with 4 + years of relevant work experience. 
  • 4+ years' experience in Synthesis of a digital logic block or partition.
  • At least 1 Completion of Tape Out on advanced technologies.

4+ years of experience in each of the following:

  • Experience with integrated circuit design tools (ex: Synopsys/Cadence), including logic synthesis, place and route, static timing analysis and design closure.
  • PV convergence (including static timing and power analysis).
  • Chip physical design verification including formal equivalence, electrical rules, DRC/LVS, and Noise flow.
  • Scripting with TCL.


Preferred Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of Tape Out experience.
  • Strong knowledge with Physical design best known practices concerning floor-planning, routing techniques, clock distribution.
  • Strong knowledge of Static Timing Analysis, Noise analysis, and reliability verification techniques.
  • Strong knowledge of RTL to GDS methodologies and formal equivalence
  • Experience performing CPU level timing analysis and optimization, ensuring designs meet functional and performance requirements.
  • Experience generating and verifying timing constraints while addressing timing violations at the chip or block level for CPU cores.
  • Experience working closely with the clocking team and full-chip designers to balance timing fixes, power delivery, clocking, and partitioning.
