title: Senior AI Systems Architect/Researcher
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About Central Engineering Group — Networking Architecture

The CEG Networking Architecture Group defines next-generation networking silicon and platform architecture for hyperscale data centers, cloud infrastructure, and AI workloads. The team focuses on IPU/DPU platforms, advanced packet processing, programmable networking, and the data-movement technologies that enable modern distributed computing systems to scale efficiently.

Position Overview

This role is for a senior AI systems architect who can translate the communication, memory, and orchestration bottlenecks of large-scale AI into networking architecture, IP, and platform direction. The successful candidate will work across research, architecture, silicon, software, and product teams to shape the next generation of distributed AI infrastructure.

As a Senior AI Architect/Researcher, you will help define how AI systems communicate and move data at scale across xPUs, DPUs, IPUs, NICs, memory, and heterogeneous storage. In this pathfinding and research role, you will advance new architectural approaches and translate research insights into network architecture and software capabilities that can influence N+1 to N+3 product roadmap.

The ideal candidate thinks in systems rather than components, understands the memory wall and scale-out serving bottlenecks, and can reason across interconnect, memory hierarchy, software runtime, and compute to unlock the next order of magnitude in AI efficiency. You will help set technical direction and influence silicon and software roadmaps. The candidate is expected to maintain substantial knowledge of state-of-the-art principles and theories, contribute regularly to scientific literature and the research community-at-large, and may participate in the development of Intellectual Property.

Key Responsibilities

Turn Workload Analysis into New IP

• Analyze real AI serving and training workloads, identify communication and memory bottlenecks, and translate those findings into new IP, offload engines, platform features, and architecture requirements

• Drive hardware-software co-design across compute, DPU/IPU, NIC, SoC fabric, and AI serving runtimes, ensuring that networking and data-movement capabilities are reflected in modern inference and training frameworks such as vLLM, SGLang, and others

Architect AI-Scale Networking and Interconnect

• Define the architectural direction for how AI systems and infrastructure move data at scale across xPU-to-xPU, xPU-to-storage, and cross-node paths spanning IPU/DPU platforms, NICs, and heterogeneous storage

• Shape next-generation packet processing, RDMA-class transport, and programmable networking IP that forms the backbone of hyperscale AI inference and training

Attack the Memory Wall and System-Level Bottlenecks

• Investigate the fundamental data-movement bottlenecks in large-scale AI and Agentic inference and training, including KV-cache transfer, disaggregated prefill/decode, model and tensor parallelism, and communication collectives, and translate them into concrete architectural requirements

• Reason across the full memory hierarchy and interconnect to minimize copies, latency, and bandwidth overhead, balancing latency-sensitive control paths against bandwidth-intensive data-paths

Set Roadmap and Lead Across Teams

• Shape multi-generation compute, memory, and interconnect roadmaps across IPU/DPU product lines by defining scaling strategies, migration paths, and architecture requirements that connect research insights to product execution

• Align architecture across networking, SoC fabric, firmware/OS/drivers, and performance modeling teams

What We're Looking For

To be successful in this role, you should demonstrate the following professional traits:

• Architectural vision — defines long-term strategy across AI systems, networking, memory, and software domains

• Influence without authority — drives alignment across multiple teams and disciplines

• Systems thinking — understands interactions across compute, memory, network, and software

• Decision-making under ambiguity — makes sound tradeoffs with incomplete data

• Collaboration — builds strong cross-functional relationships

• Customer-oriented mindset — translates workload needs into architectural innovations

• Ownership and accountability — drives initiatives end-to-end

• Continuous learning — stays current with evolving AI systems, inference runtimes, interconnects, memory technologies, and cloud infrastructure trends

A strong candidate will have enough depth to reason from first principles, enough practical experience to understand implementation constraints, and enough leadership range to align research, architecture, software, and silicon teams around a coherent direction.


Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

• Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related STEM field with 5+ years of relevant experience; or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related STEM field with 2+ years of relevant experience

The experience must include:

• Experience with modern AI training and/or inference systems, including model architecture internals, hardware algorithm code design, serving runtimes, and the memory and data-movement bottlenecks that govern large-scale performance

• Hands-on experience with modern inference and training serving stacks such as vLLM, SGLang, and others, with practical understanding of disaggregated prefill/decode, model parallelism, tensor parallelism, and the communication patterns they create

• Experience in computer architecture and system-level design, with a focus on networking, interconnect, or memory subsystems

• Proficiency in C/C++ and/or Python


Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with memory hierarchy and system bottleneck analysis, including caches, memory controllers, bandwidth/latency tradeoffs, and the memory wall as it applies to data-intensive workloads

• High-performance networking and data-movement technologies such as RDMA/RoCE, InfiniBand, or equivalent transport and interconnect

• Experience with IPU/DPU/SmartNIC or accelerator-centric SoCs, particularly in cloud and hyperscale environments

• Familiarity with PCIe, CXL, and memory semantics for high-performance IO

• Experience defining architecture from concept through silicon, platform software, or shipping product, including translating workload analysis into architecture requirements and new IP

• Track record of cross-team technical leadership and influencing architecture and roadmap at a senior level

title: AI Silicon Performance Modeling and Analysis Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Role and Team


The AI Silicon Architecture and Performance Engineering team is responsible for developing and maintaining performance models that enable architecture exploration, design evaluation, scalability analysis, and performance projection for next-generation AI silicon products. These models are a critical component of the product development process, providing early visibility into architectural tradeoffs, bottlenecks, and optimization opportunities long before silicon availability.


We are seeking a highly experienced and motivated engineer to drive AI silicon performance modeling, validation, architectural analysis, and stakeholder engagement activities. The candidate will work closely with architects, performance stimulus generation teams, silicon design teams, and product stakeholders to evaluate and optimize key AI silicon subsystems that determine overall platform scalability and performance.


The role focuses on performance modeling and analysis of AI SoC communication fabrics, memory subsystems, scale-up and scale-out interconnects, host-device memory paths, and end-to-end data movement infrastructure. The successful candidate will leverage SystemC/TLM-based modeling methodologies to generate actionable insights that directly influence architecture and product decisions.


This position requires a unique combination of software development expertise, architecture understanding, analytical problem solving, and cross-functional technical leadership. The engineer will be expected to independently drive complex technical initiatives while serving as a trusted performance expert across multiple organizations.



Key Responsibilities:

AI Silicon Performance Model Development

  • Implement new architectural features and capabilities based on evolving product requirements.
  • Improve model fidelity, scalability, maintainability, and simulation performance.
  • Perform detailed debugging and root-cause analysis of model issues and performance anomalies.
  • Contribute to the evolution of modeling infrastructure, methodologies, and best practices.
  • Develop, maintain, and enhance SystemC/TLM-based performance models representing critical AI silicon subsystems.
    • Drive modeling of key architectural components including:
    • SoC fabrics and on-chip communication networks
    • Memory controllers and memory subsystem behavior
    • Scale-up controllers and fabrics enabling accelerator-to-accelerator communication within a node, tray, or pod
    • Scale-out controllers and fabrics enabling communication across nodes, racks, and larger AI clusters
    • Host CPU to accelerator memory paths
    • Local, host, and remote memory access paths
    • End-to-end data movement architectures

Functional Validation and Model Correlation:

  • Define and execute comprehensive validation strategies to ensure correctness and architectural accuracy of performance models.
  • Develop validation plans, regression suites, coverage methodologies, and quality metrics.
  • Correlate modeled behavior against architectural expectations, reference simulations, performance projections, and available hardware measurements.
  • Investigate and resolve discrepancies between expected and observed behavior.
  • Establish robust validation frameworks that improve stakeholder confidence in model-generated performance projections.
  • Continuously improve validation methodologies and model quality.

AI Silicon Performance Characterization and Architectural Analysis:

  • Design and execute performance studies covering a wide range of workloads, traffic patterns, and system configurations.
  • Analyze performance of communication fabrics, memory systems, and data movement paths under representative AI workloads.
  • Evaluate bandwidth utilization, latency characteristics, congestion behavior, traffic distribution, buffering efficiency, and resource utilization.
  • Characterize interactions across local memory, host memory, and remote memory domains.
  • Assess scalability of scale-up and scale-out architectures across increasingly larger deployment footprints.
  • Identify performance bottlenecks and quantify their impact on overall system throughput and efficiency.
  • Conduct architectural tradeoff studies to evaluate alternative design approaches.
  • Provide performance-driven recommendations that influence architecture and product decisions.

Performance Data Generation, Analytics and Visualization:

  • Develop frameworks and methodologies for large-scale performance data generation and analysis.
  • Create automated workflows for data collection, processing, correlation, and reporting.
  • Develop performance dashboards and visualization tools that simplify interpretation of complex performance data.
  • Define and track meaningful performance KPIs and architectural metrics.
  • Utilize Python-based analysis frameworks to process large datasets and generate actionable insights.
  • Enable efficient consumption of performance information by architects, designers, and engineering leadership.

Cross-Functional Technical Leadership and Stakeholder Engagement:

  • Partner closely with architecture teams, performance stimulus generation teams, silicon design teams, and product stakeholders.
  • Drive technical discussions related to performance methodology, architectural assumptions, workload behavior, scalability analysis, and bottleneck identification.
  • Review architectural proposals and provide performance-driven feedback.
  • Present performance studies, technical findings, and architectural recommendations to engineering leadership.
  • Influence product and architecture decisions through data-backed analysis and sound engineering judgment.
  • Act as a key technical bridge between architecture, modeling, and performance analysis organizations.

Methodology Development and Team Growth:

  • Drive improvements in modeling methodologies, simulation efficiency, and analysis workflows.
  • Identify opportunities for automation across modeling, validation, performance analysis, and reporting activities.
  • Establish best practices for model quality, performance characterization, and architectural analysis.
  • Contribute to technical mentoring and knowledge sharing across the team.
  • Support the development of junior engineers and future team growth initiatives.
  • Help cultivate a culture of technical excellence and continuous improvement.

The ideal candidate should show the following behavioral traits:

  • Strong quantitative reasoning and data-driven decision-making skills.
    Analytical and Problem-Solving Skills
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills.
  • Presentation (technical) and stakeholder management skills.
  • Influence engineering decisions through rigorous analysis and technical credibility.
  • Operate independently and deliver results in ambiguous problem spaces.
  • Independently solve complex technical problems.

Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications, you must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position.

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Electronics Engineering.

  • 6+ years of industry experience in:

    • Performance modeling, AI silicon architecture, SoC architecture, computer architecture, performance engineering, or related domains.
    • SoC architecture, including on-chip communication fabrics, NoC concepts, high-speed interconnects, and scale-up/scale-out communication architectures.
    • Memory subsystem architecture, including memory controllers, cache hierarchies, data movement, and latency/bandwidth characterization and performance bottleneck analysis.
    • Software development experience in C++.
    • Working proficiency in Python for automation, performance analysis, data processing, and visualization.
    • Hands-on experience with SystemC and Transaction-Level Modeling (TLM) methodologies.
    • Experience developing or validating performance models for AI accelerators, SoCs, CPUs, GPUs, networking products, or complex hardware systems.
    • Performing architectural tradeoff analysis and performance debug and characterization studies.

This position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship.


Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

title: AI System Performance Architect
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Role
We are looking for a talented and motivated AI System Performance Architect. The role owns the end-to-end understanding of AI training and inference systems, sitting where serving strategy, parallelism, collective communication, and interconnect behavior come together. Through analytical modelling and multi-GPU simulation, the candidate translates SLA and deployment targets into concrete architectural guidance for Intel's future AI platforms. Strong analytical skills and the ability to present performance findings and configuration recommendations to engineering and leadership teams are essential.

Key Responsibilities
• Own end-to-end understanding of the AI training/inference system and build analytical models and multi-GPU simulation - including MPI/collective communication (allgather, allreduce, all-to-all) and interconnect contention - to project performance, expose architectural bottlenecks, and recommend optimal Intel system configurations.
• Model inferencing strategies - static batching, continuous batching, disaggregated serving, and chunked prefill - across frameworks such as vLLM and SGLang, covering agentic inferencing, prefix caching, and multi-turn flows.
• Cover data, pipeline, tensor, and expert parallelism and their communication patterns.
• Drive studies against SLA targets - batch size, TTFT, TPOT, ISL/OSL, and TPS.
• Analyse regression run traces and find patterns in utilization counters across SLA operating points to identify architectural bottlenecks.
• Perform what-if analysis by sweeping core count, memory/cache capacity and bandwidth, fabric bandwidth, GPU interconnect, and deployment options; deliver optimization and optimal architecture recommendations.
• Scout whitepapers, blogs, and conferences; keep self and team updated on AI innovations applicable to Intel's end-to-end system.

Qualifications:

Required Qualifications
• Bachelor's, master's or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
• Bachelors with 8+ yrs, master’s with 6+ years and Ph.D. with 3+ years of experience in system performance modelling, AI workload analysis, or hardware architecture.
• Strong proficiency in Python, with the ability to build modular, maintainable analytical models and simulation frameworks.
• Solid understanding of LLM inference and training mechanics: prefill vs. decode, KV cache, batching policies, and quantization.
• Working knowledge of distributed parallelism strategies and their communication patterns.
• Familiarity with multi-GPU interconnect architectures (NVLink, PCIe, CXL, or equivalent).
• Understanding of SoC and platform fundamentals: core count scaling, cache/memory capacity and bandwidth, and fabric behavior.

Good-to-Have Skills
• Experience building discrete-event simulators for multi-node or multi-accelerator systems.
• Familiarity with performance profiling tools (e.g., Intel VTune, NVIDIA Nsight, or similar).
• Prior experience in a semiconductor or hardware company working on AI accelerator or platform products.

As a GPU Software Development Engineer, you will play a critical role in designing and developing software solutions that enable Intel's GPUs, ranging from firmware and device drivers to APIs and application layers. Our primary objective is the development and deployment of robust and performant Windows kernel GPU drivers.  These drivers are instrumental in unleashing the full potential of Intel's integrated and discrete GPU hardware for user-space clients, games, and applications.

Our focus lies in managing critical low-level functions, including device activation, reset and power state transitions, workload submission, power conservation, and scheduling, as well as collaboration with System-on-Chip (SOC) Intellectual Properties (IPs). With this charter, we conceive, create, and verify software solutions that serve as the link between user-space applications and the underlying GPU and SOC.  If you thrive in an environment that involves working on system-level software, with regular exposure to diverse domains such as graphics rendering, firmware, SOC, and power management, then a role on our Kernel Mode Driver Team is where you should be.

title: DevOps Engineering Intern
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Join the DevOpsAI Integration and Distribution organization and gain hands-on experience operating the continuous integration infrastructure behind large-scale driver and platform validation.

Our CI systems run validation around the clock on a large fleet of physical test machines. Today the bulk of that is Linux graphics driver testing, and the scope is expanding to other platforms and products. At this scale, hardware failures are a daily occurrence, and they surface as reports from developers whose tests failed on a machine they suspect is faulty.

As an intern on this team, you will be the first line of triage for those reports. You will confirm what actually happened, determine whether the fault lies in the machine or in the software under test, and route it to the right owner - a lab support request for a physical repair, or back to the development team when a test left the system in a state that only looks like a hardware fault. Distinguishing between the two is the core skill of this role and the one you will develop fastest.

The work is primarily analytical and log-driven: reading system logs, debug output, and monitoring dashboards, and recognizing the detail that does not fit. We value curiosity highly here - the instinct to keep investigating until the cause is understood - and we care more about how you approach a problem than about the length of your CV.

There is also scope to apply AI in this role, and we encourage it: helpers that summarize or classify large volumes of log data, and monitoring tools that use AI to surface anomalies worth a human review. This is both a practical way to accelerate your own work and a direction that matters to the wider organization.

The team and how we work

The team is based in Poland and works in a hybrid model. Because a significant part of this work involves physical test systems in the lab, regular on-site presence is required; this is not a fully remote position. We are a small, fast-moving team with an informal and collaborative culture.

Key Responsibilities

- Triage incoming infrastructure failure reports: review logs and test artifacts, assess the state of the machine, and determine whether the fault originates in the hardware or in the software under test.
- Raise lab support requests for confirmed hardware faults, documenting the affected component, the symptoms observed, and the causes already ruled out.
- Return software-induced failures to the owning team, identifying the test or change that left the system in a faulty state.
- Monitor the health of the test fleet across our dashboards - machine availability, device detection, storage and network errors - and escalate anomalies before they lead to widespread test failures.
- Collect diagnostics on demand: system and kernel logs, console output, device and firmware state, and artifacts from specific CI runs.
- Work directly with test systems in the lab: verify connections and peripherals, confirm component replacements, and validate that a machine is ready to return to production.
- Track recurring failures so the team can identify the least reliable components and platforms, and feed those findings into how the environment is built.
- Automate recurring checks, including with AI-assisted tooling, turning manual dashboard reviews and log analysis into repeatable processes.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

The candidate must be pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electronics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.
- Curiosity and persistence in investigating technical problems, with the patience to work through logs and evidence.
- Working knowledge of the Linux command line and the ability to read system and kernel logs.
- Basic scripting ability in Python or shell.
- A methodical, evidence-based approach to troubleshooting, including the ability to state clearly what has been ruled out.
- Clear written communication in English, as much of this work involves handing findings to others in an actionable form.
- Availability to work on site in the lab on a regular basis, within a hybrid arrangement.

Preferred Qualifications
- Exposure to CI/CD systems, monitoring, or observability tooling.
- Interest in applying AI and large language models to practical problems such as log analysis, failure classification, or anomaly detection.
- Practical PC hardware experience, including assembling systems, replacing components, and diagnosing faults.
- Familiarity with containers and automation tooling such as Docker, Jenkins, or Ansible.
- Experience with log or data analysis and with presenting findings clearly.
- Familiarity with Git and pull request workflows.
- Interest in open source and in the operation of large-scale validation infrastructure.

title: AI Software Development Intern
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Join Intel's Datacenter and AI Software Ecosystem Engineering team to help accelerate the deployment and optimization of Generative AI solutions. This internship focuses on evaluating, benchmarking, and optimizing large language model (LLM) inference workloads across Intel platforms using state-of-the-art serving frameworks such as vLLM, SGLang, and OpenVINO. You will work on AI infrastructure, performance analysis, and cloud-native deployment solutions spanning on-premises and public cloud environments.

Project Context
Generative AI is rapidly transforming enterprise applications, with organizations increasingly deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) for conversational AI, knowledge retrieval, software development, content generation, and intelligent automation. As model sizes and user adoption continue to grow, delivering low-latency, cost-efficient, and scalable AI inference becomes a critical challenge.
Modern AI serving stacks combine model serving frameworks, optimized inference engines, cloud infrastructure, and observability platforms to deliver production-ready AI services. Organizations must balance performance metrics such as throughput, Time to First Token (TTFT), Time per Output Token (TPOT), latency, scalability, and total cost of ownership (TCO) while supporting a diverse range of deployment environments spanning on-premises datacenters, private clouds, and public cloud platforms.
This internship focuses on developing and validating modern AI inference solutions using technologies such as vLLM, SGLang, and OpenVINO. The work will involve deploying and benchmarking state-of-the-art LLMs, analyzing inference performance across Intel platforms, automating testing and deployment workflows, and evaluating cloud-native AI architectures. The objective is to help build scalable, efficient, and production-ready AI serving solutions that enable customers to maximize the value of Generative AI deployments.

What You'll Work On
You will explore the design, deployment, and optimization of Generative AI infrastructure, including:
- LLM deployment and serving: Deploy and evaluate large language models using frameworks such as vLLM, SGLang, and OpenVINO
- Performance analysis: Measure and optimize serving metrics including throughput, latency, TTFT, TPOT, concurrency, and resource utilization
- AI benchmarking: Develop automated benchmarking workflows to characterize model performance across different hardware and software configurations
- Cloud infrastructure: Deploy and evaluate AI workloads in AWS and Google Cloud Platform environments
- DevOps and automation: Build CI/CD pipelines, test automation, and infrastructure tooling using Jenkins, Python, and Linux-based environments
- Data management: Design and maintain systems for storing, querying, and analyzing benchmarking and telemetry data using PostgreSQL and related technologies
- Solution validation: Investigate trade-offs between performance, scalability, accuracy, and cost across various deployment scenarios

Why This Internship?
- Cutting-edge AI engineering: Work on real-world Generative AI deployment and inference optimization challenges
- Industry impact: Contribute to technologies that help customers deploy and scale AI solutions on Intel platforms
- Hands-on experience: Gain practical expertise with LLM serving frameworks, cloud infrastructure and execution
- Mentorship: Learn from experts in AI systems, performance engineering, cloud computing, and software development
- Broad technical exposure: Develop skills across AI, Linux, DevOps, cloud computing, databases, and infrastructure automation
- Intel ecosystem: Build deep knowledge of AI deployment and optimization on Intel Xeon processors and Intel AI software solutions

Qualifications:

Required Qualifications:
- Strong background in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Computer Science, or related field
- Programming skills: Proficiency in Python and experience developing software applications and automation tools
- LLM knowledge: Understanding of transformer-based generative AI models, inference workflows, tokenization, quantization, and serving architectures
- Linux proficiency: Experience working in Linux environments, shell scripting, system monitoring, and troubleshooting
- Academic standing: Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD program in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Software Engineering or related field

Preferred Qualifications:
- Experience with one of LLM serving frameworks such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, TGI, or similar
- Experience benchmarking and performance tuning AI inference workloads

- Cloud fundamentals: Experience with AWS and/or Google Cloud Platform services
- DevOps knowledge: Understanding of CI/CD concepts and tools such as Jenkins, Git, and containerized workflows
- Knowledge of model optimization techniques including quantization, pruning, KV-cache optimization, and speculative decoding
- Experience working with container orchestration technologies such as Kubernetes and Docker
- Experience building APIs and services using Python frameworks such as FastAPI
- Personal or academic projects involving LLM deployment, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), AI agents, or inference optimization

Take the next step in your career by joining a team passionate about advancing the future of AI software. This internship offers a unique opportunity to develop your skills, contribute to impactful projects, and grow alongside industry-leading experts.

title: GPU Architecture and AI Performance Simulation Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Role
We are looking for a talented and motivated GPU Architecture and AI Performance Simulation Engineer. The role sits at the intersection of AI workloads and next-generation GPU hardware - analyzing, modeling, and optimizing AI workload performance on GPU and SoC architectures to shape architectural decisions across current and future silicon. The candidate will guide the team in fine-tuning workload, SoC, and system models, propose data-backed architectural enhancements, and track the AI GPU market to inform Intel's future accelerator roadmap. Strong analytical skills, the ability to present performance findings and trade-offs to engineering and leadership teams, and a willingness to mentor peers are essential.

Key Responsibilities
• Analyze AI workload behavior on GPU architectures - distinguishing compute-bound, memory-bound, and cache-bound behavior to identify performance bottlenecks and optimization opportunities.
• Build and maintain roofline analytical models and cycle-accurate performance models to support hardware what-if studies and guide micro-architectural decisions.
• Analyze AI workloads built on Transformer and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures, inference and training, and assess the hardware-utilization impact of kernel-level optimizations such as Flash Attention, Flash Decode, Sparse Attention, and Causal Masking.
• Model and analyze multi-GPU and at-scale AI systems - workload distribution, synchronization overhead, and communication-compute overlap.
• Drive workload and architectural bottleneck analysis for the early architecture definition phases of Intel's future AI GPU accelerator roadmap products.
• Guide and mentor the team in delivering analytical models and end-to-end system-level performance projections; review modeling methodology and drive consistency across studies.
• Propose new architectural enhancement ideas, backed by quantitative modeling data and workload evidence.
• Maintain a forward-looking view of the AI GPU and accelerator market - tracking competitive roadmaps, whitepapers, and conferences - and translate those trends into architectural requirements while keeping the team updated on applicable AI innovations.

Qualifications:

Required Qualifications
• Bachelor's with 10+ yrs, master’s with 8+ years and Ph.D with 5+ years of experience in System/GPU/SoC performance engineering, AI workload analysis, or hardware architecture.
• Deep knowledge of GPU microarchitecture (NVIDIA SM/CUDA cores, Intel Xe cores, or equivalent), GPU execution pipelines, and cache hierarchy design (L1/L2/L3).
• Familiarity with SoC design principles, on-chip fabric, memory subsystems, and interconnects.
• Experience with multi-GPU system architectures (NVLink, PCIe, CXL, or equivalent) and scaling AI workloads across multiple devices.
• Good understanding of distributed training/inference techniques: Tensor Parallel, Data Parallel, Pipeline Parallel, Expert Parallel, and Model Split methodologies.


Good-to-Have Skills
• Experience with cycle-accurate simulators or hardware performance emulation platforms.
• Familiarity with AI framework internals (PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow) and kernel-level optimization (CUDA, SYCL, HIP, Triton).
• Exposure to LLM inference optimization techniques (quantization, KV-cache management, speculative decoding).
• Experience with performance profiling tools (e.g., NVIDIA Nsight, Intel VTune, AMD ROCProfiler, or similar).
• Publications or patents in GPU architecture, AI systems performance, or related areas.

We're looking for talented individuals excited to solve complex challenges and shape the future of platform architecture. If you're ready to make an impact and contribute to Intel's success, we encourage you to apply today.

title: Design Automation Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel Foundry is at the forefront of technology innovation, enabling the design and manufacturing of world-class semiconductor products. As part of this team, you will collaborate with experts across domains to enhance Intel's design and manufacturing capabilities. Intel Foundry plays a key role in delivering solutions that power the next generation of technology products, supporting Intel’s broader mission to create a better future through innovation. 

As a member of the Frame Automation Team (FRAT) in Intel Foundry, you will design, develop, test, and debug software tools, flows, and methodologies used in design automation and by teams in the design of hardware products, process design, or manufacturing. Responsibilities include capturing user stories/requirements, writing both functional and test code, automating build and deployment, and/or performing unit, integration, and end to end testing of the software tools. Designs and builds web-based interfaces to configure launch and control tools - including frontends, backends, databases and APIs.  

The Frame is a critical component of every wafer that is manufactured by Intel. The frame contains silicon structures that are needed by various metrology and lithographic tools.  Intel's Frame Automation Team is responsible for developing automation and specifications to support the Frame.  To keep the process going, we work closely with engineers from Lithography, Process Integration, Device Physics, Circuit Design, and RET (Resolution Enhancement Technology) teams to understand and establish frame structures. We design frame structures so that the next generation of Intel products are the best they can be.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Design, develop, test, and debug software tools and methodologies for design automation
  • Capture user stories and requirements to inform tool design and functionality

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
As a Facilities Water/Waste Treatment Technician, you will play a critical role in the operation and maintenance of Intel's industrial water and wastewater systems. On a daily basis, you will conduct sampling and analysis to ensure water quality across systems such as UltraPure Water (UPW), Liquid Industrial Waste (LIWS), and Industrial Wastewater Treatment (IWT). Your work will directly contribute to maintaining the integrity of Intel's water treatment infrastructure, ensuring consistent performance and compliance with environmental and operational standards.

Business group
The Intel Foundry organization is dedicated to driving innovation in semiconductor manufacturing while maintaining operational excellence and sustainability. Within this team, you will join a group committed to supporting Intel's advanced manufacturing capabilities by ensuring the reliable and efficient operation of critical facilities systems. Your contributions will help advance Intel's leadership in the industry by supporting the foundational systems that enable cutting-edge production.

- Perform sampling and analysis across water systems such as reverse osmosis (RO), ion exchange, ultrafiltration, ultraviolet light sterilization, and wastewater systems to monitor water quality.
- Operate, maintain, and troubleshoot industrial water, waste, and chemical systems, including cooling towers, steam boilers, heat exchangers, and air scrubbers.
- Utilize analytical instruments, including ion chromatography and particle analysis tools, to assess water health and system performance.
- Coordinate with third-party laboratories to ship samples, obtain results, and maintain robust testing protocols.
- Assist in preparing technical reports and presenting findings to diverse audiences, including technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
- Support the implementation of new methods and technologies to improve analysis accuracy, reduce turnaround times, and optimize costs.

- Familiarity with analytical instruments for water analysis, including ion chromatography or Differential Microbio Analysis (DMA).

title: Gases Technician
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role

Intel Foundry is seeking a skilled Gases Technician to support the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of gas delivery systems that enable advanced semiconductor manufacturing. In this role, you will operate, maintain, troubleshoot, and continuously improve critical gas distribution infrastructure that directly impacts manufacturing performance, product quality, and

operational reliability.

As a member of the Facilities team, you will partner with engineers, manufacturing teams, suppliers, and fellow technicians to ensure uninterrupted delivery of high-purity gases while maintaining Intel's world-class standards for safety, quality, and environmental stewardship.

What You'll Do


Operations & Maintenance

  • Operate, monitor, maintain, and troubleshoot gas delivery systems supporting high-volume semiconductor manufacturing.
  • Perform preventive and corrective maintenance on gas distribution equipment and associated facility systems.
  • Conduct inspections, repairs, equipment changeovers, and system restorations while ensuring compliance with established procedures.
  • Coordinate gas deliveries, vendor activities, and operational transitions to maintain uninterrupted manufacturing support.

Monitoring & Troubleshooting

  • Monitor SCADA/Cimplicity and related control systems to evaluate alarms, trends, and system performance.
  • Diagnose equipment and process issues using operational data, analytical instrumentation, and technical expertise.
  • Respond to equipment alarms and abnormal operating conditions, minimizing manufacturing impacts and restoring safe operations.
  • Lead structured troubleshooting and root-cause analysis efforts to resolve recurring reliability, process, and gas-quality issues.

Quality & Continuous Improvement

  • Perform gas sampling and analytical testing while maintaining contamination control and sample integrity requirements.
  • Support semiconductor purity standards through knowledge of gas compatibility, materials of construction, and process controls.
  • Identify and implement continuous improvement opportunities that enhance reliability, reduce operational risk, and prevent future failures.
  • Review performance trends and equipment history to proactively address emerging issues before they affect manufacturing.

Documentation & Collaboration

  • Maintain accurate maintenance, operational, sampling, and shift-turnover records.
  • Utilize computerized maintenance management systems and digital tools to document work and track asset performance.
  • Support the development and revision of operating procedures, job plans, risk assessments, and change-control documentation.
  • Share technical knowledge and assist with training and qualification of technicians.

Job Requirements

Candidates must be able to:

  • Work a compressed 12-hour night-shift schedule, rotating between three and four days per week.
  • Work in cleanroom and industrial environments while wearing required personal protective equipment.
  • Lift and carry up to 30 pounds and move heavier materials using approved handling equipment.
  • Walk several miles per shift and work in physically demanding environments.
  • Support weekend, holiday, overtime, and on-call operational requirements as needed.
  • Work at heights, climb ladders, and operate powered industrial equipment after certification.

What Makes You Successful

The ideal candidate demonstrates:

  • An unwavering commitment to safety and quality.
  • Strong mechanical and technical troubleshooting skills.
  • Sound judgment in dynamic operational environments.
  • The ability to communicate effectively across technicians, engineers, suppliers, and manufacturing stakeholders.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • A continuous improvement mindset focused on reliability, efficiency, and operational excellence.
  • The ability to thrive in a fast-paced, team-oriented manufacturing environment.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.

Qualifications:


Candidates must meet the minimum qualifications listed below to be considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are additional criteria that may be used to identify the most qualified candidates.

This position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship.


Minimum Qualifications

  • Candidates must possess one of the following:
    • Highschool diploma or equivalent and 6+ years of relevant technical experience.
    • -or- Associate degree in a technical discipline with 3+ years of technical experience;
    • -or-Relevant military training and technical experience.
  • Experience supporting hazardous production materials (HPM), bulk gas systems, industrial controls, or semiconductor manufacturing facilities.
  • Experience in high-purity process environments.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in gas delivery systems, semiconductor facilities, industrial maintenance, or related technical operations.
  • Associate or bachelor's degree in a technical field and 4 + years of technical experience.
  • Proven ability to collaborate across cross-functional teams and drive operational improvements.

Why Intel Foundry

At Intel Foundry, you'll help support the infrastructure behind some of the world's most advanced semiconductor manufacturing technologies. You'll be part of a highly skilled team responsible for enabling innovation through operational excellence, technical expertise, and continuous improvement. Intel’s Data Center Platform Engineering hardware team develops and supports platform solutions for leading cloud service providers and internet companies. descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
Intel's Automated Material Handling Systems (AMHS) team is the backbone of our 24x7 manufacturing and foundry operations, ensuring the seamless automated delivery and storage of materials across our state-of-the-art fabrication facilities. We are looking for a motivated and skilled AMHS Equipment Technician to join our dedicated team of technicians, engineers, and managers in Rio Rancho, NM. In this role, you will play a critical part in keeping Intel's manufacturing operations running at peak performance by maintaining, troubleshooting, and optimizing our AMHS infrastructure.

Business Group
The Intel Foundry business group focuses on delivering cutting-edge manufacturing solutions, enabling Intel's leadership in the semiconductor industry. This group drives innovation and ensures operational excellence in Intel's state-of-the-art facilities.   • Adaptable - You embrace change and thrive in dynamic, evolving environments

  • A self-starter - You take initiative, anticipate challenges, and proactively seek solutions

The Advanced Design and Foundational IP (AD-FIP) organization within Intel's Design Technology Platform (DTP) is seeking a dynamic and technically accomplished DTCO & Design Technology Integration Technical Program Manager to help lead and shape one of Intel Foundry's most strategically critical organizations. descriptionHtml:

Job Description: 

 Intel Foundry Capacity and Strategic Planning is responsible for ensuring the right capacity is available at the right place, time, and cost to support customer commitments and business objectives across Intel's manufacturing network. This role drives strategic capacity planning across multiple technologies, sites, and planning horizons, enabling informed decisions that support growth, profitability, and operational excellence.

Lead long-range capacity planning, scenario development, and supply-demand analysis across Intel's manufacturing network.

Partner directly with Fab Managers and manufacturing leadership to ensure plans are executable and aligned with factory realities.

title: E-core CPU Full Chip Physical Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Become a key member of a team participating in the physical design construction and integration and verification of a future Intel CPU. This position requires an engineer with broad physical design and STA skills, coupled with leadership skills necessary to drive methodology and to collaborate effectively with multiple functional teams within the CPU design team. We are looking for a talented individual to drive the physical convergence of a Full-Chip (FC) assembly of partitions.

As a Full Chip design engineer, you will perform floorplanning, pin and feedthrough planning, repeater insertion, power grid generation and assembly of partitions. Given the need for executing multiple projects in parallel, you will be responsible for driving efficiency and quality improvements to the overall FC methodology - including floorplan optimization for better utilization/QoR/runtime and timing and physical aware feedthrough/pin placement. You will also be responsible for coordinating collateral handoffs between the FC Design team and other functions within back-end design such as Clocking, Power Delivery and Partition synthesis/APR. You will drive physical design and timing closure including FEV, LVS, DRC, and reliability verification (IR drop / EM analysis).

The ideal candidate should have an aptitude to work effectively with EDA tools and exhibit behavioral traits that indicate:

  • Ability to work well in a team and be productive under aggressive schedules
  • Excellent written and verbal communications skills
  • Self-motivation and well organized

Must have either BS or MS in Electrical Engineering or Computer Engineering
Minimum 7 years of experience in


  • CPU physical design and timing verification
  • Synthesis/APR flows on multi voltage high frequency designs including custom polygon editing
  • Tcl scripting
  • Noise, cross-talk, OCV analysis.
  • Floorplanning and physical design and timing closure.
  • Formal equivalence, DRC/LVS, IR and electro-migration checks

title: CPU Senior Timing Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact As a CPU Senior Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the future of high-performance computing by driving the physical design implementation of cutting-edge CPU designs. You will ensure that the design meets frequency, power, and signoff targets across all required modes and corners. This role works across design, block timing, physical design, clocking, and integration teams to resolve critical timing issues, improve timing predictability, and support successful tapeout. Business group You will join Intel Corporation's CPU design and development team, which is dedicated to engineering world-class computing solutions. This group is at the heart of innovation, delivering high-performance designs that power industry-leading technologies and support Intel's broader mission to advance computing performance and capabilities globally. Key Responsibilities - Drive top-level timing analysis and closure for CPU IP across implementation and signoff stages. - Develop, review, and maintain timing constraints, MMMC scenarios, path budgets, and timing exceptions for top-level integration. - Analyze and resolve setup, hold, clock gating, noise, and cross-block timing issues affecting CPU performance targets. - Partner with RTL, block owners, physical design, and clock teams to close critical paths and improve timing convergence. - Ensure correlation between block-level, top-level, and signoff timing environments, and track timing risks against project milestones. - Develop scripts and methodology improvements to automate timing analysis, reporting, and closure efficiency.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications - Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or related field with 4+ years of hands-on experience OR Master's degree in a relevant field with 3+ years of hands-on experience with strong exposure to CPU or high-performance IP timing closure. - Strong knowledge of static timing analysis, MMMC flows, timing constraints, OCV/derates, crosstalk, and timing exceptions. - Hands-on experience with STA tools such as PrimeTime or Tempus, and familiarity with implementation tools such as ICC2 or Innovus. - Proficiency in Tcl and at least one scripting language such as Python, Perl, or shell. - Strong debugging, problem-solving, and cross-functional communication skills. Preferred Qualifications - Knowledge of scripting languages like Tcl, Perl, or Python for workflow automation in physical design. - Proven ability to work effectively in dynamic, cross-geographical, and interdisciplinary teams. - Enthusiasm for designing world-class CPUs that drive innovation and empower future technologies. The ideal leader has experience with fully automating high-tech manufacturing factories in Semiconductor Advanced Packaging.  They can combine their operational experience in semiconductor manufacturing, large-scale factory transformation, and strong knowledge of emerging automation technologies. title: Senior Platform Hardware Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Position Overview As a Platform Hardware Design Engineer, you will provide technical leadership for the architecture, design, integration, bring-up, and validation of complex platform hardware. You will drive hardware development end-to-end, translating high level system requirements into detailed circuit and component specifications and leading designs from architecture and schematic development through PCB implementation, board power-on, debugging, validation, and delivery. You will be expected to make platform level technical decisions, resolve complex and ambiguous multidisciplinary problems, lead critical design reviews, drive cross-functional alignment, mentor engineers, and influence hardware development practices across projects. Our Business Group You will be joining the Silicon and Platform Engineering Group (SPE), an organization at Intel committed to advancing Intel's mission of delivering world-class silicon and platform solutions. The group focuses on developing integrated systems that align with customer needs and support Intel's broader goals of leadership in technology innovation. SPE collaborates across diverse domains to ensure Intel platforms meet performance, reliability, and scalability requirements. Our work sits at the intersection of silicon, board hardware, firmware, validation, signal and power integrity, mechanical and thermal engineering, PCB technology, manufacturing, and system integration. Our senior hardware engineers have a broader responsibility than executing an individual design. They help establish platform architecture, guide implementation, identify and qualify appropriate hardware solutions, provide technical leadership during board power-on and debug, and lead resolution of schematic, layout, SI/PI, and hardware issues. Key Responsibilities Platform Architecture and End-to-End Technical Ownership • Own complex platform-board designs from requirements and architecture through deployment. • Translate high level platform and silicon requirements into system architecture, circuit level requirements, component specifications, and PCB implementation requirements. • Define and drive critical platform architecture decisions encompassing high speed interfaces, memory, power delivery, clocking, resets, sequencing, control, management, and validation functionality. • Lead design trade-offs across electrical performance, SI/PI, thermal and mechanical constraints, board complexity, reliability, manufacturability, component availability, cost, schedule, and system compatibility. • Establish clear technical direction where platform requirements or implementation approaches are initially ambiguous. Advanced Board Design and Technical Leadership • Lead development of complex high density, multilayer PCBs incorporating advanced digital, analog, mixed signal, and power circuitry. • Own or provide technical leadership for schematic design, component selection, interface definition, PCB implementation, and design verification. • Establish PCB stack-up, placement, routing, impedance, power distribution, and critical interface requirements in collaboration with layout and analysis teams. • Lead schematic, layout, and technical design reviews and ensure critical findings are driven to closure. • Guide engineers and layout teams in resolving challenging schematic, PCB, layout, and design-for-X issues. • Identify and qualify new hardware solutions and reusable design approaches where appropriate. High-Speed Design and SI/PI • Apply deep understanding of signal integrity, power integrity, transmission-line behavior, high-speed interfaces, and platform power delivery to architecture and implementation decisions. • Partner with SI/PI engineers to establish design constraints and evaluate critical interfaces and power delivery networks. • Review PCB implementations for stack-up, placement, routing, return path continuity, high speed performance, and advanced SI/PI considerations. • Use modeling, simulation, measurement, and hardware correlation to guide technical decisions as appropriate. Power Architecture and Power Delivery • Define and review platform power delivery architecture, voltage regulation, sequencing, power budgeting, and power distribution networks. • Evaluate board and system power delivery tradeoffs, considering electrical performance, transient behavior, PCB implementation, and platform requirements. • Work with power integrity specialists to assess PDN behavior and drive required design improvements. • Apply simulation and hardware measurement to correlate power delivery behavior and resolve platform issues. Board Bring-up, System Integration and Debug • Define and lead power-on, bring up, validation, characterization, and debug strategy for complex platform hardware. • Lead resolution of difficult issues spanning board hardware, silicon, firmware, high-speed interfaces, power delivery, and system integration. • Use disciplined root cause analysis to diagnose failures and define corrective actions. • Provide hands-on technical leadership in the lab during critical power-on, bring up, and debug activities. • Apply appropriate measurement techniques and laboratory equipment for high speed, low speed, clock, power, and digital/analog circuitry. • Drive problems across engineering boundaries until technical closure. Program and Cross-functional Leadership • Serve as a senior technical interface across silicon, firmware, validation, SI/PI, mechanical, thermal, PCB layout, manufacturing, suppliers, and program teams. • Lead technical discussions and design reviews and communicate risks, tradeoffs, recommendations, and design decisions clearly to stakeholders. • Identify technical and execution risks early and drive mitigation plans. • Own technical readiness for critical hardware milestones, including design release, fabrication, assembly, power-on, and validation. • Develop and improve reusable architectures, review methodologies, design checklists, development flows, and engineering practices. • Mentor engineers through architecture development, schematic and PCB reviews, bring-up, debug, and technical problem solving. • Influence technical decisions and engineering practices beyond an individual board or project.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications
• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related discipline.
• 6+ years significant hands-on industry experience in complex platform hardware, PCB development, or system hardware engineering.
• Demonstrated experience leading complex board designs from architecture and requirements through schematic design, PCB implementation, bring-up, debug, and validation.
• Deep understanding of digital and analog board design, electrical interfaces, mixed-signal fundamentals, and system architecture.
• Strong knowledge of high speed interfaces, transmission line behavior, signal integrity, power integrity, memory, clocking, reset, sequencing, and power delivery.
• Proven experience with PCB technologies and layout techniques, including stack-up, placement, routing, and advanced SI/PI considerations.
• Advanced experience with schematic capture and PCB design/review environments.
• Strong hands-on laboratory experience and demonstrated ability to diagnose complex board level problems, determine root cause, and drive corrective actions.
• Demonstrated ability to analyze board/system level design tradeoffs and make sound technical decisions.
• Ability to independently lead complex technical development activities and drive issues across multiple engineering functions.
• Strong technical documentation, presentation, written communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
• Demonstrated technical leadership and mentoring capability.
Preferred Qualifications
• Extensive experience designing complex compute, server, client, FPGA-based, semiconductor validation or other high performance platform hardware.
• Experience with high speed I/O and memory technologies such as PCIe, DDR/LPDDR, Ethernet, USB, or comparable interfaces.
• Deep understanding of PCB stack-up, placement, routing, high speed design, transmission lines, signal integrity, crosstalk, power integrity, and PDN design.
• Experience applying SI/PI, power, circuit, or electromagnetic simulation to board architecture and design decisions.
• Experience defining and validating sophisticated power delivery solutions, power management architectures and basic Verilog coding,
• Strong understanding of PCB fabrication, assembly manufacturing flows, DFM/DFT, component selection, and design release processes.
• Proven experience taking complex boards through the complete lifecycle from architecture through PCB implementation, fabrication, assembly, power-on, validation, and deployment.

title: Platform Integration Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About Central Engineering Group

The Central Engineering Group (CEG) is Intel's hub for driving innovation and excellence in silicon development. Focused on engineering solutions that power Intel's flagship products, CEG architects, designs, and validates IP foundational to Intel's broader technology portfolio. By joining this team, you will be part of a collaborative, inclusive environment driving advancements to strengthen Intel's leadership in the semiconductor industry.

Position Overview

As an IP Logic Design Engineer at Intel, you will play a pivotal role in developing high-quality IP blocks and subsystems for integration into full chip designs. You'll be responsible for creating cutting-edge logic designs, optimizing power, performance, and area, and ensuring seamless integration with the broader system. Your contributions will directly impact Intel's ability to deliver next-generation silicon solutions with speed, efficiency, and reliability.


Key Responsibilities

• Develop logic designs, register transfer level (RTL) coding, and simulation for IP blocks and subsystems for integration into full chip designs

title: Manufacturing Equipment Technician (MTE) - Day Shift - Shift 5
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel Corporation is a global leader in the semiconductor industry, designing and manufacturing the vital technologies that power our connected world. Within Intel, the Advanced Packaging Technology Development - Substrate and Wafer Assembly (ATPD: SWA) team is at the cutting edge of micro processing evolution. Our mission is to be the premier supplier of leading-edge, cost-effective substrate packaging solutions, enabling the next generation of high-performance computing.

We are seeking a highly motivated Manufacturing Equipment Technician (MTE) - Day Shift - Shift 5 to join our cleanroom operations in Arizona. In this role, you will play a critical part in maintaining, troubleshooting, and optimizing the advanced machinery that makes our microchip packaging possible. Working under general supervision in a fast-paced R&D and production cleanroom, you will support state-of-the-art wet chemistry, plating, and dry high-vacuum toolsets, driving continuous improvement and equipment reliability.

Shift Information

This role operates on Shift 5: 6:00 AM – 6:18 PM on an alternating weekly schedule:

Sun-Tues and alternating Wednesday days

Key Responsibilities:

  • Troubleshoot & Repair: Perform complex electrical and mechanical troubleshooting to diagnose and repair non-functioning semiconductor manufacturing equipment.
  • Maintenance & Calibration: Conduct routine setup, calibration, and preventive maintenance on high-tech wet chemistry, plating, and dry high-vacuum toolsets.
  • Technical Interpretation: Read and interpret complex electrical schematics, blueprints, engineering drawings, and operating manuals to assemble or dismantle hardware.
  • Documentation & Compliance: Systematically document all maintenance events, repairs, findings, and parts usage in tracking databases.
  • Collaborative Optimization: Partner with engineering, process, and support teams to conduct root-cause analyses, reduce equipment downtime, and implement yield improvement initiatives.

As a Successful Candidate, You Will Bring:

  • Strong Judgment & Initiative: Proactively makes data-driven decisions and resolves nonstandard equipment and process anomalies.
  • Adaptable & Resilient: Thrives under minimal supervision in a fast-paced, rapidly shifting manufacturing environment.
  • Team-Oriented & Self-Motivated: Strong individual ownership of tasks balanced with a dedication to collaborative team goals.
  • Multitasking Agility: Welcomes the opportunity to manage multiple toolsets and priorities concurrently.
  • Analytical Problem Solver: Logical mindset geared toward systematic troubleshooting and interpretation of equipment logs.
  • Effective Communicator: Strong verbal and written communication skills to collaborate seamlessly with peers, engineers, and internal stakeholders.

Are you ready to shape the future of technology and build a world-class career in semiconductor manufacturing? Apply today to join the Intel ATPD team in Arizona!

title: Senior Azure DevOps Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Senior Azure DevOps Engineer - Full-Stack and Hybrid Cloud Systems
Bangalore, India ' Full-Time
About the Role
We are looking for an experienced, versatile Azure DevOps Engineer to join our team and become a genuine part of what we are building.
This is not a straightforward DevOps role. Our system spans a full-stack web application, a rich and deliberately complex Azure cloud environment, and on-premises Linux lab infrastructure that talks directly to FPGA hardware. The person who thrives here will be someone who gets energized by that kind of variety, not overwhelmed by it.
Just as importantly, we are looking for someone who communicates well, enjoys working closely with developers and customers, and takes real pride in the quality and reliability of what they build and maintain. Technical depth matters, but so does being someone the team genuinely enjoys working with.
The Environment You Will Be Working In
The Application
We build and operate a full-stack web application with a Node.js server, TypeScript services, and a React.js client. The application connects to on-premises Linux lab environments where a Python-based layer orchestrates and controls FPGA hardware. The cloud and the physical lab need to talk to each other reliably, securely, and continuously.
The Internal Azure Subscription
This environment is mature, fully operational, and genuinely complex. Containerized workloads run on Kubernetes. We use the right database for the right job: relational databases for structured data, a document store for flexibility, in-memory caching for performance, distributed file storage for shared access, and large-scale telemetry and analytics through Azure Data Explorer. Identity and access management spans SSO, Active Directory, Kerberos, and Microsoft Entra ID, because our permission model is real-world complex, not textbook simple. We also run an internal HPC-grade job scheduling system that manages compute resource allocation and permissions across lab infrastructure.
The External Azure Subscription
This subscription is starting now and will serve customers outside our organization. Security, network architecture, compliance, and performance are the foundation here, not afterthoughts. You will be building this alongside our network and cybersecurity teams with genuine ownership of getting it right.
What You Will Be Doing
CI/CD and Developer Support
Design, maintain, and continuously improve pipelines covering the full delivery lifecycle for our Node.js, TypeScript, and React codebase. When something breaks in a pipeline or a release goes sideways, the development team will come to you, and you will be the person who unblocks them calmly and effectively. Beyond day-to-day support, you will raise the quality bar by embedding good practices into the workflow: automated testing, regression coverage, reproducible builds, and documentation that people actually use.
Automation and AI-Driven Operations
We want a platform that monitors itself, detects problems, and recovers on its own wherever possible. When it cannot, it should tell us clearly and give us what we need to act fast. We want you to use AI tools actively and creatively to get there, whether that means intelligent alerting, automated remediation, generated runbooks, or things we have not thought of yet. Every repeated manual task is a candidate for automation.
Platform and Infrastructure Engineering
Own the day-to-day health and long-term evolution of our internal Azure environment: Kubernetes workloads, data services, storage, networking, and identity systems. Maintain the bridge between cloud and lab, keeping our Linux hosts and hardware systems connected and operational as the platform grows.
Security and the External-Facing Cloud
Work closely with our network and cybersecurity teams to design and harden the external subscription before customers ever touch it. Zero-trust access, network segmentation, secrets management, private endpoints, and audit logging need to be built in from the start. We need someone who thinks about security architecturally, not just operationally.
Required Qualifications
Why Join Us
The work is technically rich and varied in a way that is hard to find. You will not be executing tickets. You will be shaping how the platform evolves, with real ownership and real impact on both the team that builds the product and the customers who use it. We are a collaborative group that values good judgment, welcomes new ideas, and tries hard to be a team people are glad to be part of.

Qualifications:

4+ years of hands-on experience with Azure DevOps and cloud infrastructure, including ownership of production environments.
Azure DevOps and CI/CD: Strong experience with YAML pipelines, Repos, Artifacts, self-hosted build agents, Git workflows, and release management, including deployment across development, test, and production environments, versioning, and rollback.
Kubernetes and AKS: Practical experience deploying, operating, and troubleshooting production workloads using Docker and Helm, including configuration, networking, storage, scaling, and upgrades.
Azure infrastructure and networking: Experience managing compute, storage, virtual networks, DNS, firewalls, and connectivity between cloud and on-premises environments.
Infrastructure as Code: Experience creating repeatable infrastructure deployments using Terraform, Bicep, or equivalent tools.
Linux administration: Strong troubleshooting skills across services, processes, permissions, networking, storage, and shared file systems such as NFS.
Scripting and automation: Ability to write maintainable automation using Python, Bash, PowerShell, or similar languages to reduce manual work and improve reliability.
Application delivery: Experience building CI/CD pipelines for JavaScript and TypeScript applications, particularly React frontends, Node.js backends, and containerized microservices.
Identity and cloud security: Practical understanding of Microsoft Entra ID, authentication and authorization, role-based access control, service and workload identities, secrets and certificate management, least privilege, and network isolation.
Database operations: Working knowledge of relational databases, particularly Microsoft SQL Server, and familiarity with NoSQL systems. Ability to manage deployment, connectivity, access permissions, monitoring, backup and recovery, and operational troubleshooting.
Monitoring and incident resolution: Experience with centralized logs, metrics, dashboards, and alerts using Azure Monitor, Application Insights, or equivalent tools, with the ability to investigate failures across applications and infrastructure.
Technical ownership and collaboration: Ability to drive infrastructure improvements from design through production, document decisions, and work effectively with developers, IT, and security teams.
Advantages
Experience securing and operating customer-facing or external-user cloud environments.
Experience with hybrid platforms connecting cloud services to physical hardware, lab systems, or FPGA environments.
Experience managing both Linux and Windows build agents and their dependencies.
Practical use of AI-assisted engineering or AIOps tools for automation, troubleshooting, incident analysis, or operational improvement.

title: PnP System Validation and Integration Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The PnP SV (Power and Performance System Validation) group is responsible for the functional (logical) integrity of the processor, from the first silicon stage through to mass production.

In the period before the first silicon, the group is responsible for defining the processor testing methodology and its environment, defining test plans, and developing some of the software and hardware tools required to perform the tests.

In the period between the first silicon and readiness for mass production, the group focuses on running the defined tests and performs DEBUG of failures in order to ensure that all logical bugs have been found. After approval for mass production, problems and bugs that were missed (from customers) arrive, and work is done on them (as each processor has many derivatives).

The work in the department involves collaboration with additional groups – logic design, architecture, software groups for tool and simulator development, and more.

A complete project lasts between two to four years, with each phase taking approximately half of that period.

Job Description

  • Taking an active part in performance and power measurement and improvement tests for Intel's flagship processors and various platforms.
  • Defining and executing test plans, debugging in highly complex environments using advanced equipment and innovative methods.
  • Participating in setting goals, plans, and work methodologies. Working closely with product architects, the design group, software, and Validation teams in Israel and abroad.

Qualifications:

  • Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or Computer Science
  • 3-6 years of experience working with processor architecture or at the system/platform level of a processor and operating system, preferably in the field of Silicon/Platform Validation – mandatory
  • Programming knowledge in Python – mandatory
  • Programming knowledge in C++ – advantage
  • Good familiarity with hardware testing methods and laboratory equipment
  • Advantage in software background, commercial systems

title: Senior Analog and Mixed Signal Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Group

Intel's Advanced Design Foundational IP Organization (AD-FIP) within Design Technology Platform (DTP) drives pathfinding and development of the analog/mixed-signal and high-speed I/O IP that defines what Intel's leading-edge process technologies can deliver. The High-Speed I/O team develops SerDes and die-to-die interface reference designs and test chips that co-optimize Intel process technology with next-generation wireline standards, including high-speed PAM4 electrical links, PCIe, UCIe, and HBM.

The Role

We are seeking a senior technical expert in high-speed SerDes circuit design and SerDes system architecture. You will own SerDes link architecture on Intel's leading technology test chips, from link budget and equalization strategy down to transistor-level design of the critical analog front-end and clocking blocks. You will also translate link requirements into device, interconnect, and design-rule requirements that shape future Intel process nodes. This is a senior individual-contributor role with technical leadership across design, layout, and measurement engineers.

Responsibilities

  • Define SerDes link architecture for next-generation interfaces (224G/448G-class PAM4 electrical links, PCIe Gen7/Gen8, UCIe): channel analysis, link budget, jitter and noise budgeting, and equalization partitioning across TX FFE, RX CTLE, DFE, and ADC/DSP-based receivers.
  • Build and maintain system-level link models (statistical and time-domain, in MATLAB or Python; COM and IBIS-AMI based) and use them to derive block-level specifications for TX, RX, ADC, and clocking circuits.
  • Lead transistor-level design of critical SerDes blocks: TX drivers (SST/CML) with FFE, RX AFE (CTLE, VGA, termination, T-coil and ESD co-design), DFE and slicers, time-interleaved ADC front ends, CDR and phase interpolators, LC and ring PLLs, and clock distribution.
  • Drive test-chip definition, integration, tapeout readiness, and silicon bring-up; correlate measured BER, eye, jitter, and power against models, and lead root-cause analysis of silicon-to-model gaps.
  • Translate SerDes requirements into process and PDK requirements (device fT/fmax and parasitics, BEOL RC, inductor Q, matching, ESD capacitance budget, reliability and aging) and drive design-technology co-optimization with process, PDK, and template-library teams.
  • Provide technical leadership: mentor engineers, lead design reviews, and represent Intel Foundry in technical engagements with IP partners and foundry customers.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelors Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or Electrical and Computer Engineering with 6+ years of industry experience in high-speed wireline SerDes circuit design experience -OR- Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or Electrical and Computer Engineering with 4+ years of industry experience in high-speed wireline SerDes circuit design, -OR-  Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or Electrical and Computer Engineering with 2+ years of industry experience in high-speed wireline SerDes circuit design.
  • Experience in Transistor-level design of SerDes TX, RX, or clocking circuits in at least one silicon-proven design at 28 Gb/s per lane or higher.
  • Experience in at least one of the following:
    • SerDes link architecture: channel and link-budget analysis or equalization trade-off studies used to set block-level specifications.
    • Lab validation of high-speed links: BER, eye, or jitter measurement and correlation to simulation.
    • Behavioral or statistical link modeling in MATLAB or Python.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Silicon-proven designs at 56 Gb/s PAM4 or higher, in FinFET or GAA CMOS; multiple tape-outs with block ownership.
  • Experience across all three areas above (architecture, lab validation, and link modeling).
  • Experience in ADC/DSP-based receivers at 112 Gb/s PAM4 or higher, including time-interleaved ADC design. - 224 Gb/s-class link development (IEEE 802.3dj, OIF CEI-224G). - PCIe Gen6/Gen7 PHY or UCIe die-to-die PHY development.
  • Design experience on 5nm-class or more advanced nodes, with design-technology co-optimization experience with process teams.
  • Experience in package and channel co-design: package/PCB channel modeling, signal and power integrity, crosstalk.
  • Experience with first-author publications at ISSCC, VLSI Symposium, CICC, or JSSC; patents in SerDes circuits or architecture.
  • Technical leadership of a multi-engineer SerDes design team through a full PHY delivery.
