title: APTM Yield Analysis/Device Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

At Intel, we create world-changing technology that improves the life of every person on the planet. By joining the Advanced Packaging Technology and Manufacturing (APTM) Yield Group, you will be part of a team tasked with the critical objective of driving yield and defect improvement across our entire advanced packaging portfolio. We solve highly complex physical and electrical problems to ensure our latest packaging technologies successfully transition from development into high-volume manufacturing.

We are seeking a APTM Yield Analysis/Device Engineer to drive technology development, transfers, and manufacturing ramps in Rio Rancho, New Mexico. In this role, you will analyze massive, multi-dimensional datasets to identify where manufacturing processes, test content, and inline metrologies must be optimized. Acting as a strategic technical advisor, you will set clear engineering priorities, lead cross-functional problem-solving initiatives, and directly influence our technology yield roadmap.

  • Data Synthesis & Insight Extraction: Extract insights from structured and unstructured factory datasets using statistical methods, machine learning, and tools like JMP or Python.
  • Failure Correlation: Correlate electrical and physical failure mechanisms by utilizing deep knowledge of Failure Analysis (FIFA), Design for Test (DFT), Sort/Test, and Integration/Process flows.
  • Defect System Optimization: Manage inline defect metrologies, evaluate detection capabilities, and drive inline defect reduction programs across the factory.
  • Technical Program Leadership: Lead a small group of engineers (direct or indirect) to execute experiments, resolve nonstandard yield events, and ensure smooth technology transfers to High-Volume Manufacturing (HVM).
  • Stakeholder Reporting & Collaboration: Deliver detailed technical reports summarizing yield and device health to upstream and downstream partners, establishing clear action plans to achieve best-in-class yield levels.

As a Successful Candidate, You Will Bring:

  • Leadership & Cross-Functional Influence: Instills a high-performing team culture with a willingness to lead, guide, and collaborate across diverse organizational boundaries.
  • Tolerance for Ambiguity & Flexibility: Adapts rapidly to changing priorities, new technical fields of study, and fluctuating business demands.

title: Intel Foundry Module Development Engineer - CMP
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Join Intel - and build a better tomorrow. Intel is in the midst of an exciting transformation, with a vision to create and extend computing technology to connect and enrich the lives of every person on Earth. So join us, and help us create the next generation of technologies that will shape the future for decades to come.

As the world's largest chip manufacturer, Intel strives to make every facet of semiconductor manufacturing state-of-the-art -- from semiconductor process development and manufacturing, through yield improvement to packaging, final test and optimization, and world class Supply Chain and facilities support. Employees in the Technology and Manufacturing Group are part of a worldwide network of design, development, manufacturing, and assembly/test facilities, all focused on utilizing the power of Moore's Law to bring smart, connected devices to every person on Earth.


Engineers within Intel's Logic Technology Development (LTD) organization are chartered with continuing to meet the challenge of Moore's Law in the 21st century. We innovate leading edge fabrication processes and continue to overcome seemingly impossible barriers as tolerances and specifications for building best-in-class computing devices become increasingly rigorous.


The role of a Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP) Process Development Engineer in LTD encompasses developing and sustaining planarization techniques for a variety of materials and architectures, enabling rapid miniaturization in the semiconductor industry and the mass production of integrated circuits. CMP techniques leverage physics, chemistry, materials science and surface science concepts, and exist at the intersection of these disciplines. As a result, our team has a diverse set of scientific backgrounds that relies on strong collaboration and shared learning.

  • Participating in the development of intellectual property
  • Developing the equipment and components necessary to leverage understanding gained in research (in collaboration with suppliers), identifying shortcomings, and proposing and evaluating modifications to mitigate issues or enable new capabilities
  • Overseeing unique CMP steps in a manufacturing line which integrates thousands of steps necessary for the manufacture of complex microprocessors, while simultaneously transferring the technology to counterparts in manufacturing sites across the globe

  • As a global leader in innovation and new technology, we foster a collaborative, supportive, and exciting environment where the brightest minds in the world come together to achieve exceptional results
  • We offer a competitive salary and financial benefits such as bonuses, life and disability insurance, opportunities to buy Intel stock at a discounted rate, and Intel stock awards (eligibility at the discretion of Intel Corporation)

title: Defect Review Technician
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Be a part of Intel's Advanced Packaging Command Center (APCC), the global command center for Advanced Packaging that provides remote capabilities, follow-on engineering, and operational support across Wafer Packaging Manufacturing (WPM). Through APCC, engineering expertise is focused to improve coordination across regions, drive standardization, and improve responsiveness, while strengthening end-to-end operational execution across regions and delivering consistent, high-quality execution at scale.

As the defect review technician, you will be instrumental in supporting global defect review activities, including defect classification, validation, and hold lot disposition. You will help maintain quality excellence while contributing to APCC's mission of delivering standardized, high-quality execution at scale. Your primary focus will be the accurate classification of defects captured by multiple inspection systems. Through precise defect classification, you will play a vital role in minimizing defect noise, driving systematic defect reduction initiatives, and maintaining the optimal balance between quality control and manufacturing efficiency.

Responsibilities will include but are not limited to
Defect Classification and Analysis:
• Review and Analyze defect images captured by diverse metrology tools.
• Accurately classify defects based on documented defect specification.
• Distinguish between true defects requiring disposition action and false positives or nuisance defects.
• Maintain proficiency across multiple inspection platforms and adapt classification criteria to different tool capabilities and imaging conditions

Defect Validation:
• Verify defect classifications against established criteria and specifications
• Partner with Layer Owner to ensure consistent defect categorization approaches
• Prevent over-rejection scenarios by accurately identifying non-critical defects and cosmetic variations that do not impact product performance.
• Avoid under-rejection situations by ensuring killed defects are properly identified and flagged for disposition.

Hold Lot Disposition:
• Ensure strict compliance in review and disposition of hold lots based on documented Out-of-Control Action Plans (OCAP)
• Ensure proper documentation and traceability of all disposition decisions.
• Collaborate with Layer Owner to update and refine OCAP procedures based on emerging defect patterns
• First Level Defect Analysis
• Perform comprehensive first level defect analysis as the initial point of technical review for all flagged defects.
• Document initial findings and recommendations to support Layer Owner analysis and decision-making processes.

Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position.
• Diploma in Engineering (Manufacturing, Mechatronics, Semiconductor Technology, Electronics, Mechanical or related disciplines), Diploma in Science Stream (Computer Science, Information Technology (IT), Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics & Statistics or related disciplines)
• 1+ years of working experience in semiconductor manufacturing, wafer fabrication, advanced packaging, metrology, inspection, quality, or manufacturing operations environments.
• Ability to work rotating shifts to provide continuous support across global manufacturing operations.
• Strong English communication skills, including reading, writing, and verbal communication.
• Proficiency in computer-based work and ability to maintain focus and accuracy while reviewing large volumes of inspection images.
• Ability to work at a workstation for extended periods while maintaining attention to detail and review quality.

Preferred Qualifications:
• Experience with defect classification, image review, defect inspection systems, or manufacturing quality processes is an added advantage.
• High attention to detail and commitment to quality standards.
• Effective communication and teamwork skills in a global, cross-functional environment.
• Willingness to learn new technologies, inspection platforms, and manufacturing processes.

We invite you to bring your technical expertise, curiosity, and passion for innovation to Intel, where you will have the opportunity to contribute to groundbreaking technologies and shape the future of semiconductor manufacturing.

descriptionHtml:

As a Die Sort Module Engineer, you will play an essential role in ensuring the efficiency and reliability of high-volume manufacturing equipment and processes that support Intel's advanced semiconductor production.

title: CPU Physical Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Performs physical design implementation of CPU designs from RTL to GDS to create a design database that is ready for manufacturing. Conducts all aspects of the CPU physical design flow including synthesis, place and route, clock tree synthesis, floor planning, static timing analysis, power/clock distribution, reliability, and power and noise analysis. Conducts verification and signoff including formal equivalence verification, static timing analysis, reliability verification, static and dynamic power integrity, layout verification, electrical rule checking, and structural design checking. Analyzes results and makes recommendations to improve current and future CPU microarchitectures closely collaborating with logic, circuit, architecture, and design automation teams. Possesses CPU specific expertise in various aspects of structural and physical design, including physical clock design, timing closure, coverage analysis, multiple power domain analysis, structured placement, routing, synthesis, and DFT. Works intimately with industry EDA vendors to build and enhance tool capabilities to design a highspeed, low power synthesizable CPU. Optimizes CPU design to improve product level parameters such as power, frequency, and area. Participates in the development and improvement of physical design methodologies and flow automation.

Qualifications:

As a CPU Physical Design Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in implementing high-performance, low-power CPU designs from RTL to GDSII. You will focus on detailed processes such as synthesis, placement, routing, timing analysis, and power optimization, enabling designs that meet stringent performance and efficiency targets. Your work will directly influence the success of Intel's next-generation CPUs and their manufacturing readiness, contributing to innovative advancements in computing technology.

You will join a dynamic team dedicated to designing Intel's latest high-performance CPUs using cutting-edge technologies. This group focuses on delivering innovative solutions that propel Intel's leadership in the semiconductor industry. Collaborating across multiple domains, the team drives groundbreaking designs that support Intel's mission of creating world-changing technologies to enrich the lives of every person on Earth.

Key Responsibilities
- Perform physical design implementation from RTL to GDSII, including synthesis, placement, routing, clock tree synthesis, and optimization.
- Conduct static timing analysis, power distribution analysis, and reliability verification to ensure design convergence and high manufacturability.
- Collaborate with logic, circuit, architecture, and automation teams to improve CPU microarchitectures and design methodologies.
- Work closely with industry-leading EDA vendors to enhance tool capabilities for high-speed, low-power CPU development.
- Optimize designs for power, frequency, and area, ensuring product-level parameter excellence.
- Participate in developing and improving physical design methodologies and flow automation for future projects.

Qualifications
- B. Tech or M. Tech degree in Electrical, Electronics with 3+ years of relevant experience.
- Technical expertise in synthesis, placement, clock tree synthesis (CTS), and routing tools, particularly using Synopsys and Cadence platforms.
- Proficiency in timing signoff, formal verification, and low-power design techniques.
- Solid understanding of submicron process node technologies and layout verification methods such as LVS/DRC.
- Skilled in power estimation, power optimization, and power delivery methodologies.

Preferred Qualifications
- Familiarity with scripting languages like Tcl, Perl, and Python for automating physical design workflows.
- Experience with Verilog or VHDL for hardware description and design execution.
- Strong communication skills, both verbal and written, for collaborative problem-solving.
- Demonstrated ability to work effectively in dynamic environments across geographies.
- Knowledge of innovative feature feasibility studies and SD flow methodologies.

Be part of a world-class team driving innovation in CPU design. Apply today to contribute to Intel's mission of shaping the future of technology.

title: SoC Design Verification Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

As a SoC Design Verification Engineer, you will be responsible for ensuring the functionality and reliability of Intel's cutting-edge server SoCs. You will perform functional logic verification and emulation validation to confirm designs meet specifications, uncover potential issues, and implement corrective measures. Through your technical contributions, you will play a vital role in advancing the development of next-generation Xeon server products, driving innovation and excellence in Intel's technology offerings.

Business group

You will join Intel's Data Center Group (DCG), which is dedicated to delivering leading-edge technologies and solutions for data centers that power the world's digital infrastructure. The team focuses on validating advanced Xeon server SoCs and IPs, providing innovative solutions that enhance performance, scalability, and efficiency. The group's mission aligns with Intel's broader vision of creating world-changing technology that enriches lives globally.

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform functional verification and emulation validation of integrated SoCs to ensure designs meet specifications.
  • Develop scalable and reusable block, subsystem, and SoC verification plans, test benches, and environments.
  • Execute verification plans, analyze system simulation models, and debug power and performance issues.
  • Root-cause failure issues and implement corrective measures in the pre-silicon environment.
  • Collaborate with architects, RTL developers, post-silicon teams, and physical design experts to enhance verification.
  • Document test plans and drive technical reviews with design and architecture teams.
  • Conduct regression and debug tests to integrate security activities and ensure comprehensive coverage.
  • Maintain and improve verification infrastructure and methodology, absorbing learnings from post-silicon validations.

title: SoC Logic Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

As a SoC Logic Design Engineer, you will actively contribute to the development, coding, and simulation of system-on-chip (SoC) designs. You will integrate logic from various IP blocks and subsystems into a complete chip design, ensuring power, performance, area, and timing goals are met. Your work will directly impact the delivery of cutting-edge, high-quality SoC solutions that drive advancements in technology and innovation.

The role is part of Intel's Data Center Group (DCG), which focuses on delivering advanced solutions that enable data-centric computing for global industries. As a member of this organization, you will collaborate on projects that shape the performance, security, and efficiency of Intel's data center offerings, contributing to the broader infrastructure required for modern computing needs.

The primary responsibilities for this role will include, but are not limited to:

  • Design and implement logic for SoC blocks and subsystems using register transfer level (RTL) coding techniques.
  • Integrate IP blocks and subsystems into full chip SoC designs, ensuring seamless functionality.
  • Conduct quality checks across various aspects of logic design, from RTL coding to timing, power, and area convergence.
  • Optimize logic designs to meet power, performance, area, and timing targets.
  • Review verification plans and resolve failing RTL tests to ensure correctness of design features. - Collaborate with IP providers to integrate and validate IPs for SoC-level designs.

  • Drive compliance with quality assurance standards for successful IP and SoC handoff.

title: Deep Learning Hardware Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact

Intel's Client AI Architecture team is seeking an Deep Learning Hardware Engineer to help shape future generations of Intel's Neural Processing Unit (NPU) architecture for AI PCs, Edge AI, Agentic AI, Physical AI, and multimodal foundation models.

In this role, you will work at the intersection of AI, computer architecture, and hardware-software co-design to optimize AI workloads and drive innovations in next-generation AI acceleration technologies. You will collaborate with architecture, software, compiler, and machine learning teams to develop high-performance, power-efficient AI solutions for Intel client platforms.

The ideal candidate has experience developing, optimizing, or deploying AI workloads on NPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, or related computing architectures. Experience with Intel NPUs, OpenVINO, AI software stacks, compiler technologies, AI inference optimization, and hardware-software co-design is highly desirable.

What You’ll Do

Key responsibilities will include but not limited to:

  • Contribute to the design and optimization of neural compute and AI accelerator architectures.
  • Develop and evaluate RTL implementations of hardware features supporting machine learning workloads.
  • Analyze AI models and workloads to identify performance, power, and efficiency opportunities.
  • Partner with architecture, software, and algorithm teams to define future hardware capabilities.
  • Support hardware-software co-design efforts to optimize AI solutions across the technology stack.
  • Evaluate neural network mapping strategies for accelerated inference execution.
  • Apply optimization techniques such as quantization, compression, pruning, and sparsity to improve AI efficiency.

  • Participate in technical innovation activities, including invention disclosures, patents, conference papers, and publications.

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact As a Module Engineer, you will be at the forefront of managing and optimizing high-volume manufacturing equipment and processes critical to the production of cutting-edge integrated circuits. You will conduct precise tests, implement improvements, and collaborate on technology transfers to ensure manufacturing excellence while meeting safety, quality, and cost goals. Your contributions will directly drive device miniaturization and process innovations that shape Intel's global manufacturing capabilities. Business Group Intel Corporation's Assembly Engineering group is a dynamic team focused on accelerating semiconductor manufacturing processes and technology development. The group plays an instrumental role in advancing high-volume production, fostering innovation, and enabling global technology transfers. By joining this team, you'll contribute to Intel's mission of creating world-changing technology that improves lives everywhere. Key Responsibilities - Manage critical high-volume manufacturing equipment and processes to support device miniaturization and integrated circuit production. - Conduct tests and measurements to ensure control over critical dimensions and defectivity within the production line. - Recommend and implement modifications to optimize production techniques and enhance manufacturing efficiencies. - Execute maintenance and repair activities for equipment and relevant module components. - Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on safety, quality, cost, productivity, defects, and yield. - Collaborate with equipment suppliers to resolve technical issues and implement key improvements. - Develop and optimize systems for excursion prevention and discrepancy detection in materials and processes. - Participate in technology transfer and audit activities to ensure aligned standards across global manufacturing sites. - Lead equipment installation, conversion, and qualification during factory ramps, ensuring safety and quality standards are met.

- Bachelor's degree or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Automation Control, Electronics, Data Science, Materials Science & Engineering, Metallurgy, Chemical Engineering or a related physical science/engineering discipline.

- Minimum 1–3 years of experience in semiconductor packaging, electronics manufacturing, or high-volume Surface Mount Technology (SMT) assembly environments.

- Proficient in both spoken and written English communication.

- Working knowledge of BGA package assembly and SMT manufacturing processes.

- Experience in yield improvement, quality engineering, and manufacturing problem-solving.

- Knowledge of BGA package assembly and SMT manufacturing processes.

- Knowledge of FMEA, PFMEA, Control Plans, SPC, and corrective/preventive action methodologies.

- Knowledge of data analysis tools, scripting and programing such as JMP,  SQL, Power BI, Python.

- Strong troubleshooting, analytical, and root-cause investigation skills.

- Ability to work effectively across multiple engineering disciplines and manufacturing organizations.

Additional preferred qualifications include:

- Experience supporting automated inspection systems and vision-based manufacturing equipment.

- Familiarity with quality methodologies such as Six Sigma, DMAIC, 8D, FMEA, and Statistical Process Control.

- Experience driving yield improvement projects in semiconductor or electronics manufacturing.

You bring relevant experience in one or more of the following areas:

- Hands-on experience with AutoCAD, Solidworks, with the ability to produce designs for fabrication.

- Hands-on experience sustaining automated optical inspection, visual inspection, or automated manufacturing equipment.

- Hands-on experience sustaining, programming, and troubleshooting -automated stencil printing systems, 3D Solder Paste Inspection (SPI), multizone reflow ovens, and aqueous/chemical deflux cleaning modules.

- Process Metallurgy & Joint Reliability: Working knowledge of BGA package assembly, lead-free solder metallurgy (SAC alloys, low-temperature Bismuth), intermetallic compound (IMC) growth control, and package warpage due to Coefficient of Thermal Expansion (CTE) mismatch.

- Hands-on experience with industrial imaging hardware, High-Precision 2D/3D Metrology.

- Proven experience with successful projects with main task of developing automation script and app that improve manufacturing processes (including process optimization, add-in detection capabilities using image processing / ML / AI).

At Intel, we create world-changing technology that improves the life of every person on the planet. title: Compiler Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Compiler Engineering team in Data Center Group at Intel has an opportunity available for a Compiler Engineer.


At Intel, we are building the next generation of software technologies that unlock the potential of heterogeneous computing. Our compiler technologies help developers harness CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators through high-performance, portable software. You will contribute to an ecosystem that advances performance, scalability, reliability, and developer productivity for AI, HPC, and other demanding workloads, while supporting Intel's commitment to contributing to and collaborating with open-source communities.


The Intel Compiler Engineering Team develops LLVM-based C, C++, SYCL, Triton, MLIR, Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), and Fortran compiler technologies for Intel processor platforms, including CPUs and GPUs. The team works across the compiler stack and in close collaboration with hardware architecture teams, covering language front ends, intermediate representations, optimization, code generation, debug information, runtimes, offload support, quality, and developer tooling. This work connects Intel hardware and compiler capabilities with AI frameworks and software ecosystems such as PyTorch, inference engines, and machine-learning models.


As a Compiler Engineer, you will play a critical role in advancing compiler technologies that deliver exceptional performance and scalability across Intel architectures.


Your responsibilities will include:

  • Designing, developing, testing, debugging, and maintaining advanced compiler technologies and software components.
  • Driving the implementation of new compiler features and resolving software defects.
  • Analyzing real-world applications, workloads, and benchmarks to identify optimization opportunities.
  • Improving the performance and efficiency of compiler-generated code for Intel CPU architectures.
  • Conducting functional, performance, scalability, and stress testing to ensure product quality and reliability.
  • Partnering with hardware architects and platform teams to enable new processor capabilities.
  • Collaborating across global engineering, validation, and performance teams to deliver high-quality products.
  • Contributing to open-source compiler initiatives and industry standards.

Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.


Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Informatics, or a related technical field.
  • 3+ years of professional software development experience and advanced knowledge in C/C++.
  • Strong background in object-oriented programming, algorithms, and data structures.
  • Experience optimizing software for CPU performance and efficiency.
  • Excellent analytical, debugging, and problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master's degree or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline.
  • Proven ability to work independently.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills within global engineering environments.
  • Experience with vectorization technologies and parallel programming models such as OpenMP.
  • Experience with compiler development using LLVM or similar compiler frameworks.
  • Knowledge of assemblers, linkers, and low-level system software.
  • Strong understanding of compiler optimizations, code generation, and CPU architecture.
  • Familiarity with performance profiling and analysis tools such as perf or equivalent solutions.

Requirements listed would be obtained through a combination of industry relevant job experience, internship experiences and or schoolwork/classes/research.

title: Quality Manager
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Join Intel Foundry Construction and Sourcing in building the world's largest semiconductor manufacturing factories across the globe. The future is what we build.

Our enterprise manages a portfolio of capital projects on-site with a large contractor workforce that encompasses outsourced general contractors, A/E firms, and key trade companies in the Semiconductor Construction Industry.
The scope of our work includes but is not limited to New Wafer Fabrication factories (Fabs), Fab Conversions, Process Tools Install, Infrastructure, and Progressive Build.

We are looking for world-class technical talent to join our team. If you enjoy working with the latest technology in a rewarding, fast-paced environment, this is the right place for you. Everywhere you go, you'll find an opportunity to make a difference. In any given workday, you will be given the responsibility to innovate and create an impact on our business. This onsite position reports to the Director of Construction

The Quality Assurance/Quality Control Manager will be responsible for the Intel site construction quality assurance program and project quality systems to support all areas of semiconductor construction projects. The Quality QA/QC manager will also provide oversight to Intel's direct contracted 3rd party inspection firms (geotechnical, civil, structural, architectural, mechanical, electrical, and process).

Responsibilities will include but are not limited to:

  • Develop and implement a total and complete Construction Quality Management Plan
  • Develop a 3rd party resource plan to include QAR firm, high purity analytical test firm, Exhaust Test and Balance firm, Special Inspection Agencies, Gas and Chem system technician team, Life Safety system startup and test team
  • Develop a total resource cost forecast for all programs on the site and gain approval from all Program Managers and Finance.
  • Review and approve the Design-Builder (DB), Construction Manager (CM), or Multi Prime trade contractors (MP) Quality Assurance Plan (QAP) and Construction Project Execution Plan (CPEP).
  • Respond to and document quality issue notifications to DB, CM, or MP, ensuring onsite construction work conforms to drawings codes and specifications, improving the quality of construction through our 3rd party and/or contracts.
  • Ensure DB, CM, or MP contractors perform to quality assurance plans (inspection checklists, indicator, and non-conformance reports); ensure is meeting contracted metrics and the systems provide Intel management contracted metrics and updates.
  • Ensure the 3rd Party is performing work to Scope of Work (SOW) (individual certifications, fab shop audits, etc.); ensure is performing to budget and is not incurring unnecessary charges.
  • Review 3rd parties Timecards (periodically).
  • Review 3rd Party monthly billing in Tracker.
  • Review Change orders as needed for scope not identified for 3rd parties.
  • Understand contract language and ensure DB, CM or MP is working to the Quality General Requirements.
  • Read and Improve SOW's for gaps.
  • Quality management by walking around - Onsite walks to ensure inspectors, DB, CM, or MP and contractors are performing to Intel Master Construction Specifications (IMCS) and contracted documents.
  • Attend QIA (quality incident analysis) when needed.
  • Work/Develop cost reduction efficiencies with trades and project teams and stakeholders.
  • Proactive in mitigating issues before they occur.
  • Quarterly assessment of DB, CM, or MP quality program with identifying issues to be corrected as they occur.
  • Meet with 3rd party teams as frequently as needed based on the frequency of quality issues or at a minimum of every 2 weeks.
  • Ensure quality inspections by either 3rd party or AHJ are robust and are being entered appropriately by the DB, CM, or MP into a tracking mechanism and KPIs are generated and reviewed at a minimum of every month.
  • Able to work with cross-site VF teams to develop and drive Best known methods (BKMS), learnings, efficiencies, and standardization across the Virtual Factory (VF). Report issues that could impact the VF.

The successful candidate should exhibit the following behavioral traits:

  • Quality as a value, right first time.
  • Communicator and written presentation skills.
  • Negotiation and conflict management skills.
  • Lead teams and projects with minimal supervision.
  • Willingness to build and maintain strong relationships with all project stakeholders.
  • Skills to drive project deliverables.
  • Willingness to work with varied individuals and disciplines with Intel, DB, CM, or MP and contractors.
  • Proactiveness in mitigating issues before they occur.
  • Project management skills and leadership ability to manage multiple firms.

This position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship.

title: Senior Process Integration Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
As a Process Integration Development Engineer, you will drive revolutionary advancements in substrate manufacturing technologies, ensuring smooth and efficient integration processes for next-generation packaging solutions. Your primary focus will be working closely with supplier engineering teams to develop and optimize processes, manage capacity, improve yield and enhance lead times. This role is pivotal to Intel's ability to deliver cutting-edge solutions to meet growing customer demand on EMIB-T advanced packaging solutions.

Business group
The role resides within Intel Corporation's Substrate Packaging Technology Development (SPTD) Dept and in the Substrate Integration Asia group, which focuses on advancing substrate packaging technologies to enable innovative solutions for heterogeneous chip architectures. The group collaborates with global teams and suppliers to deliver scalable manufacturing processes, supporting Intel's broader goals of technology leadership and innovation in advanced packaging.

Key Responsibilities
• Engage with supplier engineering teams and Intel's US integration group to advance substrate technologies and manage critical process interactions.
• Monitor, optimize, and enhance bottleneck processes to reduce throughput time (TPT) and improve efficiencies.
• Oversee schedules for product and test vehicle (TV) deliveries, resolving issues to meet aggressive on-time delivery (OTD) goals.
• Analyze substrate lead times, develop reduction roadmaps, and ensure quarterly lead time targets are met.
• Ensure supplier adherence to Process Control System (PCS) commitments.
• Collaborate with internal teams to design and implement factory certification plans focused on yield improvement.
• Develop milestone-driven micro-schedules for new factory startups, ensuring supplier compliance with startup timelines.
• Lead qualification activities and monitor ramp indicators to ensure seamless production ramp-up for new capacity.
• Influence strategic decision-making at supplier management levels through data-driven insights and recommendations.

• Expectation is for candidate to be at supplier factory on-site for minimum of 4 days a week.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications
• Bachelor's degree in Science or Engineering with 10+ years, a Master's degree with 8+ years, or a PhD with 6+ years of work experience in a relevant field.
• 8+ years of experience in fab back-end or substrate manufacturing process development.
• Proficiency in supplier management, yield improvement and lead time analysis, with hands-on experience in structured problem-solving and supplier influence.

Preferred Qualifications
• Expertise in substrate process building blocks, including component embedding, laser drilling, dielectric lamination, lithography, multi-metal electrolytic plating, defect inspection/metrology, and electrical testing.
• Proven experience with process tool qualification in TD/ramp or HVM environments.
• Familiarity with factory operations, substrates, manufacturing, process engineering, and yield improvement.
• Fluent English communication skills, with exceptional presentation abilities and confidence to engage with supplier management.

title: Sort Interface Pathfinding and Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel Corporation is one of the world's leading semiconductor companies, driving innovation across computing, connectivity, and artificial intelligence. With a bold vision to shape the future of technology, Intel is transforming how the world processes, stores, and communicates data. Our Advanced Packaging ,Test and Manufacturing (APTM) organization is at the forefront of this transformation, delivering industry-leading packaging and test technologies that power products across Client, Data Center, AI, Networking, and External Foundry markets. At Intel, we believe the next big thing starts with you.

We are seeking a talented and driven Sort Interface Pathfinding and Development Engineer to join our Sort Interface Development team in Oregon. In this high-impact role, you will pioneer breakthrough silicon interface probing & test solutions that enable best-in-class die and wafer sort capabilities across leading-edge process nodes and advanced heterogeneous packaging platforms — including EMIB, EMIB-T, Foveros, and Foveros Direct.

As Intel scales its Open System Foundry and OSAT (Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test) business model, you will play an instrumental role in establishing world-class, customer-ready sort interface capabilities. You will lead electro-mechanical pathfinding, test hardware development, customer and supplier technical co-design, and probing process qualification to support both Intel's internal product roadmap and external Foundry customers.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Formulate and execute rigorous Design of Experiments (DOE) to optimize and qualify next-generation probing technologies and contact architectures for wafer and die sort operations
  • Serve as the lead technical liaison for Foundry and OSAT customers, translating complex chiplet and package requirements into scalable sort interface specifications
  • Author industry-standard sort design rules and Interface Design Kits (IDKs) to streamline ecosystem integration for external fabless customers and design partners
  • Collaborate with customer design and DFT teams to architect test interface hardware, resolve technical gaps, and synchronize testability roadmaps
  • Partner with global Test Solution vendors and PCB suppliers to pioneer state-of-the-art probing capabilities
  • Direct supplier and pathfinding initiatives to align vendor roadmaps with internal efficiency and performance goals
  • Drive supplier accountability and manufacturing readiness to guarantee on-time hardware delivery for critical New Product Introductions (NPI)

As a Successful Candidate, You Will Bring:

  • Collaborative mindset — you thrive working across cross-functional teams, customers, and global suppliers
  • Strong communicator — you can translate highly technical concepts into clear, actionable specifications for diverse audiences
  • Analytical thinker — you approach complex problems with curiosity, structure, and data-driven decision-making
  • Self-starter — you take initiative, drive projects forward, and hold yourself and others accountable
  • Customer-focused — you understand the importance of building trust and delivering value to external partners
  • Adaptable — you are comfortable navigating ambiguity and evolving priorities in a fast-paced, cutting-edge environment
  • Continuous learner — you stay current with emerging technologies and proactively seek opportunities to grow

If you are passionate about pushing the boundaries of advanced packaging and test technology, and you want to make a meaningful impact on products that power the world's most advanced computing systems, we want to hear from you.

descriptionHtml:

Job Description: 

At Intel, we create world-changing technology that improves the life of every person on the planet. This position is part of Intel's Advanced Packaging Technology Manufacturing (APTM) organization, which is dedicated to advancing and scaling innovative semiconductor packaging solutions. APTM's mission is to deliver state-of-the-art technologies that empower mobile, edge, and high-performance computing applications, while supporting Intel's broader goals of technological leadership and global customer success.

We are seeking a Senior Packaging Module Development Engineer to join our team in Chandler, Arizona. In this role, you will play a critical part in developing and optimizing the semiconductor packaging processes and equipment that drive Intel's next-generation roadmap. You will develop advanced assembly processes, design rigorous reliability testing simulations, and drive standardized manufacturing configurations across global Intel factories. This role requires regular onsite presence to collaborate hands-on with cutting-edge equipment, materials, and development tools in our state-of-the-art labs.

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Role Overview:

The E2E Finance Architect will own the enterprise Finance solution architecture across SAP Financial Accounting and Controlling (FICO), subledger accounting, product costing, fixed assets, Project Accounting, SAP Profitability and Performance Management (PaPM), and SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC) for Financial Planning and Analysis (FP and A).

This role will provide architecture leadership for the current IAO transformation and maintain long-term ownership of the Finance technology roadmap after implementation. The architect will partner with Accounting, Manufacturing Finance, FP and A, business process owners, IT, and implementation partners to deliver integrated, scalable, and controlled Finance solutions.

Key Responsibilities:

End-to-end solution architecture ownership: Define and govern the Finance target architecture, solution designs, integration patterns, and architectural standards. Resolve cross-functional design issues and ensure consistency across accounting, costing, profitability, planning, and reporting.

Accounting and subledgers: Lead solution architecture across general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, intercompany accounting, bank accounting, financial close, and subledger-to-general-ledger reconciliation. Ensure consistent financial data, reporting dimensions, and auditability.

  • Product costing and manufacturing finance: Solution Architect standard and actual costing, Material Ledger, inventory valuation, work in process, overhead allocation, production variances, and profitability analysis. Address semiconductor requirements across wafer fabrication, assembly and test, yield and scrap impacts, and internal or outsourced manufacturing.
  • Fixed assets and Project Accounting: Own solution architecture for asset acquisition, assets under construction, capitalization, depreciation, transfers, and retirement. Integrate project structures, budgeting, commitments, cost collection, and settlement with fixed assets and financial accounting.
  • SAP PaPM: Define solution architecture for cost allocations, profitability models, business-driver calculations, and scenario analysis. Ensure transparent calculation logic, traceable results, and reconciliation with financial source systems.
  • SAC for FP and A: Lead solution architecture for budgeting, forecasting, long-range planning, and management reporting, including operating expenses, capital expenditures, workforce costs, and integrated financial statements. Connect planning models with actuals and operational drivers.
  • Treasury: Lead solution architecture for cash and liquidity management, bank account management, payments and bank connectivity, cash forecasting, and treasury risk management. Ensure integration with financial accounting, banking platforms, and FP and A to support accurate cash visibility, treasury accounting, and financial controls.
  • Tax with ONE SOURCE: Own solution architecture and integration between SAP and Thomson Reuters ONESOURCE for indirect tax determination, calculation, and compliance reporting, including sales and use tax, VAT, and GST. Ensure accurate tax postings, reconciliation, and auditability across procurement, sales, and intercompany transactions.
  • Current business transformation: Provide design authority through solution validation, build, integration testing, user acceptance testing, data migration, cutover, and stabilization. Review partner deliverables, resolve critical design gaps, and ensure business and operational readiness.
  • Post-transformation ownership: Maintain the Finance architecture roadmap, govern enhancements and releases, guide resolution of complex production issues, reduce technical debt, and drive continuous improvement. Establish effective knowledge transfer and support ownership.
  • Integration, controls, and leadership: Ensure Finance integration with procurement, sales, manufacturing, supply chain, projects, and enterprise data platforms. Embed financial controls, data governance, security requirements, and reconciliation into designs. Mentor solution leads and communicate solution architectural decisions and trade-offs to senior stakeholders.

title: Client Electrical Validation Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact

As an Electrical Validation Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring the reliability and performance of Intel's next-generation silicon products. You will actively validate circuit analog performance, analyze electrical signal integrity compliance, and ensure system-level margins for stable operation. This hands-on role directly contributes to the development of high-quality products that delight customers while meeting production and industry standards.


Business group

The Electrical Validation team is part of Intel Corporation, supporting Intel's commitment to delivering innovative and high-performing silicon solutions. This team works on validating and debugging integrated products, leveraging state-of-the-art laboratory equipment to ensure product quality and reliability.

Their focus on multidisciplinary research and collaboration plays a vital role in supporting Intel's broader mission to deliver cutting-edge technology.


Key Responsibilities

  • Define electrical validation strategies for IO interfaces to achieve optimized analog performance and meet product production goals.
  • Validate circuit analog performance, electrical signal integrity compliance to industry-standard specifications, and system-level margins for stable operation.
  • Conduct multidisciplinary research in the design, testing, and validation of IO and mixed-signal architectures, including datacom applications, custom Intel interfaces, and RF systems.
  • Develop procedures, analyses, and designs for validation infrastructure and systems margin validation.
  • Perform root cause analysis and resolve functional and triage failures for electrical issues.
  • Test interactions between various electrical design features using validation infrastructure.
  • Apply knowledge of Design for Testability (DFT) and Design for Manufacturability (DFM) to collaborate with architecture, design, and pre-silicon validation teams.
  • Prepare validation specifications, evaluate intellectual property (IP), and generate comprehensive test reports.
  • Analyze internal and external customer returns to enhance yields and drive test escape closure

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications, you must possess the minimum qualifications below to be initially considered for this position.

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field,

  • 2+ years of hands-on experience in:
    • Digital-analog design, CPU architecture, and microarchitecture.
      programming languages such as Python or C-programming.

title: Senior Product Failure Analysis Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role


Intel Foundry is seeking a highly skilled Senior Product Failure Analysis Engineer to lead complex failure investigations that drive product quality, manufacturing excellence, and technology development across advanced semiconductor technologies.

In this role, you will leverage deep expertise in semiconductor devices, electrical characterization, physical failure analysis, and root cause investigation to identify and solve challenging product and process issues. You will partner across engineering, manufacturing, yield, process integration, quality, reliability, and design teams to develop corrective actions that improve technology robustness and accelerate product success.

This position offers the opportunity to influence the development of future technologies while advancing Intel Foundry's commitment to delivering world-class semiconductor solutions.

What You Will Do

Key responsibilities will include but not limited to:

  • Lead complex failure analysis investigations involving semiconductor devices, integrated circuits, packages, and manufacturing processes.
  • Develop and execute comprehensive failure analysis strategies using electrical, physical, material, and structural characterization techniques.
  • Perform root cause analysis of yield, reliability, performance, and customer-return failures.
  • Utilize fault isolation and failure localization methodologies to identify defect mechanisms and process interactions.
  • Drive corrective and preventive actions through collaboration with manufacturing, process engineering, design, product engineering, quality, and reliability organizations.
  • Define and implement advanced methodologies, tools, and workflows that improve failure analysis effectiveness and throughput.
  • Provide technical leadership during technology transfers, manufacturing ramps, process qualifications, and new product introductions.
  • Analyze large datasets and laboratory findings to identify trends, risks, and opportunities for continuous improvement.
  • Document findings and present technical recommendations to senior engineering and business stakeholders.
  • Mentor junior engineers and contribute to the development of organizational failure analysis expertise.
  • Leverage data analytics and AI-enabled tools to improve investigation efficiency, knowledge sharing, and decision-making.

Behavioral Traits that we are looking for:


  • Strong analytical thinking and structured problem-solving skills.
  • Intellectual curiosity and a passion for understanding complex failure mechanisms.
  • Technical leadership and ability to influence without direct authority.
  • Ownership mindset with accountability for delivering results.
  • Effective communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical findings into actionable recommendations.
  • Collaboration and partnership across global, cross-functional teams.
  • Adaptability and resilience in fast-paced, highly technical environments.
  • Continuous learning mindset and willingness to embrace emerging technologies and methodologies.
  • Attention to detail while maintaining focus on broader business objectives.
  • Customer-focused approach to quality, reliability, and operational excellence.

title: AMHS Intelligent Systems Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Drive the Automated Circulatory Engine of Intel Foundry

At Intel Foundry Technology & Manufacturing, we design, build, and scale the physical and digital infrastructure that powers the future of computing. Automated Material Handling Systems (AMHS) serve as the circulatory system of Intel’s high-volume manufacturing facilities, enabling continuous 24x7 wafer transport and reticle delivery across our Gordon Moore Park at Ronler Acres and Aloha campuses.


We are seeking an experienced Manufacturing Systems Software Development Engineer to take ownership of real-time cleanroom automation architectures, high-availability control software, and data-driven factory throughput. Operating at the convergence of distributed software systems, factory physics, and advanced cleanroom operations, you will directly influence wafer cycle times, tool availability, and operational yield for next-generation process nodes.


What You Will Do

  • AMHS Equipment Ownership: Serve as the technical expert responsible for ensuring optimal performance, reliability, and continuous improvement of the AMHS within the manufacturing environment. Maintain system uptime targets based on organizational goals, through proactive monitoring, preventive maintenance execution, and rapid response to Major Impacts (MI), while simultaneously driving innovation through the evaluation and implementation of new technologies.   Flexibility to participate in an operational on-call rotation to support 24x7 manufacturing escalations.
  • Architect & Deliver Factory Automation Software Integration: Design, integrate, and deploy robust end-to-end software solutions for 300mm wafer transport, reticle management, and automated stocker systems across high-volume cleanroom environments
  • Optimize Distributed Control Systems: Debug, tune, and sustain multi-tier automation platforms—spanning low-level firmware, OS configurations, database interfaces, and real-time scheduling algorithms—to maximize tool availability and eliminate dispatch bottlenecks.
  • Lead New Product Introductions (NPI): Partner cross-functionally with IT Platforms, Networks, Middleware, and Module Equipment Engineering to qualify and integrate new automation capabilities with zero operational disruption to high-volume manufacturing line balance.
  • Own Complex Escalations & Root Cause Analysis: Function as the module technical authority for system excursions; drive structured Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and implement robust permanent corrective and preventive actions (CAPA).
  • Champion Fab Data Intelligence: Develop performant SQL queries, Python automation routines, and PowerBI dashboards to monitor fleet health, analyze telemetry logs, and proactively eliminate systemic failures before they manifest as tool downtime.
  • Continuous Improvement: Strive to improve corrective and preventive maintenance overload from maintenance by continually looking for opportunities to improve maintenance through innovative ideas and enhancements. All improvements need to be driven through the DPO and DPG to ensure all sites benefit through these CIPs.
  • Project Management: Complete equipment qualification in accordance with the appropriate qual specifications, contribute to global knowledge revisions based on ongoing learning and lessons learned during system qualifications. Willingness to work in a cleanroom environment (including walking long fab distances and working at heights around automated track superstructures).
  • Execute Global Standards: Collaborate with Intel’s worldwide AMHS engineering network to maintain alignment with Copy Exactly! (CE!) protocols and industry SEMI standards.

Why Join Intel Foundry?

  • Direct Impact at Global Scale: Your code directly governs real-time wafer movement and operational KPIs across one of the most sophisticated semiconductor manufacturing ecosystems on earth.
  • World-Class Automation Ecosystem: Direct, hands-on access to multi-million-dollar automated storage, overhead transport (OHT), and robotics infrastructure engineered alongside premier global equipment partners.
  • Accelerated Technical Leadership: Direct mentorship and collaboration with Intel Fellows and Senior Principal Engineers on an accelerated path toward technical distinction.

title: Senior PDK Physical Verification Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Shape the Future of Advanced Semiconductor Technology at Intel


Join Intel's Design Technology Platform (DTP) organization and become part of a world-class team enabling the next generation of semiconductor innovation. In this highly visible role, you will develop and deploy advanced density fill methodologies and Process Design Kit (PDK) solutions that directly impact Intel's most advanced technology nodes and product designs.


Working at the intersection of process technology, physical verification, and design automation, you will collaborate with leading engineers across Intel and the EDA ecosystem to solve complex manufacturability challenges, improve design productivity, and enable breakthrough technologies. Your contributions will influence how future products are designed and manufactured, helping Intel maintain technology leadership in an increasingly competitive industry.


What You'll Do

  • Lead the development, implementation, and validation of density fill solutions within advanced Process Design Kits (PDKs).
  • Develop algorithmic solutions using industry-leading physical verification platforms, including Calibre, Synopsys ICV, and Cadence Pegasus, to ensure density compliance and manufacturability across advanced process technologies.
  • Collaborate with process integration teams, design rule owners, product design engineers, and customers to define requirements and deliver state-of-the-art solutions.
  • Drive automation initiatives that improve engineering efficiency, solution scalability, and deployment across multiple design environments.
  • Design and develop robust validation frameworks, test suites, and qualification methodologies to ensure high-quality tool and rule deck releases.
  • Advance innovative physical verification methodologies to address emerging challenges associated with technology scaling.
  • Partner closely with external EDA vendors to influence and deploy next-generation tool capabilities and methodologies.
  • Develop technical documentation, training materials, and best practices that enable successful adoption across Intel's design community.
  • Serve as a technical expert and contribute to strategic initiatives that shape Intel's design enablement roadmap.

Ideal Candidate Background

We are particularly interested in candidates who have developed physical verification methodologies, density-fill solutions, or PDK technologies within:

  • Semiconductor Foundries.
  • Integrated Device Manufacturers (IDMs).
  • Advanced Packaging and OSAT Organizations.
  • EDA Software Companies.
  • Design Enablement or CAD Teams supporting advanced-node development.

Core Competencies

  • Excellent communication and technical presentation skills, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts into actionable solutions.
  • Strong problem-solving, debugging, and analytical skills.
  • Strong understanding of technology scaling challenges and their impact on physical verification and design rule development.

Qualifications:

The Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position.  Minimum qualifications listed below would be obtained through a combination of industry relevant job experience, internship experience and / or schoolwork/classes/research. The preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field with 6+ years of relevant experience;
    • OR - Master's degree with 5+ years of experience.
    • OR - PhD with 2+ years of experience.
  • 4+ years of hands-on experience with at least one industry-standard physical verification platform such as Calibre, ICV, or Pegasus, including methodology development, rule deck debugging, validation, or production deployment.
  • 3+ years of experience developing, maintaining, or debugging physical verification rule decks using SVRF, TVF, PXL, PVL, or Tcl-based verification environments.
  • Experience with semiconductor process technology, device physics, design rules, and manufacturability requirements.
  • Experience developing algorithmic solutions for physical design and manufacturing challenges at advanced technology nodes.
  • Experience with with Unix/Linux operating systems and engineering computing environments.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 4+ years of direct experience developing, deploying, or supporting density fill methodologies for advanced semiconductor technologies at 16nm and below.
  • Proven expertise in fill rule implementation, density optimization, and manufacturing-driven design methodologies.
  • Deep experience with physical verification flows, including DRC, density analysis, fill verification, and process-aware design enablement.
  • Experience supporting or developing solutions for leading foundry, IDM, or advanced process technologies.
  • Familiarity with custom layout environments such as Cadence Virtuoso or Synopsys Custom Designer.
  • Experience collaborating across multidisciplinary engineering teams and external partners to deliver innovative solutions.
  • Experience leading technical initiatives, driving process improvements, or influencing product and methodology roadmaps.
  • Prior experience with semiconductor foundries, IDMs, OSATs, or EDA vendors developing physical verification methodologies, density-fill solutions, PDKs, or design-for-manufacturing technologies is highly desirable.

Why Intel?

This role offers a rare opportunity to work on technology challenges that influence the future of semiconductor manufacturing. You'll collaborate with experts across process technology, CAD, physical design, and EDA while helping define methodologies used across Intel's most advanced products. If you are passionate about solving complex physical verification and manufacturability problems at scale, this role offers both significant technical depth and broad organizational impact. Join Intel and make a direct impact on the next generation of semiconductor innovation.

title: Strategic / Development Industrial Engineer (Senior Individual Contributor)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Foundry Capacity Optimization (FCO) and Strategic Planning organization is seeking a visionary, high-impact Grade 10 Strategic / Development Industrial Engineer to lead the next era of operational transformation across our planning and capacity ecosystems.

As a senior individual contributor reporting directly to the VP/GM of Foundry Capacity Optimization, you will partner closely with Staff Area Managers (AMs), Principal Engineers, and senior FCSP stakeholders to architect and execute a multi-year digital and operational transformation roadmap.

Your charter is clear: radically increase the strategic impact, velocity, and analytical depth of the organization without expanding headcount. You will eliminate manual data manipulation, disparate spreadsheet modeling, and repetitive reconciliation, enabling FCO engineers to focus on solving high-value, complex semiconductor capacity and customer delivery challenges.

Core Responsibilities

1. Transformation Roadmap and Systems Architecture

• Define, architect, and deliver the end-to-end Foundry Capacity Optimization (FCO) Digital Transformation Roadmap, aligning long-range planning (LRP), capacity modeling, tool allocation, and operational execution systems.

• Translate complex foundry operational workflows into automated, scalable, and resilient enterprise system requirements.

• Establish quantifiable efficiency and productivity metrics to track manual labor reduction, cycle-time compression, and decision-velocity improvements across planning cycles.

2. AI, Machine Learning, and Automation Implementation

• Spearhead the adoption of modern Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and Generative AI technologies to automate complex decision-support pipelines, including automated tool mismatch identification, capacity balancing, and yield/mix scenario modeling.

• Partner directly with Foundry Automation, Enterprise IT, software development groups, and specialized third-party technology consultants to rapidly prototype, validate, and deploy production-grade solutions.

• Drive the transition from fragmented desktop spreadsheets and static databases to unified, low-latency, automated enterprise planning engines.

3. Data Integration and Elimination of Manual Reconciliation

• Eliminate the time engineers spend manually mapping, transforming, stitching, and reconciling disparate fab, demand, and tool datasets.

• Partner with data engineering and business intelligence teams to establish a robust single source of truth for fab capacity, equipment lines, capital planning, and customer allocations.

• Institutionalize automated exception handling, data anomaly detection, and self-healing data pipelines across critical planning feeds.

4. Industry Benchmarking and External Innovation

• Actively benchmark peer semiconductor foundries and adjacent hyper-capital-intensive industries, including advanced aerospace, automotive, display, and energy, for state-of-the-art planning systems, algorithmic optimization, and operational efficiency methodologies.

• Evaluate commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) platforms versus proprietary internal builds and develop disciplined business cases, ROI models, and technology roadmaps for executive review.

• Bring external best practices into Foundry Capacity Optimization (FCO), fostering a culture of continuous modernization, technological curiosity, and systems thinking.

5. Stakeholder Alignment and Change Leadership

• Function as a trusted technical advisor and thought partner to Staff AMs, Principal Engineers, and executive management.

• Drive operational change management across diverse engineering disciplines, ensuring seamless adoption of new digital tools, automated interfaces, and standardized workflows.

• Mentor and upskill the broader engineering cohort in modern analytical tools, automation scripts, and systems-level problem solving.


Required Skills and Experience

• Proficiency with data analysis and automation tools such as SQL, Python, Excel, business intelligence platforms, or similar technologies.

• Experience developing capacity models, facility layouts, or manufacturing systems.

• Knowledge of supply chain processes, production systems, or factory operations.

• Familiarity with forecasting methodologies and statistical techniques.

Preferred Skills and Experience

• Experience within high-volume semiconductor manufacturing, semiconductor foundry operations, or complex wafer fab supply chains, including familiarity with fab toolsets, lithography/etch/thin-film constraints, cycle-time dynamics, and capacity models.

• Familiarity with commercial supply chain/capacity planning suites such as Kinaxis, Anaplan, SAP IBP, and Blue Yonder, as well as modern business intelligence architectures.

• Experience engaging with and directing external technology vendors, systems integrators, and management consultants to execute technology pilots and full-scale rollouts.

• Demonstrated expertise in Lean, Six Sigma, Design for Excellence, or formal Business Process Re-engineering (BPR).

Qualifications:

• Bachelor's/BS degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Operations Research, or a related field.

• 12+ years of experience with a Bachelor's degree, 8+ years with a Master's degree, or 6+ years with a PhD in a relevant domain.

title: Process Integration Development Engineer - Defect Metrology
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Embark with us on a journey of growth and transformation as we create exceptionally engineered technology and bring AI everywhere. As a valued team member, your adaptability and attention to detail will contribute to our drive for results and relentless pursuit of quality, ensuring we meet our customers' needs with precision.

Join us and build on our legacy of innovation and collaboration as we deliver world‑changing technology that improves the life of every person on the planet.

Life at Intel: https://jobs.intel.com/en/life-at-intel

At Intel's Logic Technology Development (LTD), we have continued to extend Moore's law to be world leaders in computing technology. To achieve the necessary scaling of our semiconductor manufacturing process, we have led the industry in developing enhancements such as strained silicon for carrier transport enhancement, high-k metal gates, FinFETs, and next-generation Gate-All-Around architectures. LTD has been at the center of every new development that has kept Moore's Law moving forward.


Defect Metrology plays a key role in the development of every new silicon process technology. Our analysis builds the plan that allows LTD to take technology from the research phase to the high-volume manufacturing phase while maintaining high-quality standards. In the Manufacturing Integration Engineering (MIE) organization, we engineer world-class yields on advanced processes by driving defects down to Best-in-Class targets.


As a Defect Metrology Engineer, you will be responsible for identifying all defects that impact yield and performance in an advanced silicon process technology. You will characterize the process using cutting-edge metrology tools. With this characterization, you will be responsible for investigating the root cause owners and developing defect reduction roadmaps to achieve program milestone commitments to our customers. You will then work directly with the process modules and integration teams to drive that roadmap by developing and qualifying process fixes through Model-Based Problem Solving (MBPS). You will also respond to defect baseline shifts to isolate the root cause and implement preventative actions consistent with 8D methodology. This role provides an opportunity to influence Intel's future process technologies that will keep Moore's Law moving forward.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Owning a segment of the process to ensure adequate metrology is placed to detect and respond to all yield-limiting defects prior to reaching end-of-line sort.
  • Investigate and respond to exclusionary baseline shifts to ensure segment defect health is restored to capable, demonstrated baseline.
  • Develop new recipes and RFCs as part of New Product Introduction (NPI).
  • Provide navigation and leadership to meet Intel's yield objectives, utilizing state-of-the-art metrology tools and test vehicles (QTM, Short Loop, etc.).
  • Organizing and presenting defect summaries to F25, LTD, MDCE engineering teams.
  • Partnering with Intel Integration, Yield, and failure analysis labs to provide root cause for all defect issues.
  • Hold the team and collaborators accountable for quality through Integrated Module Team (IMT) and Focus Team (FT) forums.
  • Work collaboratively as a part of the overall LTD Defect metrology group.
  • Role-model and establish a team culture of trust, collaboration, safety, accountability, and sustaining excellence.
  • Build strong relationships with other LTD teams based on mutual trust and respect.

The Ideal Candidate Must Demonstrate:

  • Strong data analysis and problem debug skills.
  • Team player with flexibility and adaptability to changing business needs.
  • Strong ownership mindset and driving closure-see the problem, own the problem.
  • Excellent communication and navigation skills to larger audiences.
  • Understand and adhere to Intel cultural values such as Customer First, Fearless Innovation, Results Driven, One Intel, Integrity, Quality, Inclusion.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Experience would be obtained through a combination of prior education level classes, and current level school classes, projects, research, and relevant previous job and internship experience.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Must possess a Master's degree in Materials Science and Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Physics, Nuclear Engineering, Optics, Chemistry, or Computer Science.
  • Hands-on experimental research experience: designing and conducting experiments, operating laboratory equipment (characterization, fabrication, or synthesis), and analyzing statistical data.

Preferred qualifications:

Demonstrated academic research, coursework, laboratory, or internship experience with one or more of the following:

  • Materials characterization (SEM, TEM, AFM, etc.), materials fabrication, synthesis, metrology, statistical or data analysis (MATLAB, Excel, JMP, Python, etc.).
  • Semiconductor processing fundamentals (lithography, wet and/or dry etch, chemical mechanical polishing, thin films), semiconductor and/or transistor device physics, and Design of Experiments (DOE).
  • Defect metrology, defect inspection/improvement, yield analysis, or process integration.
  • Demonstrated application of Statistical Process Control (SPC) or Design of Experiments (DOE) principles.
  • Complex problem-solving methodologies: root cause analysis, Model-Based Problem Solving (MBPS), 5 Why, Fishbone diagrams, or 8D frameworks.
  • Understanding of semiconductor physics or semiconductor processing cleanroom unit operations.
  • Understanding of defect metrology tools such as brightfield, darkfield, or voltage contrast (VC).
