title: Process Integration Development Engineer - Defect Metrology
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Embark with us on a journey of growth and transformation as we create exceptionally engineered technology and bring AI everywhere. As a valued team member, your adaptability and attention to detail will contribute to our drive for results and relentless pursuit of quality, ensuring we meet our customers' needs with precision.

Join us and build on our legacy of innovation and collaboration as we deliver world‑changing technology that improves the life of every person on the planet.

Life at Intel: https://jobs.intel.com/en/life-at-intel

At Intel's Logic Technology Development (LTD), we have continued to extend Moore's law to be world leaders in computing technology. To achieve the necessary scaling of our semiconductor manufacturing process, we have led the industry in developing enhancements such as strained silicon for carrier transport enhancement, high-k metal gates, FinFETs, and next-generation Gate-All-Around architectures. LTD has been at the center of every new development that has kept Moore's Law moving forward.


Defect Metrology plays a key role in the development of every new silicon process technology. Our analysis builds the plan that allows LTD to take technology from the research phase to the high-volume manufacturing phase while maintaining high-quality standards. In the Manufacturing Integration Engineering (MIE) organization, we engineer world-class yields on advanced processes by driving defects down to Best-in-Class targets.


As a Defect Metrology Engineer, you will be responsible for identifying all defects that impact yield and performance in an advanced silicon process technology. You will characterize the process using cutting-edge metrology tools. With this characterization, you will be responsible for investigating the root cause owners and developing defect reduction roadmaps to achieve program milestone commitments to our customers. You will then work directly with the process modules and integration teams to drive that roadmap by developing and qualifying process fixes through Model-Based Problem Solving (MBPS). You will also respond to defect baseline shifts to isolate the root cause and implement preventative actions consistent with 8D methodology. This role provides an opportunity to influence Intel's future process technologies that will keep Moore's Law moving forward.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Owning a segment of the process to ensure adequate metrology is placed to detect and respond to all yield-limiting defects prior to reaching end-of-line sort.
  • Investigate and respond to exclusionary baseline shifts to ensure segment defect health is restored to capable, demonstrated baseline.
  • Develop new recipes and RFCs as part of New Product Introduction (NPI).
  • Provide navigation and leadership to meet Intel's yield objectives, utilizing state-of-the-art metrology tools and test vehicles (QTM, Short Loop, etc.).
  • Organizing and presenting defect summaries to F25, LTD, MDCE engineering teams.
  • Partnering with Intel Integration, Yield, and failure analysis labs to provide root cause for all defect issues.
  • Hold the team and collaborators accountable for quality through Integrated Module Team (IMT) and Focus Team (FT) forums.
  • Work collaboratively as a part of the overall LTD Defect metrology group.
  • Role-model and establish a team culture of trust, collaboration, safety, accountability, and sustaining excellence.
  • Build strong relationships with other LTD teams based on mutual trust and respect.

The Ideal Candidate Must Demonstrate:

  • Strong data analysis and problem debug skills.
  • Team player with flexibility and adaptability to changing business needs.
  • Strong ownership mindset and driving closure-see the problem, own the problem.
  • Excellent communication and navigation skills to larger audiences.
  • Understand and adhere to Intel cultural values such as Customer First, Fearless Innovation, Results Driven, One Intel, Integrity, Quality, Inclusion.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Experience would be obtained through a combination of prior education level classes, and current level school classes, projects, research, and relevant previous job and internship experience.

Minimum qualification/s:

Must possess a PhD degree in Computer Science, Physics, Material Science and Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Nuclear engineering, Optics, or Chemistry (with focus on hands on experimental research)

Preferred qualifications:

Minimum of 1+ years of experience with one or more of the following:

  • Experimental research - designing and conducting experiments, operating equipment (characterization, fabrication, synthesis), analyzing statistical data
  • Materials characterization (SEM, TEM, etc.), materials fabrication, synthesis, metrology, statistical or data analysis (MATLAB, Excel, JMP, etc.)
  • Semiconductor processing fundamentals (lithography, wet and or dry etch, chemical and or mechanical polishing, etc.), semiconductor and or transistor device physics, and design of experiments.
  • Defect metrology, defect improvement, yield improvement, or process integration
  • Demonstrate experience of Statistical Process Control (SPC), or Design of Experiments (DOE) principles
  • Complex problem-solving methodologies - root cause analysis, model-based problem solving (MBPS), 5 Why, Fishbone, etc.
  • Understanding of semiconductor physics or semiconductor processing
  • Understanding of defect metrology tools such as brightfield, darkfield, or voltage contrast (VC)

We welcome motivated professionals to bring their expertise and enthusiasm to Intel, where you will have the opportunity to grow your career while helping to shape the future of technology in a collaborative and forward-thinking environment. title: Intel Foundry LTD Product Yield Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Embark with us on a journey of growth and transformation as we create exceptionally engineered technology and bring AI everywhere. As a valued team member, your adaptability and attention to detail will contribute to our drive for results and relentless pursuit of quality, ensuring we meet our customers' needs with precision.


Join us and build on our legacy of innovation and collaboration as we deliver world‑changing technology that improves the life of every person on the planet.

Life at Intel: https://jobs.intel.com/en/life-at-intel

About Logic Technology Development: Technology Development (TD) is the heart and soul of Moore's Law at Intel. TD has enabled Intel to create world-changing technology that enriches the lives of every person on earth. TD's employees drive breakthrough research, develop next generation process and packaging technologies, while also running high volume manufacturing operations in its state-of-the-art facilities in Oregon and Arizona. Intel Foundry is developing the next generation of silicon solutions to enable tomorrow's computing solutions. Within Intel Foundry, Logic Technology Development (LTD) creates and perfects each process technology node.

About the Role: As a senior LTD product yield engineer, you will work to deliver test and analysis solutions for LTD Yield. You will partner with design groups to develop methods and strategies for improving product yield.

The responsibilities include (but are not limited to):

  • Formulate yield problems mathematically, identify solutions, and remove technical and non-technical barriers by influencing stakeholders to achieve successful solutions.
  • Identify root cause of systematic yield issues and propose mitigation plans in defined timeline to meet committed production yield targets.
  • Develop new yield analysis methods and algorithms to deliver world class yield analytics.
  • Work with design business units to debug new and novel process/product interactions.
  • Develop, organize, and present-yield strategies to LTD leadership.
  • Collaborate with Program Managers, Process Integration, Device Integration and Defect teams to identify yield detractors and yield enhancement opportunities.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position.   • Master's degree in electrical engineering, computer science, VLSI design, physics and 3+ years of experience in advanced node semiconductor industry in semiconductor yield or product engineering

Preferred Qualifications:

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
Join Intel Foundry Construction and Sourcing (FCS) in building the world's largest semiconductor manufacturing facilities across the globe. As a Construction Central Document Control Manager, you will play a pivotal role in executing a new document control and records management strategy, ensuring consistent, efficient document control processes across all Intel Foundry construction projects. You will own the standards, operating model and oversight required to ensure project and business records are complete, secure, compliant and retrievable throughout their lifecycle.

Business Group
Within the Foundry Construction and Sourcing (FCS) organization in Intel Foundry, the FCS Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) team operates to ensure that Intel Foundry compliantly operates free from construction and supply risk disruption. We do this by relentlessly delivering agile and reliable oversight with an Intel Foundry governance, risk, and compliance framework that minimizes foundry risks and business impacts for our customers. Within the FCS GRC team, the Central Document Control Manager governs the FCS enterprise document and records management strategy, enabling compliant, efficient and scalable information management across FCS.

This individual will play a critical, forward-looking role in modernizing document control and records management practices across all sites, including executing a new, holistic cross-FCS records management strategy and evaluating processes for efficiency, standardization, automation and appropriate use of AI-enabled capabilities. This role will closely partner with construction project teams, project controls teams, design teams, sourcing teams, CW workgroups and other stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

  • Owns and governs the centralized enterprise document control framework used across all FCS Construction projects.
  • Executes the updated global FCS Construction Document Control and Records Management strategy, operationalizing centralized improvements for process simplification, automation, AI enablement, Project File Index (PFI) modernization and operating model optimization.
  • Streamlines, maintains and enforces Construction Document Control standards, processes and controls to ensure consistent execution by project teams and Local Document Control resources.
  • Ensures the Construction Document Control system protects Intel intellectual property, supports contractual, legal, audit and claims defense requirements, maintains complete, accurate and retrievable project records and serves as the single source of truth for project documentation.
  • Defines, maintains and governs the standard Project File Index (PFI), approving updates, deviations or exceptions, ensuring contractual deliverables are properly stored and searchable in accordance with PFI requirements and overseeing deployment of the PFI structure within approved project platforms (e.g., BIM360).
  • Manages Construction Document Control platform administration and access governance, overseeing implementation of permissions and role alignment by Local Document Control teams and ensuring access audits are conducted in accordance with Intel policy.
  • Ensures contractual deliverables are transmitted through Intel Document Control in accordance with contract requirements.
  • Governs FCS records management practices to support traceability, audit readiness and claims defense.
  • Partners with Program and Project Managers to align Construction Document Control services with project needs, recommending opportunities for reducing document control cost footprint across sites.
  • Manage Construction Document Control requirements from project initiation through project closeout, ensuring document control standards are applied consistently throughout projects at all sites and aligned with Intel Records Retention Policy.
  • Ability to lead cross-functional teams and align stakeholders in matrixed organizations.

  • Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Business, Engineering, Information Management or related field.
  • 4+ years of experience in document control, records management, or information governance across multi-site or enterprise environments.
  • Experience with process improvements and operational efficiencies through standardization, automation, AI or digital transformation.

title: Project Scheduler
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 


Join Intel Foundry Construction and Sourcing (FCS) in building the world's largest semiconductor manufacturing factories across the globe. The future is what we build.


Our enterprise manages a portfolio of capital projects on-site with a large contractor workforce that encompasses outsourced general contractors, A/E firms, and key trade companies in the Semiconductor Construction Industry. The scope of our work includes but is not limited to New Wafer Fabrication factories (Fabs), Fab Conversions, Process Tools Install, Infrastructure, and Progressive Build.


We are looking for world-class technical talent to join our team. If you enjoy working with the latest technology in a rewarding, fast-paced environment, this is the right place for you. Everywhere you go, you'll find an opportunity to make a difference. In any given workday, you will be given the responsibility to innovate and create an impact on our business. The FCS portfolio delivers billions of dollars in construction projects around the world, and the successful delivery of these contributes to Intel's success.This position reports to the Director of Project Controls.This is an onsite position in Hillsboro, Oregon.


As a Project Schedule Manager your responsibilities will include but are not limited to:

  • Coordination, analysis, and integration of schedules produced by others to support the project requirements.
  • Development of owner's schedules to set timing constraints on other schedules.
  • Determine program and project schedule risk and explain that risk to management.
  • Partner successfully with key stakeholders: including factory facility owners, site construction contractors, Basebuild and Lay Out Dependent (BB/LOD) manager(s), Schedule Manager, Project Management Office (PMO), Etc.
  • Work directly with the schedulers from the various general contractors and design build teams to monitor schedule risks.
    Define and analyze Project critical paths across all schedules and project stages.
  • Organize, prepare, and facilitate interactive planning and schedule review sessions with the project team and key stakeholders.
    Support the site's Basebuild, Layout Dependent Projects, and Tool Install as needed.
  • Integrate schedules among different projects/scopes like Basebuild, Progressive Build, Tool Install, etc. to ensure the program level goals are achievable.
  • Provides analysis on schedule information for example PAS Indicators, float trends and lookahead reports, etc.
  • Validate Contractor approaches/schedule's soundness and reasonableness while measuring and reporting of progress against schedule.
  • Provide what-if support to Projects as needed.
  • Proactively troubleshoot schedule issues and gaps and work on issues with stakeholders.
  • Support negative float resolution.
  • Develop reports to show changes and impacts from week to week at Program level Support weekly meetings with stakeholders to review and disposition discrepancies gaps.
  • Establish, implement, and adhere to Schedule Change Control processes.
  • Evaluate schedule risks using Earned Value Method (S curve).
    Build and drive safety culture of caring in every business environment, office to the construction sites, and from front-end planning to construction execution.

The successful candidate should exhibit the following behavioral traits:


  • Communication skills, written and oral, including the expertise to manage discussions with executive management drilling down to details and managing an effort hands-on if the need arises to drive necessary decision making.
  • Diplomatic customer-orientation.
  • Willingness to influence highly matrixed teams with seemingly conflicting needs.
  • Expertise to extract information from construction drawings, specifications, contracts, and proposal documents.
  • Expertise to work in a fast-paced environment with multiple customers and stakeholders.
  • Team player, Inquisitive, self-starter with a keen eye for details and skills to learn quickly.
  • Champion and value the safety culture of caring throughout the project lifecycle.

This position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship.

Experience in the following:

title: Intel Foundry/PCC Semiconductor Manufacturing Student Technician – ICE Program
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Why Intel Foundry? 

Every technological breakthrough starts with a spark of curiosity and hands-on determination. At Intel Foundry, we design, develop, and manufacture the cutting-edge semiconductor chips that power the world—from AI-driven supercomputers and autonomous vehicles to global cloud networks and everyday smart devices. 


As a Manufacturing Student Technician Intern, you won’t just read about semiconductor innovation, you will be inside one of the world’s most advanced cleanroom environments, operating multi-million-dollar toolsets and driving real-time wafer production. This 2-year part-time program is specifically designed for college students pursuing associate degrees, offering competitive pay, practical training, flexible scheduling around your classes, and an express ramp into high-tech manufacturing careers. 


What You Will Gain 

  • World-Class Cleanroom & Tool Experience: Develop hands-on operational and maintenance mastery over state-of-the-art semiconductor fabrication equipment. 
  • Direct Technical Mentorship: Collaborate alongside seasoned process engineers, module technicians, and factory leaders invested in your growth and success. 
  • Academic Flexibility & Total Rewards: Work compressed work-week shifts structured around your academic schedule, backed by industry-leading pay, performance bonuses, and benefits. 

Key Responsibilities & Day-to-Day Impact 

  • Drive Wafer Production & Operations: Oversee automated wafer fabrication and movement processes within the Oregon Fab network, maintaining strict adherence to quality benchmarks, output targets, and operational discipline. 
  • Hands-On Maintenance & Troubleshooting: Diagnose equipment anomalies, conduct preventative maintenance (PM), and utilize precision hand tools and diagnostic fixtures to maximize equipment availability and yield. 
  • Execute Technical Procedures: Interpret and execute instructions from comprehensive engineering drawings, schematics, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and technical specifications. 
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Deliver crisp, concise shift pass-downs to incoming teams and partner closely with module teams to sustain continuous factory flow. 
  • Uphold Safety & Cleanroom Standards: Serve as a safety champion by adhering strictly to fab safety protocols, chemical safety standards, and cleanroom contamination controls. 

Work Schedule & Program Structure 

  • Program Duration: 2-Year Cohort Internship Program. 
  • Term-Time Hours: 20 to 32 hours per week during active school terms. 
  • Break/Summer Hours: Up to 40 hours per week during academic breaks and summer sessions. 

Compressed Workweek (CWW) Shifts (12-Hour Day Schedules): 

  • Shift 5 (Day): Sunday through Tuesday (and alternating Wednesdays) | 7:30 AM – 8:00 PM 
  • Shift 7 (Day): Thursday through Saturday (and alternating Wednesdays) | 7:30 AM – 8:00 PM 
  • Additional schedule options available for AMHS Area
  • Shift8 (Day/Night) AMHS FH Sunday Through Tuesday (alternating Wednesday) | 12:00 PM – 00:00 AM  
  • Shift8 (Day/Night) AMHS BH Thursday Through Saturday (alternating Wednesday) | 12:00 PM – 00:00 AM    

This position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Relevant experience can be obtained through schoolwork, classes and project work, certifications, apprenticeships, internships, military training, and/or work experience.


Minimum Requirements:

  • Active Student Status: Currently enrolled in good standing at a locally accredited community college, trade school, or university pursuing an Associate’s degree in Microelectronics, Automation STEM, or applicable technical trade. 
  • Applicable fields include Microelectronics, Robotics, Electrical/Electronic Engineering Tech, Mechanical Technology, Automotive/Diesel Systems, Aviation Maintenance, HVAC, Machining, Life Safety Systems, Industrial Automation, Welding, and Precision Manufacturing. 
  • Shift Availability: Ability to commit to at least 20 hours per week aligned with 12-hour compressed work-week factory shifts. 

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Sustained strong academic performance during rigorous first-term electrical and mechanical engineering coursework. 
  • Demonstrated mechanical or electrical aptitude gained through hands-on projects, auto repair, robotics clubs, maker spaces, soldering, welding, vocational programs, or military technical experience. 
  • Strong diagnostic, problem-solving, and logical reasoning skills with a commitment to continuous learning in a high-tech cleanroom environment. 

Cleanroom Environment & Physical Expectations 

  • Spend substantial shift time (>90% less break time) inside a high-tech cleanroom environment wearing full cleanroom attire (bunny suit, hood, booties, safety glasses, and nitrile gloves). 
  • Ability to stand, walk, bend, reach, and lift to 45 lbs. across a 12-hour manufacturing shift. 
  • Comfort utilizing precision tools, mechanical fixtures, and safety-rated equipment. 

Compensation, Benefits & Growth 

Intel offers a robust total compensation package, including competitive hourly rates, shift differential premiums, annual performance bonuses, stock opportunities, employee discounts, and comprehensive medical, wellness, and retirement benefits.

Job Description: 

Intel is seeking an experienced APTM NPI (New Product Introduction) Integrator to lead technology transfer, manufacturing readiness, quality improvement, and yield optimization activities for advanced packaging and technology development programs. The successful candidate will drive the integration of new technologies into manufacturing by defining roadmaps, establishing operational strategies, and ensuring product and process readiness from startup through high-volume manufacturing.

This role requires combines deep manufacturing expertise, advanced data analytics capabilities, and strategic influence to accelerate technology deployment, improve manufacturing performance, and drive organizational excellence.

We are seeking a highly motivated and technically skilled Integrator to lead the development and execution of new product/ process introduction and process transfers across factories.

The ideal candidate will play a key role in ensuring that technology, platforms, and products meet certification requirements before transferring to HVM.

  • Setting up lot flows, kicking off NPI Checklists for each module, starting the silicon and monitoring its progress through the process flow for set up, power-on and engineering samples until first production.
  • Develop and implement new NPI systems and business processes as they become ready and close any issues identified in a NPI reflection
  • Utilize data analytics tools (e.g., SQL, Python) to synthesize insights from structured and unstructured data, driving continuous process improvement and troubleshooting.
  • Lead cross-functional teams through model-based problem-solving methodologies to address process excursions and drive operational efficiencies.

  • Candidates are expected to have strong understanding of a product’s life cycle, fab processing, and post fab activities.

title: Process Integration Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Embark with us on a journey of growth and transformation as we create exceptionally engineered technology and bring AI everywhere. As a valued team member, your adaptability and attention to detail will contribute to our drive for results and relentless pursuit of quality, ensuring we meet our customers' needs with precision.


Join us and build on our legacy of innovation and collaboration as we deliver world‑changing technology that improves the life of every person on the planet.

Life at Intel: https://jobs.intel.com/en/life-at-intel

At Intel's Logic Technology Development (LTD) we have continued to extend Moore's law to be world leaders in computing technology. To achieve the necessary scaling of our semiconductor manufacturing process, we have led the industry in developing enhancements such as strained silicon for carrier transport enhancement, high-k metal gates, and FINFETs. LTD has been at the center of every new development that has kept Moore's Law moving forward. TMI Integration plays a key role in the development of every new silicon process development. Our analysis builds the plan that allows LTD to take technology from the research phase to the high-volume manufacturing phase while maintaining high-quality standards. In the MIE organization, we engineer world-class yields on D1 processes by driving critical Fab and E-Test parameters to Best-in-Class targets. As a TMI Integration engineer, you will be responsible for identifying all the process parameters that impact yield and performance in an advanced silicon process technology. You will characterize the process using cutting-edge metrology tools. With this characterization, you will be responsible for creating a yield cliff parameter improvement roadmap. You will then work directly with modules and TD integration to drive that roadmap by developing and qualifying process fixes. This role provides an opportunity to influence Intel's future process technologies that will keep Moore's Law moving forward. 

Responsibilities will include but will not be limited to:

  • Provide navigation and leadership to meet Intel's yield objectives.
  • Organizing and presenting process parameter summaries to LTD engineering teams.
  • Partnering with Intel TD Integration, Yield, and Module engineers to drive root cause understanding for all critical process parameters. 
  • Institute ramp to manufacturing volumes to demonstrate the technology meets requirements while simultaneously transferring the technology to counterparts in manufacturing via the Copy Exactly Methodology. 
  • Hold the team and collaborators accountable for quality through TMIs and FTs. 
  • Role-model and establish a team culture of trust, collaboration, safety, accountability, and excellence. 
  • Build strong relationships with other LTD process and design teams based on mutual trust and respect. 
  • An ideal candidate should be willing to demonstrate the below behavioral traits - Strong data analysis and problem debug skills, Excellent communication skills, Understand and adhere to key Intel values.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates Experience listed below would be obtained through a combination of your schoolwork, classes, research and/or relevant previous job and/or internship experiences.


Minimum Qualifications:

The ideal candidate must possess at least one of the following: 

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer/Data Science, Physics, Materials Science and Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, Optics, Chemistry, or any related field (with focus on hands-on experimental research) with 4+ years of Engineering Industry experience; OR
  • Master's degree in Computer/Data Science, Physics, Materials Science and Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, Optics, Chemistry, or any related field (with focus on hands-on experimental research) with 3+ years of Engineering Industry experience; OR
  • PHD in Computer/Data Science, Physics, Materials Science and Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, Optics,  Chemistry, or any related field (with focus on hands-on experimental research).

Preferred Qualifications: 
1+ year’s experience with one or more of the following:

  • Materials characterization (SEM, TEM, etc.), materials fabrication, synthesis, metrology, statistical or data analysis (MATLAB, Excel, JMP, etc.)
  • Semiconductor processing fundamentals (lithography, wet and or dry etch, chemical and or mechanical polishing, etc.), semiconductor and or transistor device physics, and design of experiments.
  • Demonstrate experience of Statistical Process Control SPC or Design of Experiments (DOE) principles.

Take advantage of this opportunity to join Intel and shape the future of engineering. Apply today to be part of a team that drives industry-leading innovation and transformation.

title: Silicon Packaging Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Define packaging solutions for highly innovative integrated circuits, meeting adequate mechanical, thermal and electrical performance with the goal to achieve lowest package and system level cost. Co-design with chip designer, system engineering and PCB design teams during the development stage to optimize pad layout and pin map for most cost effective package and system. Independently plan, design and develop quality custom lead frame/substrate/module with supporting electrical simulation to reduce cross-talk, IR drop, and noise issues of the device. Technical lead for implementing packaging solutions at OSAT assembly site and/or internal assembly site. Ensure optimized package design which meets the assembly design rules of the selected assembly site. Work with the assembly partner to mitigate any potential risk and improve situation to meet yield target within the project milestone requirement. Co-work with NPI manager to prepare assembly site readiness for continuous uninterrupted flow from wafer fab-out to quality packaged sample meeting the required NPI schedule. Maintain complete set of product specific packaging related drawings, and reports.

Qualifications:

Bachelor / Master degree in Electrical Engineering / Mechanical Engineering / Material Science with more than 10 years experience in the field of IC Packaging Design and Layout. Package design experience using Siemens Xpedition EDA tool set is a must. Understand performance and cost trade-offs for different layout and assembly rules. Extensive manufacturing process knowledge regarding wafer bumping, substrate and lead frame manufacturing and assembly of wire bond and flip chip packages is required. Practical knowledge of Signal integrity and Power integrity in PCB design will be an advantage. Possesses good analytical, communication and organization skills.

title: Supply Chain Planning and Operations (SCPO) AI Lead
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Supply Chain Planning Operations (SCPO) organization is seeking an AI Software Architect to serve as the SCPO AI Lead.

This is a founding technical leadership role embedded within supply planning operations. The role will define and execute the AI strategy for connecting planning and execution data, detecting emerging supply, flagging demand and product risks, and enabling planners and leaders to act on trusted, explainable insights.

The Supply Chain Planning Operations (SCPO) AI Lead will architect and build the intelligent stitching and alerting layer across Plan of Record (POR), Long Range Planning (LRP), Sales and Operations Planning (SnOP), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), and other supply chain related data.


The role will convert fragmented data from multiple sources and manual reconciliation into production capabilities that continuously monitor supply execution, identify likely failures, explain the drivers, and guide timely intervention.


The successful candidate will deliver production solutions used in operational decisions, work directly with planners, and establish the technical foundation and engineering practices for SCPO. Please note that this is not a research-only or advisory role.

The SCPO AI Lead is responsible for, but not limited to:


  • Define the SCPO AI and data intelligence strategy, architecture, roadmap, and standards in alignment with supply-chain priorities and measurable business outcomes.
  • Architect and operationalize a trusted data stitching layer across POR, LRP, SnOP, ERP, and other planning data sources, including lineage, controls, reconciliation, and data-quality monitoring and governance.
  • Develop production machine-learning and AI capabilities for time-series analysis, anomaly detection, root-cause identification, supply-risk sensing, and early warning of execution failures.
  • Integrate AI outputs with enterprise planning systems and operational workflows using reliable APIs, data pipelines, monitoring, access controls, and override mechanisms.
  • Build agentic workflows that automate recurring analyses, evidence gathering, exception triage, and narrative generation while maintaining human-in-the-loop controls, auditability, and appropriate governance.
  • Develop scenario and sensitivity capabilities that evaluate supply disruptions, demand changes, yield shifts, capacity reallocations, material constraints, and other operational decisions across planning horizons.
  • Create explainable alerts and decision-support experiences that show what changed, why it matters, the level of confidence, and the recommended next action.
  • Map the planning-system ecosystem, data flows, manual intervention points, process breakpoints, dependencies, and failure modes; prioritize automation and guardrails based on business risk and value.
  • Partner with supply planning, demand planning, manufacturing, foundry, procurement, finance, data engineering, information technology, and business teams to translate operational problems into scalable technical solutions.
  • Establish MLOps and software-engineering practices for model versioning, testing, deployment, observability, retraining, documentation, security, and responsible AI governance.
  • Communicate technical findings, model limitations, risk signals, architecture decisions, and business recommendations clearly to planners, technical partners, senior managers, and executives.
  • Operate with intellectual rigor in ambiguous environments where data, systems, and requirements are incomplete or evolving.
  • Commitment to explainability, responsible AI, human oversight, security, and governance for decisions with material financial or operational consequences.

Initial success measures include:


  • Within 90 days: define the target stitching architecture, data ownership model, prioritized use-case roadmap, and deploy an initial live reconciliation capability.
  • Within 6 months: deploy an explainable alert that detects a material supply-execution risk early enough to support intervention.
  • Within 12 months: demonstrate sustained planner adoption, measurable reduction in manual reconciliation, and operational decisions informed by trusted alerts and scenarios.

The ideal candidate should exhibit the following behavioral traits:


  • Advanced communication skills to tailor complex technical content for engineering, planning, and executive audiences.
  • Tolerance for responsible experimentation, including disciplined learning from approaches that do not succeed.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications, you must possess the minimum qualifications below to be initially considered for this position.


  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Industrial Engineering, Operations Research, Applied Mathematics, or a related quantitative field.
  • 8+ years of experience in:

    • Machine-learning engineering, AI engineering, data science, data engineering, optimization, or related technical roles, including leadership of complex production deployments.
    • Architecting, deploying, and operating machine-learning solutions in production on complex enterprise data.
    • Programming experience in Python and strong SQL skills, with practical experience in modern machine-learning, data-processing, and software-engineering frameworks.
    • Designing data pipelines, APIs, and integrations across enterprise applications, data platforms, and operational systems.
    • Leading cross-functional technical work and influencing architecture and delivery decisions without relying solely on direct authority.

This position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship.


Preferred Qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.


  • Master's degree in relevant technical or quantitative discipline.
  • Experience in semiconductors, electronics, or comparable high-volume manufacturing environments, including wafer starts and outs, yield, substrate and long-lead materials, new-product-introduction gates, and capacity commitments.
  • Working knowledge of supply planning, demand planning, SnOP or integrated business planning, capacity planning, inventory optimization, procurement, and order management.
  • Experience with enterprise planning and manufacturing platforms such as SAP, Kinaxis Rapid Response, Oracle, manufacturing execution systems, or equivalent technologies.
  • Hands-on experience with cloud data and AI platforms, distributed data processing, and enterprise-grade observability and security.
  • Experience with large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, agentic frameworks, and evaluation and governance of generative AI solutions.
  • Experience building interactive scenario-modeling or decision-support applications used by operational teams.
  • Experience hiring, mentoring, and technically leading AI, machine-learning, or data-engineering talent in a new or rapidly scaling capability.
  • APICS CPIM, CSCP, or equivalent supply-chain certification.

title: Module Development Engineer (Ph.D.) - Intel Foundry
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Role

Intel Logic Technology Development (LTD) designs and scales the advanced semiconductor process technologies that power future generations of Intel architecture.


As a Module Development Engineer, you will drive the development, optimization, characterization, and high-volume manufacturing (HVM) transfer of leading-edge semiconductor processes.

  • Patterning & Removal: Lithography, Overlay, Wet Etch, Dry/Plasma Etch, Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP).
  • Thin Films & Doping: Epitaxy (EPI), Thin-Film Deposition (ALD/CVD/PVD), Diffusion, Ion Implantation, Metals/Metallization, Dielectrics.
  • Metrology, Yield & Integration: In-line Metrology, FEOL/BEOL Process Integration, Defect Reduction, Yield Analysis, Electrical Characterization.

Key Responsibilities ("What You Will Do")

  • Process & Hardware Engineering: Design, execute, and optimize experimental runs to advance semiconductor processes, equipment hardware, and new material capabilities.
  • Process Control & Data Analytics: Apply statistical modeling, Design of Experiments (DOE), and control systems (SPC, APC, Run-to-Run) to reduce variability, mitigate defects, and drive yield enhancement.
  • Cross-Functional & Vendor Collaboration: Partner with external tool/material suppliers and internal integration teams to co-develop cutting-edge equipment and process methodologies.
  • HVM Technology Transfer: Resolve equipment, process, and yield excursion root causes to ensure smooth, robust technology transfer from development into high-volume manufacturing.
  • Documentation & Technical Reporting: Document experimental findings, operating procedures, and technical recommendations through engineering reports and presentations.

Qualifications:

Candidates must meet the following criteria (relevant experience may be gained through academic coursework, laboratory research, thesis work, internships, post doc, or publications):


Minimum Qualifications 

  • Education: Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science & Engineering, Physics, Mechanical, Chemistry, or a related STEM field (expected completion prior to start date).
  • Hands-on Experience: 6+ months of experience with semiconductor fabrication, process development, device research, materials research, or related semiconductor technology, including one or more of the following: lithography (Litho)/overlay, epitaxy (EPI), wet etch, dry etch, thin-film deposition, diffusion, ion implantation, CMP/planarization, metals/metallization, dielectrics, metrology, process integration, yield, or electrical characterization. 

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Environment & Tooling: 6+ months in a cleanroom or semiconductor research lab working directly with fabrication or analytical instrumentation (e.g., ALD, CVD, PVD, plasma etch, CD-SEM, TEM, AFM, spectroscopic ellipsometry). 
  • Data Science & Automation: 6+ months utilizing statistical methodologies (DOE, SPC) and engineering software/scripting languages (Python, MATLAB, JMP, C#, or equivalents) for data analysis and automation. 
  • Device Physics & Integration: Academic or research specialization in transistor architecture, advanced semiconductor materials, or FEOL/BEOL process integration. 
  • Technical Dissemination: Proven track record of presenting technical findings through dissertations, peer-reviewed publications, conference proceedings, patents, or white papers.

This position requires a unique combination of software development expertise, architecture understanding, analytical problem solving, and cross-functional technical leadership. The engineer will be expected to independently drive complex technical initiatives while serving as a trusted performance expert across multiple organizations. ________________________________________ Key Responsibilities 1. AI Silicon Performance Model Development • Develop, maintain, and enhance SystemC/TLM-based performance models representing critical AI silicon subsystems. • Drive modeling of key architectural components including: o SoC fabrics and on-chip communication networks o Memory controllers and memory subsystem behavior o Scale-up controllers and fabrics enabling accelerator-to-accelerator communication within a node, tray, or pod o Scale-out controllers and fabrics enabling communication across nodes, racks, and larger AI clusters o Host CPU to accelerator memory paths o Local, host, and remote memory access paths o End-to-end data movement architectures • Implement new architectural features and capabilities based on evolving product requirements. • Improve model fidelity, scalability, maintainability, and simulation performance. • Perform detailed debugging and root-cause analysis of model issues and performance anomalies. • Contribute to the evolution of modeling infrastructure, methodologies, and best practices. ________________________________________ 2. Functional Validation and Model Correlation • Define and execute comprehensive validation strategies to ensure correctness and architectural accuracy of performance models. • Develop validation plans, regression suites, coverage methodologies, and quality metrics. • Correlate modeled behavior against architectural expectations, reference simulations, performance projections, and available hardware measurements. • Investigate and resolve discrepancies between expected and observed behavior. • Establish robust validation frameworks that improve stakeholder confidence in model-generated performance projections. • Continuously improve validation methodologies and model quality. ________________________________________ 3. AI Silicon Performance Characterization and Architectural Analysis • Design and execute performance studies covering a wide range of workloads, traffic patterns, and system configurations. • Analyze performance of communication fabrics, memory systems, and data movement paths under representative AI workloads. • Evaluate bandwidth utilization, latency characteristics, congestion behavior, traffic distribution, buffering efficiency, and resource utilization. • Characterize interactions across local memory, host memory, and remote memory domains. • Assess scalability of scale-up and scale-out architectures across increasingly larger deployment footprints. • Identify performance bottlenecks and quantify their impact on overall system throughput and efficiency. • Conduct architectural tradeoff studies to evaluate alternative design approaches. • Provide performance-driven recommendations that influence architecture and product decisions. ________________________________________ 4. Performance Data Generation, Analytics and Visualization • Develop frameworks and methodologies for large-scale performance data generation and analysis. • Create automated workflows for data collection, processing, correlation, and reporting. • Develop performance dashboards and visualization tools that simplify interpretation of complex performance data. • Define and track meaningful performance KPIs and architectural metrics. • Utilize Python-based analysis frameworks to process large datasets and generate actionable insights. • Enable efficient consumption of performance information by architects, designers, and engineering leadership. ________________________________________ 5. Cross-Functional Technical Leadership and Stakeholder Engagement • Partner closely with architecture teams, performance stimulus generation teams, silicon design teams, and product stakeholders. • Drive technical discussions related to performance methodology, architectural assumptions, workload behavior, scalability analysis, and bottleneck identification. • Review architectural proposals and provide performance-driven feedback. • Present performance studies, technical findings, and architectural recommendations to engineering leadership. • Influence product and architecture decisions through data-backed analysis and sound engineering judgment. • Act as a key technical bridge between architecture, modeling, and performance analysis organizations. ________________________________________ 6. Methodology Development and Team Growth • Drive improvements in modeling methodologies, simulation efficiency, and analysis workflows. • Identify opportunities for automation across modeling, validation, performance analysis, and reporting activities. • Establish best practices for model quality, performance characterization, and architectural analysis. • Contribute to technical mentoring and knowledge sharing across the team. • Support the development of junior engineers and future team growth initiatives. • Help cultivate a culture of technical excellence and continuous improvement.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications Education • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Electronics Engineering. Technical Experience • 15+ years of industry experience in performance modeling, AI silicon architecture, SoC architecture, computer architecture, performance engineering, or related domains. • Strong software development experience in C++. • Working proficiency in Python for automation, performance analysis, data processing, and visualization. • Hands-on experience with SystemC and Transaction-Level Modeling (TLM) methodologies. • Experience developing or validating performance models for AI accelerators, SoCs, CPUs, GPUs, networking products, or complex hardware systems. • Strong understanding of: o SoC architecture o Memory subsystem architecture o Memory controllers o Cache hierarchies o Data movement architectures o On-chip communication fabrics and NoC concepts o High-speed interconnects o Scale-up and scale-out communication architectures o Performance bottleneck analysis o Latency and bandwidth characterization • Experience performing architectural tradeoff analysis and performance characterization studies. • Experience working with large performance datasets and deriving meaningful engineering insights. Analytical and Problem-Solving Skills • Strong debugging and root-cause analysis capabilities. • Ability to identify performance bottlenecks and drive optimization recommendations. • Experience developing validation strategies and performance evaluation methodologies. • Strong quantitative reasoning and data-driven decision-making skills. • Demonstrated ability to independently solve complex technical problems. Communication and Collaboration • Strong verbal and written communication skills. • Ability to collaborate effectively across globally distributed engineering organizations. • Strong technical presentation and stakeholder management skills. • Ability to influence engineering decisions through rigorous analysis and technical credibility. • Proven ability to operate independently and deliver results in ambiguous problem spaces. ________________________________________ Preferred Qualifications • Deep understanding of AI accelerator architectures and modern AI infrastructure. • Experience modeling memory, communication, interconnect, or scalability-related subsystems. • Experience with Network-on-Chip (NoC) architectures and interconnect performance analysis. • Understanding of scale-up and scale-out architectures used in modern AI computing platforms. • Familiarity with AI/ML workloads, large language models, distributed training, and inference environments. • Experience with performance stimulus generation methodologies and workload characterization. • Experience building automated dashboards and reporting solutions using Power BI, Tableau, Grafana, Plotly, or similar technologies. • Experience evaluating large-scale distributed AI systems and accelerator clusters. • Experience mentoring engineers and providing technical leadership in cross-functional environments.

title: AI SW Engineering Student
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the team
Scale the models everyone is talking about.
Today's models span hundreds of GPUs, and the network between them decides whether a training run takes a week or a month.

As AI models became larger and more complicated, a performant graph mode and efficient scaling solution became a key aspect of the SW solution.

Our team builds that layer. We own the Intel oneAPI Collective Communications Library (oneCCL) and develop the software for multiple generations of Intel AI GPUs, for training and inference.



What you'll do:

  • You'll be a member of the team, working on the library that moves data between GPUs in some of the largest AI training jobs running on Intel hardware.
  • Develop features in the core library: design and implement parts of the C++/SYCL code that run on the GPU, from the first design through code review to the release.
  • Push performance: profile communication across many GPUs, find the bottlenecks and make the fixes that cut the time it takes to train AI models.
  • Solve hard bugs: track down concurrency, synchronization and memory issues in a distributed system that runs across many GPUs at once.
  • Shape how the team builds software: improve the build system, CI pipelines and developer tooling the whole team depends on every day.
  • Learn to use AI tools as part of the development process.

What you'll get:

  • Hands-on work with code that runs in production and is open source.
  • A mentor from the team and regular one-on-one guidance.
  • Experience with high-performance computing and AI infrastructure, a fast-growing field.

Qualifications:

Required:

  • B.Sc. or M.Sc. student in Computer Science, Computer/Electrical Engineering or a related field.
  • Good working knowledge of C++from courses or personal projects.
  • Solid basics in data structures and algorithms.
  • Comfortable with, or eager to learn, working in Linux and on the command line.
  • Curious, willing to ask questions, and able to learn new things on your own.
  • Available 3 days per week

Nice to have:

  • A course or project in parallel programming, operating systems or computer architecture.
  • Exposure to GPU programming (CUDA, SYCL, OpenCL) or MPI.
  • Python scripting.
  • Experience with Git and GitHub.

You don't need prior industry experience. We care more about how you think and learn than about what you already know.

title: Senior Manager, Data Center Portfolio & Demand Management
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact

Intel's Global IT organization is seeking a strategic and results-oriented leader to drive demand management, portfolio governance, and investment planning across Data Center and Infrastructure programs. This role leads a team responsible for evaluating technology demand, prioritizing investments, managing portfolio performance, and ensuring execution aligns with business and technology strategies.

As a senior leader, you will partner across business, engineering, infrastructure, operations, finance, and executive stakeholders to establish governance frameworks, optimize resource allocation, and provide visibility into portfolio health, risks, and outcomes. Success in this role requires strategic thinking, business acumen, strong leadership, and the ability to influence decisions across a complex global organization.

This position offers the opportunity to shape how infrastructure and data center investments are planned, prioritized, governed, and delivered to support Intel's long-term business objectives.

What You’ll Do

Key responsibilities will include but not limited to:

  • Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team responsible for demand management, portfolio governance, strategic planning, and investment prioritization.
  • Partner with business and technology leaders to evaluate demand, align priorities, and ensure investment decisions support organizational objectives.
  • Establish and continuously improve portfolio governance frameworks, prioritization processes, and executive decision-making mechanisms.
  • Oversee portfolio intake, resource planning, prioritization, and execution tracking across data center and infrastructure initiatives.
  • Provide executive-level reporting, portfolio insights, and actionable recommendations to support strategic business decisions.
  • Drive visibility into portfolio performance, investment outcomes, resource utilization, risks, dependencies, and capacity constraints.
  • Facilitate investment trade-off discussions and enable data-driven prioritization across competing business needs.
  • Build strong partnerships across infrastructure, cloud, engineering, operations, and finance organizations to ensure successful execution of strategic initiatives.
  • Lead process improvement efforts that increase efficiency, transparency, accountability, and operational excellence.
  • Foster an inclusive, collaborative culture focused on continuous improvement, innovation, and measurable business impact.

Behavioral traits that we are looking for:

  • Strategic Mindset: Connects investments, priorities, and resources to long-term business objectives.
  • Executive Influence: Builds alignment and drives decisions across senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Business Acumen & Prioritization: Translates complex and ambiguous business needs into clear requirements, priorities, decisions, and accountable execution plans.
  • Executive Communication: Communicates effectively with executives and influences stakeholders across business, technology, facilities, finance, sourcing, and delivery organizations.
  • Results Orientation: Uses data to prioritize effectively, manage trade-offs, and deliver measurable business outcomes.
  • Change Leadership: Leads through ambiguity and drives organizational improvement and transformation.
  • People Leadership: Develops talent, builds inclusive teams, and creates an environment of accountability and growth.

Intel invests in our people and offers a complete and competitive package of benefits employees and their families through every stage of life.

Join Intel Wafer Packaging Manufacturing WPM C4 Ireland as a Module Engineer, and play a key role in advancing one of Intel most important manufacturing operations.

C4 sits at the center of this capability, directly supporting product delivery, factory output, and customer commitments. As we scale, our focus is on building strong, high performing processes that consistently deliver for our customers across safety, quality, and output.

descriptionHtml:

title: Process and Equipment Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
As a Process and Equipment Engineer specializing in Wafer Laser and Saw Singulation Technologies, you will serve as the technical owner responsible for driving the performance, capability, and stability of advanced wafer singulation processes within our high-volume semiconductor manufacturing environment. In this role, you will leverage your expertise in precision laser-material interaction, wafer dicing, laser ablation, and singulation technologies to solve complex process and equipment challenges, optimize manufacturing performance, and implement innovative solutions that enable next-generation semiconductor products.

Your hands-on contributions will directly impact factory yield, quality, equipment uptime, Manufacturing Availability (MA), cost competitiveness, and process robustness. You will play a critical role in supporting Intel's advanced packaging, NPI and wafer manufacturing roadmap through the deployment of cutting-edge laser and sawing technologies.

Business group:
As part of Intel Wafer Packaging Manufacturing (WPM), you will join a globally recognized organization at the forefront of semiconductor manufacturing and advanced packaging technologies. Our organization develops and deploys innovative wafer processing, laser manufacturing, and singulation solutions that enable Intel's next-generation computing platforms.
The Wafer Laser Ablation and Saw Engineering team plays a critical role in delivering high-yield, high-quality wafer singulation processes through the integration of advanced laser processing, precision sawing, automation, data analytics, and AI-driven manufacturing solutions. We continuously push the boundaries of wafer processing capability to meet increasingly demanding product requirements across advanced packaging and silicon technologies.
Working within a highly collaborative environment, you will partner with global factory networks, technology development teams, virtual factories, equipment suppliers, and manufacturing stakeholders to develop breakthrough solutions that improve yield, quality, cost, and manufacturing scalability. This role offers unique opportunities to influence future technology roadmaps while supporting Intel's mission to create world-changing technology that improves the life of every person on the planet.

Key Responsibilities:
Process Optimization - Own and optimize laser ablation and wafer saw process parameters to achieve best-in-class yield, quality, and throughput.
Yield Improvement - Drive systematic defect reduction initiatives targeting burrs, chipping, cracking, kerf quality, and recast.
Equipment Engineering - Lead complex troubleshooting and reliability improvements for laser ablation, laser dicing, and wafer saw equipment.
Maintenance Strategy - Develop and execute preventive and corrective maintenance plans to maximize equipment uptime and MA.
Data Analytics - Utilize SPC, DOE, FMEA,JMP and advanced analytics to identify root causes of process variation and equipment failures.
Automation and AI Solutions - Develop and deploy Python/Co-pilot/Github/ Gemini- and AI-based solutions for defect monitoring, predictive maintenance, and process optimization.

As a Module Development Engineer within Intel's Advanced Packaging Technology Development (APTD) Metrology Group, you will contribute to the development, optimization, and implementation of advanced metrology capabilities supporting Intel's next-generation semiconductor packaging technologies.

Your work will combine hands-on equipment and process development, equipment qualification, manufacturing process optimization, and technology development initiatives. Intel's advanced packaging technology development organization is seeking a Module Development Engineer to support the development of next-generation semiconductor packaging technologies, with a focus on 3D Integrated Circuit (3D IC) technology and advanced manufacturing processes.

title: SoC Validation Engineer – Power Management
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The world is transforming - and so is Intel. Intel is a company of bold and curious inventors and problem solvers who create some of the most astounding technology advancements and experiences in the world. With a legacy of relentless innovation and a commitment to bring smart, connected devices to every person on Earth, our diverse and brilliant teams are continually searching for tomorrow's technology and revel in the challenge that changing the world for the better brings. We work every single day to design and manufacture silicon products that empower people's digital lives. Come join us and do something wonderful.


The Role and Impact:
Intel is seeking a motivated and experienced SoC Validation Engineer to join our Power Management Validation team. In this role, you will be responsible for validating power management architectures and features that enable Intel's next-generation products. You will play a critical role in ensuring design quality, functionality, and power efficiency by developing innovative validation strategies, executing comprehensive test plans, and driving debug activities across complex SoC designs.

As a SoC Power Management Validation Engineer, you will work closely with architecture, design, and verification teams to validate key power management features including Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS), power gating, clock gating, reset flows, low-power states, thermal management, and telemetry. You will contribute to the development of advanced validation environments, uncover design issues early in the development cycle, and drive solutions that improve product quality and readiness. This position offers an opportunity to influence future Intel products while expanding your technical leadership and validation expertise.

Business group:
You will be joining Intel's Data Center Group (DCG), a global leader in designing and delivering cutting-edge technologies that drive data center innovation and transformation. The group specializes in developing high-performance solutions to accelerate computing, storage, and networking capabilities, supporting Intel's mission to power the world's digital infrastructure.

Key Responsibilities:
- Develop and execute comprehensive validation plans to ensure power management features meet architectural and functional specifications.
- Design, develop, and maintain validation environments, automated test content, and debug infrastructure for power management validation.
- Validate critical power management features including: Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS), Power Gating and Clock Gating, Low-Power States and Power State Transitions, Reset and Power Sequencing, Thermal Management Features, Telemetry and Monitoring Logic.
- Develop validation content and infrastructure using industry-standard methodologies and tools such as SystemVerilog, UVM, simulation, and emulation platforms.
- Execute simulation and emulation workloads to validate design functionality and identify issues early in the product development cycle.
- Analyze validation results, coverage metrics, and performance data to improve design quality and validation effectiveness.
- Drive root cause analysis, debug, and resolution of complex design issues in collaboration with architecture, RTL design, and verification teams.
- Develop and maintain automation frameworks, regression environments, dashboards, and data analysis tools to improve validation efficiency and coverage.
- Review architecture specifications and design changes to assess validation impact and ensure comprehensive feature coverage.
- Contribute to validation methodology improvements and best practices across multiple product generations.
- Mentor junior engineers and provide technical leadership on complex validation and debug challenges.
- Continuously explore new technologies, automation techniques, and AI-assisted solutions to improve execution and outcomes.

- Bachelors & 6+ years or Masters & 4+ years or PhD & 2+ years degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field.

- 10+ years of experience in pre-silicon validation, functional validation, design verification, or silicon validation.

- Strong understanding of digital design fundamentals, computer architecture, and SoC design concepts.

- Strong knowledge of SystemVerilog and UVM-based validation methodologies.

- Experience with simulation or emulation environments, debugging and root-cause analysis skills.

Preferred Qualifications:

- Experience validating power management architecture and features in complex SoC designs, such as: Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS), Power Gating, Clock Gating, Low-Power State Management, Reset and Power Sequencing, Thermal Management Features.

- Experience in one or more of the following areas: Functional Validation, Design Verification, Coverage-Driven Verification, Emulation-Based Validation, Low-Power Verification Methodologies, Reset Validation, Power State Validation, Telemetry Feature Validation.

- Familiarity with assertion-based verification, formal verification, and advanced validation automation techniques.

- Demonstrated ability to lead technical initiatives and mentor engineers.

- Strong collaboration skills and ability to work effectively across architecture, design, and validation teams.

- Experience leveraging AI and advanced analytics to improve validation productivity and quality.

- Passion for innovation, continuous improvement, and technical excellence.

- Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Embark with us on a journey of growth and transformation as we create exceptionally engineered technology and bring AI everywhere. As a valued team member, your adaptability and attention to detail will contribute to our drive for results and relentless pursuit of quality, ensuring we meet our customers' needs with precision.


Life at Intel: https://jobs.intel.com/en/life-at-intel 


As a Yield Development Engineer, you will be at the forefront of advancing Intel's cutting-edge process technologies within our Logic Technology Development (LTD) organization. This pivotal role involves identifying root cause yield limiters and driving solutions that enhance manufacturability and yield across technology nodes. You will work within a dynamic, fast-paced environment to ensure the successful introduction of new products, process improvements, and robust methodologies to meet manufacturing goals. Your expertise will directly contribute to Intel's ability to deliver world-class semiconductor solutions and advance the future of computing.


About Intel Foundry


At Intel, the Foundry Technology Development (TD) unit is the driving force behind Moore's Law, enabling us to create groundbreaking technology that enriches lives globally. With over 15,000 dedicated employees, Foundry TD spearheads innovative research, develops next-generation processes and packaging technologies, and manages high-volume manufacturing in state-of-the-art facilities. Within Intel Foundry TD, our Logic Technology Development (LTD) organization is at the forefront of creating and refining each process technology node, paving the way for tomorrow's computing solutions.


Your responsibilities as a Product Yield Development Engineer will include but not be limited to:

  • Develop methods, processes, and systems to consolidate and analyze diverse big data sources for defect mode understanding and yield modeling.
  • Perform statistical analysis, create visualizations, and construct process development roadmaps that drive technology yield milestones.
  • Extract insights from structured and unstructured data using advanced statistics, machine learning, and coding techniques.
  • Organize, interpret, and structure insights from fab process, defect, and electrical data while identifying anomalies to drive process changes for yield enhancement.
  • Develop multivariate algorithms and tools to identify root cause yield limiters and recommend process changes for yield improvement.
  • Collaborate with design teams to resolve yield issues, ensuring manufacturability across process and product specifications before ramping production.
  • Execute new product introductions, enable design-technology co-optimization, and participate in design of experiments with factory task forces.
  • Develop measurement recipes for rapid feedback on product integrity and address issues impacting yield or product quality.
  • Create and harden systems capable of meeting operational needs for leading-edge logic nodes, working with equipment vendors and internal collaborators.
  • Develop AI/ML applications and computational tools to bridge the gap between design and manufacturing, improve design efficiency, and reduce debug time.
  • Document technical procedures, train colleagues, and debug equipment, software, and procedural failures in production environments when required.

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

We are seeking a transformative, results-driven leader to serve as Senior Director of Competitive and Solutions Marketing. You will architect and guide our centralized intelligence ecosystem, establishing an enterprise-wide source of truth for market conditions, competitive dynamics, growth opportunities, and market response. You will help shape the company's understanding of market opportunities, competition, emerging technology shifts, and investment priorities[WA4.1][RM4.2]. The role will deliver independent, fact-based market perspectives that influence enterprise planning, resource allocation, and strategic decision-making.

This is not a traditional reporting or analytics role. You will lead the evolution of market intelligence, shifting our capability from static, reactive dashboards to an AI-enabled strategic advisory and market response engine.
In this role, you will combine deep human judgment with AI capabilities. You will partner closely with IT to define the business architecture and product requirements for the intelligence system. You will also cultivate a collaborative Intelligence Community that breaks down information silos across departments. By using agentic tools for first-draft synthesis and continuous signal sensing, you will free the team to focus on strategic counsel, objective stress-testing of proposals, and faster, higher-value contributions to decisions across planning cycles.

  • Lead ongoing market and competitive analysis, including positioning, market sizing, forecasting, and emerging industry trends; clarify complex market shifts and identify forward-looking opportunities.

  • Define and lead Intel's vision for AI-enabled market intelligence, using agentic workflows, automated synthesis, predictive modeling, and decision-support systems to increase the speed, scale, and impact of intelligence across the enterprise. Partner with business stakeholders, IT, and external providers to define requirements.
  • Develop market responses that position and differentiate Intel's products and solutions. Establish simple mechanisms for sharing customer and partner feedback and equip teams to use AI to analyze information and communicate findings clearly.
  • Lead, mentor, and evolve a high-caliber team of data scientists and technical marketers, shifting traditional data-gathering and report-building roles toward higher-value strategic consulting, scenario modeling, and intelligence systems design.

  • Systems Thinking: Ability to connect disparate macro, competitive, and customer signals into an integrated, actionable framework for corporate investment.
  • Intellectual Courage: Willingness to provide unvarnished, objective truth and actively challenge internal assumptions, even when they run counter to the prevailing consensus.

Demonstrated success challenging conventional thinking and driving alignment among senior leaders in highly matrixed organizations and executive leadership

  • Design and implement data analytics, dashboards, simulations, and decision-support tools for factory operations.
  • Collaborate with manufacturing engineers, process engineers, automation teams, and IT partners to deliver digital manufacturing solutions.
  • Utilize statistical analysis, machine learning, and data visualization techniques to drive manufacturing optimization.
  • Develop automated monitoring systems and alerts to improve operational responsiveness.
  • Support MES deployments, enhancements, troubleshooting, and system sustainment activities.
  • Identify and implement opportunities for process automation and manufacturing digitalization.

title: Product Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

  • Drives and develops testability and manufacturability of integrated circuits from the component feasibility stage through production ramp.
  • Contributes to design, development, and validation of testability circuits, test flows, and methodologies for new products through evaluation, development, and debug of complex test methods.
  • Interfaces with process development, fab, factory, assembly, quality and reliability, and manufacturing groups to enable postsilicon HVM ramp.

Performs ATE device characterization, utilizes that data to define datasheet specifications and performs yield analysis.
  • Collaborates with designers to drive design for test/debug/manufacturing (DFT/DFD/DFM) features enabling efficient production testing of new products.
  • Develops and debugs complex software programs to convert design validation vectors and drive complex test equipment. Creates and tests validation and production test hardware solutions.
  • Tests, validates, modifies, and redesigns circuits to guarantee component margin to specification.
  • Analyzes and evaluates component specification versus performance to ensure optimal match of component requirements with production equipment capability with specific emphasis on yield analysis and bin split capability.
  • Ensures manufacturability over process and product design through thorough analysis of process and spec corners and works with design to resolve yield issues before manufacturing ramp.
  • Drives test time reduction through analysis of fallout data versus test time for various IPs to balance and drive overall product cost optimizations.
  • Analyzes early customer returns with emphasis on driving test hole closure activities.
  • Creates and applies concepts for optimizing component production relative to both quality and cost constraints.
  • Leads and drives manufacturing readiness from fab, assembly, and test factory to support engineering sample and customer sample generation (ES milestones), wafer start planning, product qual execution strategy and capacity analysis, and assembly and test site certification activities.
  • Works with fab, assembly, and test factory partners and planners to support production ramp.
  • May also manage execution of new product introductions in the fab, fab process targeting, product/process optimizations, and participate in factory task forces to bring product perspective and respond to product issues.
  • Optimizes product supply through data analysis of postsilicon binsplit, die level cherry pick (DLCP), and optimize sort/test content and yield downstream through data analysis.

descriptionHtml:

In this role, you will work across the full AI software stack, focusing on improving performance-critical GPU kernels, graph compilation flows, and inference runtimes. Your contributions will directly enhance the efficiency and scalability of modern AI workloads, helping unlock the full potential of Intel's AI technologies.

Business Group
As part of Intel's Software Group, you will join a team dedicated to delivering innovative software solutions that enable and enhance Intel's AI products. The group plays a pivotal role in developing tools, frameworks, and optimizations that empower developers worldwide, shaping the future of AI-driven applications and advancing Intel's mission to create world-changing technology.

Key Responsibilities
- Optimize AI inference workloads, such as Large Language Models (LLMs), multimodal models, and emerging generative AI applications, for Intel GPUs.
- Design, develop, and tune performance-critical GPU kernels and runtime components using C++, SYCL, Vulkan Compute, OpenCL, or similar parallel programming technologies.
- Develop and optimize graph compilation flows and compiler passes using technologies like MLIR, LLVM, or related frameworks.
- Identify and resolve performance bottlenecks across compiler, runtime, framework, and kernel layers.

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

As a CPU HVM Functional-Test Verification Engineer, you will be part of the DFT team focusing on validating DFT for manufacturing functional testing and delivering functional test content for the manufacturing of Intel's next generation CPU IP designs.
