title: Server Architect
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
As a Principal Engineer in CPU Architecture, you will be at the forefront of developing and driving the end-to-end architectural specifications for cutting-edge, modular, and scalable CPUs that will power the next generation of computing. This role offers the unique opportunity to influence the technical direction of both Intel and the broader industry, ensuring our leadership in performance, power efficiency, and scalability. Your contributions will directly impact Intel's ability to deliver innovative solutions across diverse market segments, from high-performance computing to ultra-low power products. This is a pivotal position that combines technical strategy, architectural innovation, and leadership to shape the future of Intel CPUs.

Key Responsibilities
- Drive the development of CPU architecture specifications, including hardware feature requirements and hardware-software interoperability throughout the product lifecycle.
- Define and evaluate feasibility tradeoffs for performance, power, frequency, area, and features to meet CPU requirements across multiple segments.
- Conceptualize, invent, and specify architectural and microarchitecture features that deliver optimized CPU requirements for varying use cases.
- Develop and document new instructions to support emerging use cases, improve existing ones, and extend the instruction set architecture (ISA).
- Model CPU performance and power, analyze current CPU bottlenecks, and explore novel approaches for future workloads.
- Provide experimental proof-of-concept solutions to propose design alternatives that meet constraints related to performance, power, area, and timing.
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams including architects, design, verification, and validation engineers to execute project requirements seamlessly.
- Deliver new microarchitecture definitions and resolve issues during feature implementation to improve CPU design and overcome challenges.
- Influence and challenge cross-functional roadmaps while defining technology targets for future CPUs.
- Mentor and develop technical leaders, foster community growth, and act as a change agent while exemplifying Intel values in every aspect of your work.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, and 12+ years of relevant experience; or Master's degree and 8+ years of relevant experience; or PhD and 6+ years of relevant experience.
- Proven expertise in CPU architecture definition and feature specification.
- Advanced knowledge of performance and power modeling, bottleneck analysis, and optimization for CPU workloads.
- Experience with instruction set architecture (ISA) development and implementation.

title: TD Memory Quality and Reliability PhD Intern
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Team 

The Technology Development (TD) Quality and Reliability organization plays a critical role in enabling the successful deployment of next-generation semiconductor technologies through silicon-based quality, reliability, and technology readiness assessments. 

The Memory Quality and Reliability team works closely with Design, Device Engineering, Product Development Engineering (PDE), and Yield organizations to develop, characterize, and certify SRAM, Register File (RF), and Fuse technologies for advanced process nodes. The team supports key technology certification and PDK release milestones through memory characterization, silicon data analysis, predictive modeling, and risk assessment. 

Role Overview 

As a TD Memory Quality and Reliability Intern, you will collaborate with experienced engineers to evaluate advanced memory technologies and help drive technology readiness for future Intel Foundry process nodes. This role offers hands-on experience in memory characterization, silicon data analytics, statistical modeling, and semiconductor technology development. 

You will contribute to projects that support technology certification decisions by analyzing silicon data, developing predictive models, and assessing memory performance across various operating conditions. 

Responsibilities 

Responsibilities may include, but are not limited to: 

  • Analyze silicon characterization data from SRAM, Register File (RF), and Fuse memory test structures to identify performance trends, variability, and potential risks. 
  • Support memory characterization activities across voltage, temperature, and process conditions. 
  • Perform data analysis, visualization, and reporting using Python, JMP, or similar analytical tools. 
  • Develop and enhance statistical models for Vmin/Vmax prediction and technology readiness assessments. 
  • Support Silicon-to-Simulation (Sil2Sim) correlation studies and memory characterization methodologies. 
  • Generate technical reports and contribute to technology certification reviews. 
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Design, Device Engineering, Process Integration, Product Development Engineering, and Yield Engineering. 
  • Assist with risk assessment activities and technology certification milestones. 
  • Present data-driven findings and recommendations to engineering teams and project stakeholders. 

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications 

  • Currently pursuing a Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering or a related field. 
  • Basic knowledge of semiconductor devices, microelectronics, or integrated circuit design. 
  • Programming or scripting experience using Python or similar languages. 
  • Experience analyzing technical, scientific, or research data through academic projects, research activities, or previous internships. 
  • Strong academic performance with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher required.

Preferred Qualifications 

Coursework, research, or experience in one or more of the following areas: 

  • SRAM or memory technologies 
  • Semiconductor device physics 
  • VLSI design 
  • Statistics, machine learning, or data science 
  • Semiconductor process technology 

Experience with: 

  • Python, Pandas, and NumPy 
  • JMP or other statistical analysis tools 
  • Data visualization and statistical modeling techniques 
  • Large-scale data analysis and predictive modeling 

Additional experience in memory architectures, silicon characterization, reliability assessment, or semiconductor test methodologies is highly desirable. 

What You Will Learn 

During this internship, you will gain exposure to: 

  • Advanced SRAM, RF, and Fuse memory technologies 
  • Memory characterization and certification methodologies 
  • Silicon data analytics and statistical modeling techniques 
  • Vmin/Vmax evaluation and predictive model development 
  • Technology qualification and certification processes 
  • Cross-functional semiconductor technology development workflows 
  • Silicon-based decision making for technology readiness and risk assessment

title: CPU Physical Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Are you interested in building the next generation of high-performance, power-efficient CPUs?

Join Intel as a CPU Physical Design Engineer and begin your career working on advanced processor technology. In this early-career role, you will work alongside experienced engineers and contribute to the physical design and verification of CPU designs from RTL to GDSII.

You will gain hands-on experience with industry-standard EDA tools and develop expertise across physical design areas including synthesis, floorplanning, place and route, clock implementation, static timing analysis, power optimization, and physical verification.

As part of the CPU Physical Design team, you will collaborate with engineers across logic design, architecture, circuits, and design automation while developing the technical expertise required to solve increasingly complex CPU design challenges.

What You’ll Do

Key responsibilities will include but not limited to:

  • Implement physical design and verification flows for custom CPU designs, ranging from RTL synthesis to GDS generation, custom and memory designs.
  • Perform verification and signoff processes such as formal equivalence verification, layout verification, reliability verification, and timing/power integrity analysis.
  • Collaborate with logic, architecture, circuit, and design automation teams to identify opportunities for design improvements and optimize product-level parameters such as power, frequency, and area.
  • Build and refine physical design methodologies and automation workflows to streamline the design process.
  • Work closely with EDA vendors to enhance tool capabilities for high-speed, low-power CPU design.

Behavioral traits that we are looking for:

  • Learning agility and curiosity: Eager to learn new technologies, tools, and CPU physical design methodologies.
  • Problem solving: Approaches technical challenges analytically and works through problems in a structured manner.
  • Collaboration: Works effectively with others and values different technical perspectives.
  • Initiative and ownership: Proactively seeks information, asks thoughtful questions, and takes responsibility for assigned work.
  • Communication: Clearly communicates technical ideas, questions, results, and challenges.
  • Attention to detail: Demonstrates accuracy and quality when analyzing technical information and completing engineering tasks.
  • Adaptability: Able to learn and grow within a fast-paced technical environment as design requirements and priorities evolve.

You will play a key role in maintaining lab readiness, improving operational efficiency, and ensuring the accuracy and reliability of test results.

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Join Intel Foundry Construction and Sourcing (FCS), a team dedicated to building and optimizing world-class semiconductor manufacturing facilities. FCS drives the construction and tool installation of cutting-edge factories that power Intel's global operations. As part of this group, you'll contribute to groundbreaking projects that shape the future of technology and innovation.

As a key member of the Project Execution Team, the Tool Equipment Install Engineer is an individual contributor reporting to the Tool Install Manager. A key to this role will be close engagement with customers, stakeholders, and partners as well as leadership of the site project execution team.

This is an onsite position in Phoenix, Arizona. This role will require supporting teams to solve site Tool Install Qual constraints, Scheduling Issues, and participating in Task Forces when required. It will require regular on-site engagement with stakeholders as well as virtually working with others across sites.

The primary responsibilities for this role will include, but are not limited to: 


  • Collaborate with Factory owners / stakeholders to ensure Tools/Equipment/Kits are ordered and delivered in alignment with the Tool Install schedule requirements, tracking and resolving any issues timely and escalating as required.
  • Represent local FCS site in Central Tool Install and Virtual Factory forums.
  • Work with Stakeholders to Forecast Equipment workload and funding requirements and ensure alignment with FCS Financial Planning/Reporting Cycles.
  • Ensure commit / PO's are in place for Tools/Equipment/Kits to meet the program goals.
  • Collaborate with EMS and Systems Owners ensuring Systems correctly reflect Equipment requirements and schedule.
  • Drive Systems and Part number configuration/genealogy and accuracy for RFT (right first time) Order / Kits delivery.

title: Senior Foundry Automation Solutions Architect
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Transform the Future of Semiconductor Manufacturing - Intel is transforming its backend manufacturing network operations toward autonomous, lights-out manufacturing. We are building the next generation of factory automation platforms that enable intelligent, scalable, and highly efficient operations across Intel's global backend manufacturing network.

We are seeking a Senior Foundry Automation Solutions Architect to lead the architecture strategy and technology direction behind this transformation. In this highly visible role, you will define and deliver the software architectures that connect Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), equipment automation, robotics, material handling systems, edge computing, Industrial IoT, and AI-driven decision platforms into a unified factory ecosystem.

Working across engineering, factory operations, technology development, IT, and business leadership teams, you will translate strategic automation objectives into scalable, production-ready solutions that drive measurable improvements in factory performance at global scale.

Success in this role will be measured by tangible business outcomes, including reducing manual factory touchpoints to enable zero-touch operations, improving manufacturing efficiency and quality through the elimination of human-induced variability, increasing equipment utilization and throughput, reducing cycle times and operational bottlenecks, improving system availability and resilience, accelerating deployment of new automation capabilities, and establishing reusable architecture standards that can be scaled across Intel's manufacturing network.

This is a unique opportunity to define the architectural foundation for Intel's next generation of autonomous factories. The platforms, standards, and automation frameworks you create will directly influence the future of semiconductor manufacturing and help establish industry-leading operational excellence across Intel's global Assembly and Test operations.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Define architecture strategy, standards, and reference designs for factory automation platforms.
  • Lead the design of scalable, highly available, and mission-critical solutions spanning MES, AMHS, robotics, equipment automation, and Industrial IoT.
  • Drive technology evaluation and pathfinding, technical assessments, and adoption of emerging technologies including AI/ML, edge computing, and intelligent automation.
  • Establish interoperability frameworks, integration patterns, and communication standards across manufacturing systems.
  • Provide technical leadership and architectural governance across multiple programs and factory sites.
  • Partner with senior stakeholders to align technology investments with business priorities and manufacturing objectives.
  • Mentor engineers and architects while elevating architectural excellence across the organization.

Impact
Success in this role will be measured by:

  • Accelerating Intel's journey toward autonomous and lights-out manufacturing.
  • Reducing manual factory touchpoints and enabling zero-touch operations.
  • Improving equipment utilization, throughput, cycle time, quality, and operational resilience.
  • Accelerating deployment of new automation capabilities and technology transfers.
  • Establishing scalable architecture standards and reusable platforms across Intel's manufacturing network.
  • Enabling sustainable improvements in factory performance and operational excellence.

Qualifications:

We're looking for a senior technology leader who combines deep software architecture expertise with a passion for industrial automation and large-scale operational transformation.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related field.
  • 10+ years of experience designing and delivering complex distributed software systems.
  • 5+ years in a Lead Architect, Principal Engineer, Solutions Architect, Systems Architect, or equivalent technical leadership role.
  • Expertise in distributed systems, event-driven architectures, microservices, messaging platforms, and highly available systems.
  • Experience with cloud-native, edge, or hybrid architectures for mission-critical environments.
  • Strong knowledge of industrial integration standards including SECS/GEM, GEM300, OPC-UA, MQTT, REST, and gRPC.
  • Proven ability to drive technical strategy and influence cross-functional and executive stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications:


  • Semiconductor manufacturing, Assembly and Test, wafer fabrication, or advanced manufacturing automation experience.
  • Experience leading lights-out or autonomous factory initiatives.
  • Knowledge of MES, scheduling, dispatching, robotics, AMHS, AGV, or AMR solutions.
  • Experience with Docker, Kubernetes, k3s, Industrial IoT, and edge computing platforms.
  • Familiarity with Kafka, AI/ML-enabled automation, and OT cybersecurity.
  • Candidates from advanced manufacturing, robotics, logistics automation, and Industry 4.0 environments are encouraged to apply.

Join us in defining the architecture and technology foundation for Intel's next generation of autonomous factories.

The Role and Impact As a Facilities Life Safety Systems Technician, you will play a crucial role in ensuring the safety and operational effectiveness of Intel's life safety systems, including fire alarms, HPM Systems, and related equipment. You will provide hands-on expertise, system design reviews, and proactive support to optimize these systems for compliance and performance. title: Graduate Talent (CPU-SoC Silicon Design)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

In this position, you will be involving in the training, design and development of next generation SOC/CPU for wide range of Intel products. Your responsibilities will include some of the following but not limited to:

  • Assist design unit owner in Register Transfer Level RTL model functional validation. Use CAD tool extensively to simulate logic behavior and circuit performance and direction of physical design for next generation, deep sub-micron embedded circuit solutions. Verify the circuit behavior against the original simulation model and first silicon.
  • Define VLSI Structural Design methodology and developing design flows. Implement structural physical designs, such as synthesis, floor planning, power-grid and clock tree designs, timing budgeting and closure, place and route, RC-extraction and integration. Verify structural physical designs, such as functional equivalency, timing/performance, noise, layout design rules, reliability and power.
  • Develop Analog IP on next generation deep submicron process for the Intel's SOC, perform tasks related to Very-large-scale integration VLSI complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor CMOS IC design, Solid state physics and physical layout. Such tasks may include: Circuit design of high speed clocking related circuits [phase-locked loop PLL, delay-locked loop DLL, bandgap] or high voltage input/output IO [double data rate DDR/LPDDR, General-purpose input/output GPIO, OPIO].
  • Responsible for Integration of Third party IPs -- Synthesis, functional and/or timing convergence, and pre and post-si debug of IPs developed by various external vendors as well as within the company. Handling of signals crossing power planes and clock domains, industry standard protocols including hardware and software details dealing with Memory LPDDR, storage eMMC, SATA, UFS, peripherals PCIe, USB, and MIPI interfaces in SOC devices. System integration dealing with Si/ Platform/ FW/ MW/ drivers/ OS/ Apps on Android Windows-based tablets and phones.

Qualifications:

You must possess a Bachelor of Engineering degree or a Master of Science degree in Electronic, Electrical or Computer Engineering.

Additional qualifications include:

  • Familiarity with Very Large Scale Integration VLSI Complementary Metal-Oxide Semiconductor CMOS logic circuit design
  • Well versed in UNIX, C programming and relevant Computer Aided Design CAD tools.

title: Logic Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact :
Join Intel as an SoC Logic Design Engineer, where you will play a pivotal role in developing the logic design for Intel's next-generation Client System-on-Chip (SoC) products. You will contribute to the RTL design, integration of high-performance IPs, and optimization of core functionalities, ensuring world-class technology that powers devices globally. Your work will directly influence product innovation and performance, driving advancements in computing technology.

Business group :
This role is part of the Silicon and Platform Engineering Group (SPE), which focuses on developing cutting-edge semiconductor solutions and delivering world-class silicon products. SPE drives innovation in Client SoCs by integrating advanced IPs and ensuring high-quality functionality to support Intel's mission of creating technology that enriches lives and shapes the future of computing.

Key Responsibilities :

  • Develop RTL designs for internal IPs or integrate high-performance, bandwidth IPs into SoCs.
  • Collaborate with verification teams to ensure functional, feature, and integration validation.
  • Perform quality checks across RTL static analysis, synthesizability assessments, timing/power convergence, netlist quality verification, and functional equivalence validation.
  • Work with design teams and architects to ensure functional integrity, performance, and overall chip quality.
  • Provide innovative solutions for design optimization and contribute to cross-functional reviews.
  • Follow secure development practices to address security threat models and meet design integrity standards.
  • Collaborate with IP providers to integrate and validate IPs at the SoC level, ensuring smooth IP/SoC handoff.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications :

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field with 3+ years of hands-on experience in SoC RTL/Logic Design, demonstrated through internships, academic projects, coursework, or hands-on training OR a Master's degree in Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field with no prior professional experience.
  • Proficiency in RTL design languages such as SystemVerilog.
  • Basic understanding of digital design concepts, including timing analysis, power optimization, and synthesis techniques.
  • Familiarity with verification methodologies such as OVM/UVM.

Preferred Qualifications :

  • Experience with logic design, integration of high-performance IPs, or pre-silicon validation environments.
  • Knowledge of industry-standard tools for RTL simulation, synthesis, and static timing analysis.
  • Strong problem-solving and communication skills to thrive in a collaborative team environment.

If you're passionate about technology and aspire to contribute to world-changing innovations, we encourage you to take the next step in your career with Intel today.

title: Product Quality and Reliability Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Product Quality and Reliability Modeling Engineer develops reliability models and risk assessments that enable successful qualification and launch of advanced semiconductor products. Working across Product Quality & Reliability, Design, Process, Manufacturing, and Foundry teams, this role applies device physics, reliability engineering, statistical analysis, and data science to predict product reliability, identify risks, and drive data-driven decisions throughout the product lifecycle.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute reliability models to assess product lifetime and qualification readiness.  
  • Evaluate failure mechanisms including EM, TDDB, BTI, HCI, thermal and package-related degradation.
  • Analyze qualification, characterization, and manufacturing data to quantify reliability risk.
  • Conduct reliability projections, scenario analysis, and risk assessments for new product features and technologies.
  • Drive cross-functional investigations and resolution of reliability concerns.
  • Improve modeling methodologies, automation, and predictive analytics capabilities.
  • Present reliability recommendations to technical and management stakeholders.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

  • MS or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Materials Science, Reliability Engineering, or related field.
  • Experience of 2-5 years with M.Tech/Phd and B.tech with 5+ years.
  • Strong understanding of semiconductor device physics and advanced packaging.
  • Experience in reliability modeling, accelerated stress testing, and qualification methodologies.
  • Knowledge of EM, TDDB, BTI, HCI, package reliability, and wear-out mechanisms.
  • Proficiency with Python, JMP, MATLAB, Minitab, or equivalent analytical tools.
  • Strong statistical, problem-solving, and communication skills.
  • Experience in reliability validation, product development, test engineering.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting PRQ/qualification decisions.
  • Experience with advanced node or advanced packaging technologies.
  • Knowledge of AI/ML techniques for reliability prediction.
  • Demonstrated technical leadership across complex product programs.

Ideal Candidate: A self-driven engineer capable of independently leading reliability assessments, influencing qualification decisions, and driving risk closure across multiple semiconductor product programs.

title: Senior F5 Application Delivery Network Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Role

Intel Information Technology (IT) is seeking a Senior F5 Application Delivery Network Engineer join a high-performing team responsible for delivering secure, reliable, and scalable application delivery services across Intel's global enterprise environment.

In this role, you will serve as a senior technical contributor responsible for designing, implementing, automating, and supporting enterprise-scale application delivery and load-balancing solutions. You will collaborate with network engineering, security, cloud, infrastructure, and application teams to ensure business-critical services remain highly available, secure, and optimized for performance.

The ideal candidate combines deep expertise in F5 technologies with strong problem-solving skills, a continuous-improvement mindset, and a passion for building and operating highly available infrastructure at scale.

What You’ll Do

Key responsibilities will include but not limited to:

  • Provide senior-level engineering expertise for F5 BIG-IP application delivery platforms.
  • Engineer, configure, test, and support application delivery and load-balancing solutions.
  • Lead troubleshooting and resolution of complex F5 and application connectivity issues.
  • Serve as a senior escalation point for critical production and manufacturing incidents.
  • Drive platform availability, resiliency, standardization, and continuous improvement.
  • Lead evaluation, testing, pilot, and production readiness activities for major architecture, operating system, and configuration changes.
  • Develop and maintain standardized configurations, engineering documentation, operating procedures, and troubleshooting knowledge.
  • Lead or support platform lifecycle activities, including software upgrades and end-of-support/end-of-life refresh.
  • Partner with manufacturing engineering teams on testing, releases, critical changes, factory shutdown activities, and complex production issues.
  • Work with F5 and other technology suppliers on complex technical issues and product escalations.
    Review application requirements and translate them into secure, scalable, and highly available application delivery solutions.
  • Identify opportunities for automation and self-service to improve engineering efficiency and reduce operational risk.
  • Participate in technical reviews and provide engineering guidance for new capabilities and deployments.
  • Mentor junior engineers and help build deeper technical capability across the team.

Behavioral traits that we are looking for:

  • Strong ownership and accountability for service reliability and operational excellence.
  • Ability to effectively manage priorities and make sound decisions in fast-paced environments.
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills with a structured approach to troubleshooting.
  • A continuous-learning mindset and curiosity for emerging technologies.
  • Strong collaboration and relationship-building skills across technical and non-technical teams.
  • Ability to influence through technical expertise, communication, and partnership.
  • Commitment to documentation, process improvement, and knowledge sharing.
  • Customer-focused thinking with an understanding of business impact and service quality.
  • Resilience and composure during production incidents and critical situations.
  • A proactive approach to identifying risks, opportunities, and operational improvements.

Intel invests in our people and offers a complete and competitive package of benefits employees and their families through every stage of life. 

  • See  Intel Benefits for more details. 

Qualifications:

title: GPU Validation Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact:


As a GPU Validation Engineer, you will play a critical role in ensuring the functional accuracy, performance, and reliability of Intel's cutting-edge GPUs. You will define, develop, and execute robust validation methodologies to test interactions between GPU features across hardware and software layers. Your work will directly impact the quality and performance of Intel GPUs, enabling seamless integration into diverse systems and driving innovation in graphics and compute technologies.

Business group :
You will be part of Intel's Data Center Group (DCG), which leads the development of technologies that power the world's data-centric infrastructure. This group focuses on shaping the future of cloud computing, AI, and high-performance computing by delivering solutions that advance Intel's leadership in data processing and connectivity. Joining DCG offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to groundbreaking products that support Intel's broader mission of enabling global progress through technology.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop and execute functional validation plans for GPUs, ensuring comprehensive test coverage across hardware and software components.
  • Analyze and debug silicon issues to identify root causes, resolve failures, and optimize GPU designs.
  • Test and validate system-level interactions between GPU features using advanced validation infrastructure.
  • Collaborate with architecture, design, verification, and manufacturing teams to refine validation methodologies and processes.
  • Review proposed design changes to assess their impact on validation timelines, tasks, and performance goals.
  • Design and implement post-silicon validation infrastructure, including behavioral checkers, performance monitors, and coverage tools.
  • Publish detailed validation reports summarizing key findings, results, and recommendations.
  • Maintain and improve validation strategies to support product specifications and enhance overall GPU functionality.
  • Defines, develops, and performs functional validation for GPUs, focusing on validation of interaction of GPUs, media, display and system level features. Applies various hardware and software level tools and techniques to ensure validation coverage and that performance, power, and area goals are met.
  • Reviews proposed design changes to assess impact on validation plans, tasks, and timelines.
  • Develops GPU validation methodologies, executes validation plans, and collaborates with other engineers for design optimization, troubleshooting, and failure analysis.
  • Performs silicon debug to identify root causes and resolves all functional and triage failures for GPU issues. Tests interactions between various GPU features using validation infrastructure.
  • Develops post silicon validation infrastructure (e.g., performance monitors, behavioral checkers, state space coverage) and test environment used in validation testing.
  • Publishes GPU validation reports summarizing all validation activities performed, reviews results, and communicates to relevant teams.
  • Works with architecture, design, verification, board, platform, and manufacturing teams to maintain and improve debug, validation test strategy, methodologies, and processes for graphics interfaces and to meet desired product specifications.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in a relevant field and 9+ years of experience, or a Master's degree with 6+ years, or a Ph.D. with 4+ years working in GPU validation, silicon debugging, or related domains.
  • Proficiency in validation tools and techniques, including hardware validation infrastructure and software-based testing methodologies.
  • Experience with silicon debug processes, triage failure analysis, and system-level validation.
  • Strong technical expertise in GPU architecture, media, and display technologies.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop and execute validation plans aligned with design and performance goals.

Preferred Qualifications:


  • Proven experience collaborating with cross-functional engineering teams to drive design optimizations and resolve technical challenges.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a focus on continuous improvement in validation processes.
  • Effective communication skills to present findings and recommendations through clear and concise reports.
  • Passion for innovation and a proactive mindset to contribute to advancements in GPU technologies.
  • Proven experience in platform validation, low power flow management, memory expertise and ( GDDR/LPDDR ) debugging, and test content development, with a focus on reset/boot/low power functionalities.
  • Strong understanding of server architectures, hardware components, and operating systems.
  • Proficiency in scripting languages (e.g., Python) for test automation, debugging, and test content development.
  • Experience with validation, debugging, and test content development tools and frameworks (e.g., Jenkins, GDB, WinDbg).
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively in a team environment.
  • Familiarity with version control systems (e.g., Git) and issue tracking tools (e.g., JIRA).
  • Knowledge of industry standards and best practices related to server reset, platform validation, debugging, and test content development.

Your work will help define the future of graphics processing technology, creating opportunities to grow, develop, and make a lasting impact through meaningful contributions to Intel's product excellence and innovation.

title: Senior Analog Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The world is transforming - and so is Intel. Intel is a company of bold and curious inventors and problem solvers who create some of the most astounding technology advancements and experiences in the world. With a legacy of relentless innovation and a commitment to bring smart, connected devices to every person on Earth, our diverse and brilliant teams are continually searching for tomorrow's technology and revel in the challenge that changing the world for the better brings. We work every single day to design and manufacture silicon products that empower people's digital lives. Come join us and do something wonderful.


Business group

Intel Integrated Photonics Solutions (IPS), part of the Data Center Group, is a leader in silicon photonics integration. Our team drives innovation through advanced technology and scalable, high-volume manufacturing of silicon photonics products. We are committed to developing next-generation optical connectivity solutions that enable continued data center bandwidth growth through smaller form factors, co-packaged optics, and data rates scaling from 400G today to 3.2T and beyond.
 

The Role and Impact

We are seeking a highly motivated Senior Analog Design Engineer to join our growing team and help accelerate the development of industry-leading silicon photonics solutions. As a Senior Analog Design Engineer, you will contribute to the Silicon Photonics Solutions Group's mission of transforming data center connectivity and strengthening Intel's leadership in networking technologies.


In this role, you will be responsible for:

  • The architecture, design, implementation, and validation of high-speed analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits used in advanced optical interconnect products.
  • You will collaborate closely with cross-functional design teams to deliver innovative solutions from concept through production.
  • Define circuit architectures and develop designs that meet power, performance, and functionality requirements for next-generation optical interconnects.
  • Lead block-level design and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to deliver key integrated circuit components.
  • Architect, design, and validate high-speed, low-voltage, low-power analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits.
  • Work closely with digital design teams to ensure successful integration and product execution.
  • Plan and execute design activities while balancing performance, schedule, and quality objectives.
  • Guide to the development of post-silicon test and characterization plans.
  • Create and maintain comprehensive design documentation, including design specifications, reviews, and technical reports.

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Experience listed below would be obtained through a combination of your degree, research and or relevant previous job and or internship experiences.

M.S. degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field with 4+ years of industry experience or PhD & 2+ years in the following:

  • Hands-on experience designing high-speed circuit blocks such as amplifiers, drivers, equalizers, PLLs, phase interpolators, and clock and data recovery (CDR) circuits for data rates of 32 Gbps and above.
  • Experience designing inductors, transmission lines, transimpedance amplifiers (TIAs), and optical modulator drivers.
  • Strong expertise in high-speed serial link design and analog CMOS/BiCMOS circuit design using deep-submicron process technologies.
  • Experience with full-chip integration, ESD design considerations, and verification methodologies.



Preferred Qualifications:

  • Strong understanding of mixed-signal design methodologies and flows.

title: APCC Shift Operations Manager
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Advanced Packaging Command Center (APCC) Shift Group Leader is a people manager responsible for leading a shift-based operations team that provides remote manufacturing and technical support to factory operations. This role ensures safe, reliable, disciplined and consistent execution of APCC services while maintaining strong partnership with supported factory teams and global stakeholders. The Shift Group Leader is accountable for people leadership, shift execution, operational performance, service quality, escalation management, capability development and continuous improvement. The role requires sound decision-making in a fast-paced manufacturing environment where priorities change rapidly, supported by a solid understanding of the semiconductor manufacturing flow to lead defect-related operational response and drive cross-functional problem solving across APCC and supported factories. Key Responsibilities People and Shift Leadership - Lead, supervise and develop APCC Technicians, Commanders and Runners supporting remote factory operations across assigned sites, technologies and service areas. - Own core people-management responsibilities, including onboarding, goal setting, performance management, recognition and handling of employee relations matters. - Ensure effective 24/7 shift operations, including staffing, attendance, overtime management, workload balancing, shift coverage and task prioritization. - Provide clear leadership and direction during rapidly changing manufacturing situations, balancing operational priorities, technical risk and service commitments. - Ensure team members complete required training and certification (e.g., L1O/L2O) and that training materials remain current with the latest specs and processes. - Build team capability through coaching, knowledge sharing, technical development and disciplined execution of standard work. - Establish an environment of safety, accountability, teamwork, continuous learning and effective cross-functional collaboration. Operational Execution and Escalation Management - Ensure timely response, acknowledgement, disposition and escalation of manufacturing or technical events in accordance with established procedures and service expectations. - Enforce compliance with the operating spec, escalation timelines and follow-up expectations. - Coordinate work across APCC, factory operations, engineering, equipment, automation, manufacturing and other stakeholder organizations, including global sites across time zones, to ensure issues are properly owned and resolved. - Serve as the primary shift leadership escalation point for operational abnormalities, high-impact events, staffing constraints, service disruptions and issues requiring management intervention. - Maintain effective shift-to-shift handover, ensuring significant events, open actions, risks and escalation status are clearly communicated. - Provide shift reports and operations review inputs and communicate significant events to management and site stakeholders. - Ensure compliance with EHS, information security, access control and data integrity requirements. Technical Leadership - Provide shift leadership for quality/Yield-related manufacturing events, ensuring appropriate initial assessment, containment, escalation, ownership and follow-through in partnership with manufacturing, process, yield, quality and engineering teams. - Apply knowledge of the semiconductor manufacturing flow to understand how upstream process conditions in wafer fabrication, wafer-level packaging and sort/test may appear as downstream defect or yield signals. - Use problem solving methodology and technical data to guide problem definition, challenge defect classification and disposition where needed, and route issues to the appropriate engineering owners. - Distinguish immediate operational containment needs from issues requiring deeper engineering investigation,and ensure repeat or systematic defects have clear ownership for root cause, corrective action and follow-up. Operational Performance and Continuous Improvement - Monitor operational data, KPIs, dashboards and trends to identify execution gaps, recurring issues and improvement opportunities. - Drive disciplined adoption of standard work, operational governance and continuous-improvement practices. - Partner with technical and operational stakeholders to improve execution consistency, responsiveness and service quality. - Ensure lessons learnt from manufacturing events, defect excursions and operational gaps are incorporated into team capability development and standard work where appropriate. - Drive follow-through on recurring operational or technical issues until sustainable corrective actions and ownership are established.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications - Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Science or a related technical discipline. - 3+ years of experience as a people manager, shift leader or team leader of a factory/technical team of five or more employees, with responsibility for technical or operational deliverables. - Understanding of the end-to-end semiconductor manufacturing flow, with working knowledge of at least one of the following: wafer fabrication, wafer-level packaging or sort/test. - Ability to understand technical data and use it to support problem definition, operational decision-making and appropriate engineering escalation. - Demonstrated experience coordinating multiple priorities, managing escalations and delivering results in a time-sensitive operating environment. - Demonstrated ability to coach and develop team members and to make sound decisions under pressure. - Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, including with global stakeholders and senior leaders. - Strong interpersonal skills with demonstrated ability to work effectively in a diverse and cross-functional team environment. - Demonstrated ability to operate effectively in ambiguous situations and maintain commitment to operational deliverables. - Willingness and ability to work in a compressed work week and shift-based operating model, including coordination with stakeholders across time zones. Preferred Qualifications - 6+ years of experience in semiconductor manufacturing, engineering, operations or technical support, including 3+ years leading teams. - Proven track record leading a team in a 24/7 high-volume manufacturing, command center, remote operations or factory support environment. - Working knowledge of semiconductor defect methodology and the ability to relate process conditions, defect signals and yield/quality excursions across the manufacturing flow. - Hands-on or leadership experience with wafer fabrication, wafer-level packaging and/or sort/test manufacturing operations. - Experience supporting semiconductor defect, yield or quality excursions. - Experience interpreting defect maps/images, defect Pareto/trend information, process data and equipment signals to support defect investigation and escalation. - Knowledge of structured problem-solving methodologies such as 8D, root-cause analysis, containment and corrective/preventive action. - Strong understanding of manufacturing operations, equipment support, process control, operational escalation and factory execution systems. - Knowledge of, or demonstrated aptitude for learning, manufacturing systems, automation platforms, dashboards and operational tools. - Experience using operational data, KPIs, dashboards and trend analysis to drive performance improvements. - Experience implementing standard work, operational governance, continuous improvement or quality management practices. - Experience collaborating across process, yield, equipment, manufacturing and quality engineering organizations to resolve complex manufacturing issues. We invite you to bring your experience and leadership skills to Intel and join us in driving innovation, optimizing operations, and empowering our teams to achieve their full potential.

title: Packaging Module Engineering Technician
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel Corporation is a global technology pioneer, designing and manufacturing the crucial silicon foundations that power the world’s digital infrastructure. You will join Intel's highly collaborative Advanced Packaging and Assembly team—a critical group focused on driving breakthrough packaging innovations. Our mission is to enhance production efficiency, optimize next-generation assembly processes, and deliver world-class semiconductor packaging solutions to customers globally.


We are seeking a detail-oriented and collaborative Packaging Module Engineering Technician to support advanced packaging technology development in Arizona. Operating in a state-of-the-art laboratory environment, this fully on-site role focuses on preparing samples, running analytical testing, and evaluating materials. You will work side-by-side with research engineers to generate high-quality analytical data that directly influences semiconductor process optimization, quality control, and failure analysis.

• Perform materials characterization and analysis using microscopy, imaging, acoustic inspection, and other analytical techniques.
• Prepare samples and coupons for testing through cross-sectioning, polishing, etching, ion milling, spin coating, and related preparation methods.

• Maintain laboratory equipment through routine maintenance, calibration, and basic troubleshooting.
• Ensure compliance with laboratory safety, quality, and documentation standards.
• Collaborate with engineers and cross-functional teams to execute experiments and deliver timely analytical support.
• Perform chemical handling, wet processing, and experiments in accordance with laboratory safety protocols and environmental health and safety (EHS) requirements.

As a Successful Candidate, You Will Bring:

  • Analytical & Solution-Oriented: A natural curiosity and logical approach to resolving nonstandard process, testing, and equipment issues.
  • Collaborative Communicator: Excellent interpersonal and communication skills to work effectively with cross-functional engineering and research teams.
  • Rigorous Attention to Detail: Outstanding precision, organization, and a steadfast commitment to laboratory quality and safety protocols.

title: WPM Integration: Defect Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Wafer Packaging Manufacturing organization is a global team at the heart of Intel's advanced packaging technology and high-volume manufacturing. Our vision is clear: optimize advanced packaging HVM processes end-to-end to maximize yield, quality, and customer satisfaction. WPM spans a broad and critical portfolio - including EMIB and Foveros wafer processing, TSV reveal, C4 bumping, Die Prep, and Wafer Level Assembly - supporting Intel's most strategic technologies across multiple sites worldwide

As a WPM Advanced Packaging Defect Reduction Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in protecting yield and elevating defect performance across some of the world's most advanced semiconductor packaging processes. Partnering with module engineering, QNR, manufacturing operations, and yield teams across our global network, you will bring together HVM manufacturing expertise with the technical rigor of a development organization to deliver impactful, lasting solutions. At WPM, we are more than a team - we are an organization that learns, grows, and succeeds and fails together, fostering a culture of trust, continuous improvement, and shared accountability where every individual's contribution drives our collective success.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own assigned advanced packaging layer(s), ensuring all POR defect inspection, classification, and review operations are properly established with healthy inspection recipes and NPI procedures defined.
  • Drive ADC implementation to ensure accurate defect classifications and maintain defect classification specs and Defect Menagerie for all assigned layers.
  • Partner with metro tool owners to set up and maintain SPC charts for every defect mode and layer, create OCAPs for Metro MTs and module engineering to respond to OOC events and defect tracers.
  • Own process health and product quality for the WPM manufacturing line, including defect performance, yield trends, excursions, and baseline process changes.
  • Own defect excursions through resolution, including containment, wafer/lot risk assessment, disposition, root cause, downstream impact, quality events, and non-POR material.
  •  Drive systematic defect reduction and process improvement using process/metrology data, SORT data, DOEs, FRECLs, ATVs, and experiments with process modules.

  •  Extract, analyze, and correlate data to improve defects, yields, and VF matching, identifying key toolsets driving defects through analysis, MBPS, and FA.
  • Quantify chronic defect gaps to goal, document roadmaps to close gaps, and ensure defect health dashboards are operational and incorporated into factory business processes.
  • Communicate defect metrics and findings to module and factory stakeholders through weekly summaries and strategic quarterly reviews, while providing defect training to technicians, peers, and module teams.

    • Data extraction, synthesis, and analysis using tools such as SQL and Python.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with design of experiments (DOE), statistical process control (SPC), and process capability analysis.

title: Verification Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel is seeking a highly qualified candidate to join our ASIC design verification team in a dynamic and forward-thinking organization focused on next-generation semiconductor product development. Our team focuses on being nimble, adaptable, lean and efficient to drive cutting-edge, customer impacting technology development. We embrace innovative and efficient methodologies that drive at-scale product execution. Advance your career with cutting-edge verification techniques including coverage-driven verification, formal methods, and performance analysis. Lead custom SystemVerilog/UVM development, master industry-standard EDA tools, architect verification strategies for complex ASICs, and mentor emerging talent while independently driving verification closure. Join our fast-paced semiconductor team where your technical leadership shapes next-generation chip development through comprehensive methodologies and innovative verification solutions. Transform challenging projects into career-defining achievements. If you are passionate about building products faster and more efficiently than anyone else on the planet, we want you on our team.


Key Responsibilities:
• Define Project Specific Verification Strategy: Defines and implement scalable and reusable verification plans, test benches, and the verification environments for blocks, subsystems, and SoCs. Ensure meeting the required coverage levels and confirm to microarchitecture specifications.
• Lead Verification Execution: Create detailed test plans and drives technical reviews with design and architecture teams to validate these plans and proofs.
• Executes verification plan: Implement and run block/subsystem/cluster/soc simulation models to verify the design, analyze power and performance, and identify bugs.
• Investigate and Resolve Bugs: Replicates, root causes, and debugs issues in the pre-silicon environment. Finds and implements corrective measures to resolve failing tests.
• Collaborate Across Teams: Work closely with SoC architects, micro architects, full chip architects, RTL developers, post-silicon, and physical design teams to improve verification of complex architectural and microarchitectural features.
• Enhance Future Verification Methodologies: Continuously improves existing functional verification infrastructure and methodologies.
• Absorbs learnings: From post-silicon on the quality of validation done during pre-silicon development, updates test plan for missing coverages and proliferates to future products.
• Lead and mentor others: inspire and guide junior engineers, fostering their growth and development.

Your expertise will be instrumental in cultivating a collaborative and innovative environment where every team member thrives.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications: You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. • Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or in other relevant STEM related degree. • 6+ years of experience in ASIC/FPGA design verification • Strong understanding of object-oriented programming (OOP) principles and their application in SystemVerilog UVM or other verification methodologies. • Developing UVM and/or Formal based verification architectures and methodologies. • Experience with industry standard protocols (AMBA AXI/AXI-S/CHI and Low-speed communication protocols (UART, SPI, I2C/I3C)) • Hands-on experience with simulators (Synopsys VCS, Cadence Xcelium, or equivalent). • Familiarity with coverage-driven verification, constrained-random testing and strong debugging skills. • Experience with scripting languages. Preferred Qualifications: • Graduate/post-graduate degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or any STEM related degree with overall 8+ yrs. of experience. • Skilled in various validation concepts and debug techniques relevant to ASIC/FPGA domain. • Collaborative, able to communicate well with counter parts and stakeholders. Strong written and verbal communication skills. • Strong analytical ability and problem-solving skills. • Experience in defining testbench architecture, constrained random verification methodologies. • Experience in processor-based verification using C/C++ with UVM-based verification environments. • Define and execute validation of IPs and/or SOC from spec to tape-in including setting verification strategy, creating test bench and components, defining test plan, writing tests, debugging, coverage and analysis. • Low power experience (e.g., UPF). • Experience in AMBA, CXS stream, DDR, PCIe and/or Ethernet, UCIe protocols. • Experience in EDA tools and reusable testbench for subsystem and SoC that deploys 3rd party VIPs. • Experience with formal verification techniques and tools is an asset.

title: Senior Network Security/AI Software Engineering
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Senior Network Security Software Development Engineer will lead the architecture, development, and delivery of open-source, high-performance network security and AI reference solutions for the Network Software Enabling team in the Enterprise/Cloud Networking segment. This role works closely with architects, customers, and ecosystem partners to define technical requirements and to build reference workloads, with best known methods and configurations, optimized for Intel® Xeon® processors and accelerators across on-prem, edge, and cloud deployments.

The successful candidate will drive the design and optimization of security data planes and AI-enabled security workloads. These include Next-Generation Firewall, Secure Web Gateway, SD-WAN etc. focusing on key performance areas such as scale-up, load distribution, crypto processing, pattern matching, and the migration to AI-driven security functions. The role requires expertise in high-performance packet processing, network security functions, hardware acceleration, performance engineering, and deployment automation.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the architecture and technical roadmap for one or more network security reference solutions, and keep design consistent across the portfolio.
  • Design and optimize packet-processing and security pipelines for throughput, latency, and TCO on current and upcoming Intel® Xeon® platforms.
  • Integrate hardware acceleration technologies (QAT, AVX-512/AMX, NIC offloads) into open-source security stacks such as Snort3, VPP, and Hyperscan.
  • Enable and optimize AI/ML models for security use cases such as malicious URL detection, phishing and fraud detection, anomaly detection, and encrypted traffic analysis, utilizing technologies such as OpenVINO™, vLLM.
  • Lead performance characterization, define benchmarking methods, and produce the collateral that shows customer value.
  • Drive Infrastructure as Code (IaC) automation for cloud and edge deployment, provisioning, and benchmarking using tools such as Terraform, Packer, and Ansible.
  • Evaluate emerging network security, AI, and platform technologies, and drive innovation through proofs of concept and reference implementations.
  • Provide technical leadership, mentor engineers, and lead design and code reviews.
  • Represent the team with customers, partners, and upstream open-source communities to speed up adoption of Intel-powered solutions.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • 10+ years of experience in networking or systems software development.
  • Strong programming skills in C and/or C++/Rust on Linux, with Python, PowerShell or Bash for tooling.
  • Hands-on experience with high-performance networking technologies such as DPDK, VPP, or kernel networking/XDP.
  • Exposure to AI/ML technologies and concepts, such as model training and inference, neural network architectures (CNNs, transformers), and LLMs, and how they apply to network security workloads.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with a proven ability to lead technical work across teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.
  • Strong background in network security: firewall, IPS/IDS, IPsec/TLS, VPN, or deep packet inspection (DPI) and pattern matching.
  • Experience with AI/ML training and inference optimization (including model compression) for security use cases, using frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, OpenVINO™, and vLLM.

  • Track record of profiling and tuning performance at the microarchitecture level.
  • Experience with containers, Kubernetes, and cloud or edge deployment automation.
  • Experience integrating hardware acceleration technologies (QAT, NIC offloads) and vectorized optimization of software pipelines.
  • Experience with Snort3, Hyperscan, or comparable IPS and pattern-matching engines.
  • Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines and Infrastructure as Code tools.

title: AI Software Engineer - AI Frameworks
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Overview:


We are seeking a dynamic and passionate AI software engineer to join Intel's Data Center and AI group (DCAI). In this role, you will design and develop optimizations for high-performance AI serving and training frameworks such as SGLang, vLLM, and PyTorch. You will contribute to Intel's AI framework software stack and help enable and optimize state-of-the-art solutions for Intel's AI accelerators and next-generation GPUs. This position requires deep expertise in framework internals, scheduling, memory management, and kernel optimization for production AI workloads.


Roles and Responsibilities:


  • Design and develop custom GPU kernels for AI framework operations including attention mechanisms, collective operations, and computation primitives to optimize performance on Intel accelerators and GPUs. 
  • Optimize and enhance framework components including scheduling, memory management, and execution pipeline architecture to improve throughput, latency, and resource utilization. 
  • Write and integrate high-performance kernels using GPU programming frameworks to maximize throughput and minimize latency. 
  • Identify and implement optimization opportunities in the framework stack for production AI workloads. 
  • Collaborate with the open-source community (SGLang, vLLM, PyTorch, and others), participate in upstream development, and integrate new innovations into production software. 
  • Debug and optimize complex multi-layered systems involving kernel execution, memory hierarchies, and distributed AI scenarios. 

Qualifications:

Qualifications:


  • Bachelor's degree (B.Tech) or Master's degree (M.S./M.Tech) in Computer Science, Electronics and Communications Engineering (ECE), or a related field, with 6 to 12 years of professional experience. 
  • Advanced proficiency in C++ (C++14/17) and intermediate skills in Python and parallel programming. 
  • Proven, hands-on experience writing and optimizing GPU kernels. Demonstrated expertise in kernel development for machine learning operations such as GEMM, attention mechanisms (including Flash Attention), collective operations, and sampling. 
  • In-depth, hands-on experience with AI frameworks—SGLang, vLLM, PyTorch, or similar production-grade serving and training systems. Deep understanding of their internal architecture, scheduling mechanisms, and memory management strategies is essential.

  • Published or open-source contributions demonstrating kernel optimization expertise. 
  • Knowledge of compiler algorithms for heterogeneous systems and kernel fusion optimizations. 
  • Contributions to or deep familiarity with SGLang, vLLM, PyTorch, or other open-source AI frameworks. 
  • Experience with distributed AI workloads, multi-GPU scheduling, and optimization across heterogeneous hardware.

title: Power Integrity Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The world is transforming - and so is Intel. Intel is a company of bold and curious inventors and problem solvers who create some of the most astounding technology advancements and experiences in the world. With a legacy of relentless innovation and a commitment to bring smart, connected devices to every person on Earth, our diverse and brilliant teams are continually searching for tomorrow's technology and revel in the challenge that changing the world for the better brings. We work every single day to design and manufacture silicon products that empower people's digital lives. Come join us and do something wonderful.


As a Power Integrity Engineer, you will contribute to the development and validation of power delivery solutions for complex, high-speed silicon, package, and platform designs. You will work with cross-functional engineering teams to analyze, optimize, and validate power delivery networks from silicon through package and board.

Your responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:
• Develop and analyze power delivery networks (PDNs) for silicon, packages, boards, and high-speed platforms.
• Perform 2D and 3D electromagnetic model extraction and power-noise analysis across the end-to-end power delivery path, including die/C4 bumps, package, socket, and board.
• Define and evaluate power-grid specifications, power-noise budgets, and design targets to balance power integrity, performance, area, and platform requirements.
• Apply power integrity principles and simulation methodologies to guide package and platform design and physical implementation.
• Analyze PDN impedance, voltage droop, resonance, ground bounce, decoupling effectiveness, and other power-noise characteristics.
• Develop electrical analysis methodologies, test structures, and verification plans for power delivery design and validation.
• Perform laboratory measurements to characterize power noise across frequency, transient response, ground bounce, and other key PDN metrics.
• Correlate post-silicon/platform measurements with pre-silicon simulations and models to improve design accuracy and methodology.
• Evaluate and optimize on-die, package, and platform decoupling strategies.
• Support voltage regulator (VR) performance characterization and optimization as part of the overall platform power delivery solution.
• Develop platform-level power delivery and decoupling recommendations for incorporation into platform design guides.
• Translate silicon power requirements into package and platform-level specifications and support design pathfinding to meet performance and form-factor requirements.
• Collaborate with silicon integration, die floorplanning, package, board/platform, voltage regulator, and validation teams to optimize the end-to-end power delivery solution.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Experience listed below would be obtained through a combination of your degree, research and or relevant previous job and or internship experiences.


Minimum Qualifications:
• Bachelor's in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, or a related STEM field & 1+ years of experience OR Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, or a related STEM field & 0+ years of experience.


• 1+ years of experience in one or more of the following areas:
Power integrity or power delivery.
Power electronics.
Signal integrity.
Voltage regulator design or validation.
PCB/package electrical modeling.
Electrical simulation.
Electrical laboratory testing or validation.

Preferred Qualifications:
The following qualifications are considered a plus:
• Experience with printed circuit board (PCB) and/or semiconductor package design and technology.
• Experience analyzing power delivery networks, including impedance, voltage-noise, transient-response, or decoupling behavior.
• Experience with electrical simulation, electromagnetic extraction, or high-speed design tools such as HSPICE, Ansys HFSS, Keysight ADS, Cadence PowerSI, or Cadence PowerDC.
• Knowledge of transmission-line theory, electromagnetic-field concepts, and passive component parasitics.
• Knowledge of voltage regulator operation, control, transient response, and interaction with platform-level power delivery networks.
• Experience using electrical laboratory equipment such as oscilloscopes, voltage/current probes, power supplies, and related measurement equipment.
• Experience correlating simulation results with laboratory measurements.
• Programming or scripting experience for engineering analysis and automation, such as Python, MATLAB, or similar tools.
• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and technical communication skills.

title: Senior Mixed Signal Post Silicon Validation Engineer IOs
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Team

The Hard IP Development Group (HIPD) within Intel's Central Engineering Organization is responsible for developing leadership IPs that are power-winning products for Server, Client, and Networking SOCs, as well as Intel Foundry Customers. HIPD develops a broad portfolio of Serial and Parallel IO PHYs including PCIe, USB, TypeC, UCIe Die-to-Die, DDR/LPDDR, and Ethernet PHYs.

The Electrical Validation and Debug group within HIPD is a dynamic and versatile team of engineers who directly engage with both IP design teams and SOC customers in IP validation and debug for test chips and products. These engineers embody our SOC customer obsession by validating mixed signal IPs and quickly resolving hurdles through hands-on debug.

This position is exciting and challenging, offering the opportunity to exercise your mixed signal design, architecture, and post-silicon debug expertise across all HIPD IPs, Client, and Server SOC teams.

Position Overview

This role focuses on mixed signal high-speed PHY post-silicon validation and debug, spanning IP enabling, customer sighting resolution, and cross-functional collaboration with SOC teams.

Key Responsibilities

• Generate test plans and test content for mixed signal high-speed PHY post-silicon validation, including characterization of Clocking, Transmitter, and Receiver blocks

• Perform IO protocol debug across one or more of the following: PCIe, UCIe, DDR, or Ethernet, from both PHY recipe and firmware perspectives

• Conduct SOC board design reviews, provide recommendations, and support post-silicon debug activities

• Represent the IP team during SOC Power-Ons for test chips and products, providing hands-on IP enabling support through proper recipes and firmware versions for PCIe, UCIe, and USB PHYs

• Identify clocking and PHY-related silicon issues, investigate, debug, and disposition customer bugs and sightings in a timely manner

• Reproduce customer issues and drive root cause analysis through failure analysis and structured debug methodologies

You Should Demonstrate the Following Professional Traits to Be Successful

  • Customer obsession with a strong sense of urgency in resolving technical issues
  • Versatility and adaptability when engaging across multiple teams, IPs, and debug scenarios
  • Collaborative mindset with the ability to work effectively with both IP design teams and SOC customers

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

• BS with 6+ years, MS with 4+ years, or PhD with 2+ years of experience in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field

• Relevant years of experience (as outlined above) in electrical or bench post-silicon validation with one or more high-speed PHYs such as PCIe, USB, UCIe, DDR, Ethernet, or equivalent interface experience


The experience must also include:

• Experience with lab hardware and software including Oscilloscopes, Logic Analyzers, Protocol Analyzers, and BERTs

• Knowledge of one or more industry-standard IO specifications such as PCIe, USB, or Die-to-Die UCIe


Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with mixed signal IP characterization including PLLs, TX and RX jitter characterization

• Experience leading IP debug efforts as situations arise, in addition to hands-on debug execution

• Signal integrity and power delivery knowledge

• Pre-silicon design or simulation experience in logic, circuits, firmware, MRC, or mixed signal validation

title: Power Delivery Integration and Power Rail Stress Engineer- SoC Power Thermal Performance Validation Engineer (Temporary position)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

As a SoC Power Thermal Performance Validation and Optimization Engineer, you will play an essential role in ensuring Intel's products achieve optimal power, thermal, and performance benchmarks at the system-on-chip (SoC) level.


In this position, you will develop and execute validation methodologies, optimize hardware/software solutions, and perform SoC-level debugging to address power, thermal, and performance challenges. Your contribution will directly impact Intel's ability to deliver competitive, high-performing products to market.

This is a Temporary position (12 months)


Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute System-on-Chip (SoC)-level power delivery, Power Rails Stress (PRS), maximum current (ICCmax), current transient (di/dt), minimum/maximum voltage (Vmin/Vmax), Digital Linear Voltage Regulator (DLVR)/Fully Integrated Voltage Regulator (FIVR), and concurrency plans, including feasibility study and design/verification/simulation of the Power Distribution Network (PDN) and sign-off of IR-drop/Electromigration (IR/EM) metrics, across Intel products.
  • Collaborate with architecture, design, firmware, software, Power Management architects, and layout teams to ensure power delivery meets competitive targets and specifications and to define and implement power gating solutions.
  • Establish and execute methodologies for validating hardware/software optimizations and to converge the design on all Power Distribution Network (PDN) metrics, ensuring alignment with business Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).
  • Perform System-on-Chip (SoC)-level debug to identify root causes and resolve functional and triage failures related to power delivery, on-die power grid/network, thermal, and performance.
  • Configure and set up data loggers to collect and analyze power/thermal data, and work with the package integration team to ensure the complete IP system meets the design specification.
  • Develop and maintain validation infrastructure (performance monitors, behavioral checkers, and testing environments) and work with the post-silicon debug team to triage, debug, and fix potential Power Distribution Network (PDN) issues.
  • Produce comprehensive validation reports summarizing activities and results and communicate findings effectively with relevant teams.
  • Drive continuous improvements to validation strategies, methodologies, and processes.

The ideal candidate should show the following behavioral traits

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Effective communication and documentation skills for cross-functional collaboration.
  • Advanced teamwork to work across teams in multi-faceted groups (architecture, design, verification, firmware, software, and platform teams).

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electronics, Electrical, Computer Engineering, or related field.
  • 1+ years of experience in System-on-Chip (SoC) power and performance validation and/or digital logic and optimization.
