title: Graduate Talent (Firmware Development)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

At Intel, we create world-changing technology that enriches the lives of every person on Earth. For more than 50 years, Intel innovations have powered the computing breakthroughs that shape how people live, work, and connect.

The Physical AI, Client and Edge (PACE) organization within the Client Computing & Physical AI Group (CCPG) is driving the next wave of intelligent computing by bringing Artificial Intelligence closer to where data is created and decisions are made. From intelligent edge devices and robotics to autonomous systems and AI-enabled industrial solutions, PACE develops technologies that enable the future of Physical AI.

As part of this mission, the Firmware & Functional Safety Technologies (FFST) organization develops critical platform firmware technologies that power Intel's next-generation products. Firmware is where hardware and software come together, enabling silicon features, platform reliability, security, performance, and functional safety capabilities.

As a Graduate Talent in the Boot Firmware Engineering (BFE) team, you will work alongside experienced firmware engineers to develop and validate low-level platform firmware for Intel reference platforms. You will gain hands-on experience in platform initialization, silicon enablement, system debugging, firmware automation, and AI-assisted engineering workflows while contributing to technologies that power millions of computing devices worldwide.

What You Will Do

  • Develop, integrate, and validate boot firmware components for Intel client and edge computing platforms.
  • Participate in firmware architecture discussions, feature design reviews, and requirement definition activities.
  • Design and execute unit tests, integration tests, and platform validation methodologies to ensure robust firmware quality.
  • Investigate, debug, and root-cause hardware, firmware, and system-level issues using industry-standard debugging tools and methodologies.
  • Develop automation scripts and engineering tools to improve development efficiency, test coverage, and product quality.
  • Collaborate closely with silicon architects, hardware designers, software engineers, validation teams, and platform integrators across Intel's global engineering network.
  • Apply Generative AI and Agentic AI solutions to accelerate code development, debugging, validation, knowledge discovery, test creation, and engineering productivity.
  • Explore new approaches to AI-powered firmware engineering by leveraging autonomous AI agents, intelligent workflow automation, and large language models (LLMs).
     

Qualifications:

We are seeking passionate graduates who enjoy understanding how systems work from silicon to software and are excited to build the technologies behind tomorrow's intelligent devices.

Successful candidates often demonstrate a strong curiosity for both hardware and software and enjoy building things beyond academic coursework.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's or Master's Degree in:
    • Computer Engineering
    • Electrical & Electronic Engineering
    • Computer Science
    • Embedded Systems
    • Mechatronics
    • Robotics
    • Related engineering disciplines
  • Strong programming skills in one or more of the following:
    • C
    • C++
    • Python
  • Understanding of computer architecture, embedded systems, operating systems, and software development fundamentals.
  • Strong analytical thinking, debugging skills, and problem-solving abilities.
  • Effective communication and teamwork skills.
  • Passion for learning emerging technologies and solving challenging technical problems.

Preferred Qualifications

Candidates will have an advantage if they possess hands-on experience through personal projects, hackathons, internships, university projects, or open-source contributions involving:

Embedded and Hardware Projects

  • Arduino, ESP32, STM32, RP2040, PIC, MSP430, or similar microcontroller platforms.
  • Raspberry Pi, Jetson Orin Nano, BeagleBone, or other embedded Linux platforms.
  • Robotics, IoT, sensor integration, autonomous systems, drones, or industrial automation projects.
  • Embedded Linux, RTOS, device drivers, or bare-metal firmware development.

AI and Intelligent Systems

  • Machine Learning or AI projects using TensorFlow, PyTorch, OpenVINO, ONNX, or similar frameworks.
  • Edge AI deployment on embedded devices.
  • Computer vision, speech AI, robotics AI, or autonomous systems projects.
  • Experience using AI-assisted development tools such as GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude, ChatGPT, or other AI coding assistants.

Agentic AI and Engineering Productivity

  • Development of AI agents, autonomous workflows, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, or multi-agent applications.
  • Experience integrating LLMs into software applications or engineering workflows.
  • Building automation pipelines that leverage AI for testing, debugging, code generation, or data analysis.

title: Manufacturing Quality and Reliability Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Role Summary

The Manufacturing Quality & Reliability Engineer drives product quality, manufacturing readiness, reliability assurance, and continuous improvement across semiconductor manufacturing operations. The role partners with development, engineering, operations, and customers to ensure robust product quality, successful new product introductions (NPI), and data-driven manufacturing excellence.

Quality & Manufacturing Excellence

Reliability & Data Analytics

title: Robotics Solution Architect (Quadruped Robots)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

We are seeking an experienced Senior Robotics Solution Architect to define and develop end-to-end technical solutions for quadruped robotics. This role combines deep robotics domain expertise, hands-on engineering experience, and strong system architecture capabilities to translate customer requirements into scalable, deployable solutions leveraging Intel technologies. The successful candidate will work closely with robotics OEMs, ecosystem partners, and internal solutions and engineering teams to address architectural challenges across compute, AI, perception, planning, control, and software infrastructure. The emphasis is on technical leadership, system integration, and engineering execution-from architecture definition and prototyping through validation and deployment. Key Responsibilities Lead end-to-end solution architecture for especially quadruped robotics, defining hardware and software partitioning, subsystem interfaces, compute topology, and deployment requirements. Translate robot-level requirements into detailed technical specifications, balancing performance, real-time responsiveness, power consumption, thermal constraints, reliability, and cost. Architect heterogeneous computing solutions across CPUs, GPUs, and AI accelerators, allocating workloads for perception, sensor fusion, localization, motion planning, and control. Define software architectures integrating robotics middleware, AI inference runtimes, real-time control frameworks, and development and debugging tools. Collaborate with robotics engineering teams to integrate embodied AI models and learning-based policies with robot software and control systems, addressing inference latency, resource constraints, and deployment readiness. Lead technical engagements with customers and partners, including architecture workshops, technical assessments, proof-of-concept development, integration reviews, and system-level troubleshooting. Establish benchmarking and validation methodologies covering end-to-end latency, throughput, timing determinism, power efficiency, and sustained operation under representative workloads. Develop reference architectures, technical documentation, and reusable integration guidance to accelerate engineering implementation. Work across silicon, platform, software, and robotics engineering teams to resolve architectural gaps and translate field requirements into actionable roadmap recommendations.

title: Principal Engineer, Analog and Mixed-Signal DTCO
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Group:

Intel's Advanced Design Foundational IP Organization (AD-FIP) within Design Technology Platform (DTP) drives pathfinding and development of the analog/mixed-signal, RF, and high-speed I/O IP that defines what Intel Foundry's leading-edge process technologies can deliver. The AMS Design-Technology Co-Optimization (DTCO) team sits at the intersection of process technology, design rules, PDK, EDA tools, and circuit design, making sure each new node delivers competitive analog, mixed-signal, and custom-design density, performance, and productivity.

The Role:

We are seeking a senior technical leader in DTCO to define and drive co-optimization of Intel Foundry's next-generation process technologies for analog, mixed-signal, and custom design. You will identify where technology definition limits design outcomes (density, drive, matching, high-voltage support, layout productivity), quantify the impact, and drive resolution across process, design-rule, PDK, EDA, and design teams. This is a senior individual-contributor role with technical leadership across multiple organizations and external EDA partners.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead AMS DTCO for future Intel Foundry nodes: evaluate device architecture, front-end and back-end design rules, metal stack, and patterning choices against analog, mixed-signal, and custom-design requirements.
  • Run a closed-loop DTCO process: sense issues from designers, partners, and test chips; prioritize by PPA and productivity impact; drive rule, PDK, or flow changes; and validate the result on silicon and in design.
  • Quantify technology impact on circuits through layout studies, parasitic-aware benchmarking, and area and performance scaling analysis of representative AMS building blocks.
  • Define and drive design-rule and PDK requirements with process, design-rule, OPC, and quality and reliability teams, including high-voltage device support, density and fill rules, metal width and spacing options, and layout-dependent effects.
  • Partner with EDA vendors on node enablement for custom and AMS flows: custom layout, analog placement and routing, physical verification, fill, and extraction; translate tool and flow feedback into technology decisions.
  • Represent Intel Foundry in technical engagements with EDA partners and foundry customers, and present DTCO findings and recommendations to technology and business leadership.
  • Mentor engineers and set technical direction for the DTCO team.

Required Skills and Experience:

  • 5+ years of DTCO experience for analog, mixed-signal, I/O, or custom design on FinFET or more advanced process nodes, at a foundry, an IDM technology-development organization, or an EDA vendor.
  • And experience in at least one of the following:
    • Design-rule definition for analog or custom layout, including layout-pattern studies, layout-dependent effects, and test-structure design to evaluate rule impact.
    • Circuit-level technology benchmarking of analog or mixed-signal building blocks: device-model and parasitic evaluation, matching, and area or performance scaling analysis.
    • EDA tool or flow enablement of analog and custom design for a new process node: custom layout, analog placement and routing, physical verification, fill, or extraction.

Preferred Skills and Experience:

  • Hands-on analog, mixed-signal, or RF circuit design experience (for example PLLs, data converters, regulators, high-speed I/O, LNAs, PAs, or mmWave front ends), with an understanding of how device and interconnect parameters drive circuit performance.
  • Analog and RF device and passive technology: precision resistors, MIM/MOM capacitors, inductors and transformers, varactors, analog and RF device flavors, and RF figures of merit such as fT, fmax, and noise figure.
  • Experience across two or more of the areas in the minimum qualifications, or across both foundry and EDA environments.
  • High-voltage or extended-voltage device integration on advanced CMOS nodes.
  • Analog or custom layout design experience.
  • Gate-all-around transistors, backside power delivery, or advanced multi-patterning (SALELE, EUV) technology definition as it affects analog and custom layout.
  • Automation of DTCO studies using Python, layout generators, or machine learning.
  • Customer-facing technical engagement with foundry customers or EDA partners.
  • Publications at IEDM, VLSI Symposium, CICC, ISSCC, or RFIC; patents in DTCO, design rules, design enablement, or AMS/RF circuits.
  • Technical leadership across process, design, and EDA organizations, including driving technology-definition decisions at node level.

title: Senior Principal Engineer, Device Design
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Group

Intel is transforming from an Integrated Device Manufacturer (IDM) to a leading global foundry service provider, offering world-class manufacturing capabilities to external customers worldwide. Our Manufacturing Development and Customer Engineering (MDCE) organization is at the forefront of this transformation-focusing on technology customization, yield improvement, performance optimization, and exceptional customer delivery.


About the Role
We are seeking a highly accomplished Senior Principal Device Design Engineer with broad semiconductor industry expertise to drive the high-level architecture, definition, and optimization of next-generation and high-volume manufacturing (HVM) semiconductor technologies. In this strategic technical leadership role, you will apply a deep mastery of semiconductor device physics to define technical roadmaps and ensure world-class performance across a diverse range of applications-including advanced logic, SRAM, low-power mobile, analog, and mixed-signal designs.
Serving as a primary technical bridge between Process Integration, Yield, and Module Engineering, and collaborative product partners, you will establish the technical direction, target validations, and silicon-to-simulation accuracy across Intel's diverse technology portfolio.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Technical Strategy and Architecture Leadership: Lead cross-functional, multi-disciplinary teams in defining base and derivative semiconductor architectures-including advanced transistors, interconnects, and design rules-tailored for high-performance logic, low-power, memory, analog, and mixed-signal applications.
  • Technical Partner and Customer Engagement: Partner directly with external customers, product design teams, and internal engineering groups to understand complex product requirements, resolve circuit-level performance/reliability/leakage trade-offs, and translate product needs into tailored silicon solutions.
  • Technology Customization and Optimization: Drive the development and implementation of customized semiconductor features across logic and memory technologies, ensuring seamless integration with existing manufacturing processes and platforms to support specialized applications.
  • Silicon-to-Simulation Readiness: Set and govern device and interconnect performance targets, evaluating silicon-to-simulation health, model readiness, and design feasibility for large-volume manufacturing.
  • Cross-Functional Integration: Serve as the authoritative technical interface bridging Process Integration, Process Module, Device Physics, Yield Engineering, and Product Design to coordinate complex technology handoffs and resolve system-level constraints.
  • Design Rule and Waiver Governance: Direct the validation and strategic waiver management processes for advanced design rules, balancing strict manufacturing compliance and yield with product design flexibility.
  • Advanced Data Analytics: Guide the evaluation of electrical test (E-test) and yield data using advanced statistical methods and data analysis techniques to translate experimental silicon data into actionable process and design intelligence.
  • Mentorship and Industry Thought Leadership: Provide senior technical mentorship to engineers and researchers across the organization, stay ahead of emerging semiconductor industry trends, and foster a culture of technical excellence and customer-centric innovation.

Required Skills and Experience:

  • Progressive experience in the semiconductor industry with a strong focus on CMOS device physics, device design, and semiconductor technology development.
  • Leadership and Technology Integration: Demonstrated technical leadership within the semiconductor industry, specifically leading cross-functional teams to define, develop, and deliver advanced semiconductor technologies (covering logic, memory, or integrated architectures) and design rules into High-Volume Manufacturing (HVM).
  • Design Rule Governance: Deep proficiency in design rule development, validation, and waiver management processes, with a strong understanding of how layout constraints impact product yield.
  • Data and Analytical Mastery: Proven expertise in statistical data analysis, Design of Experiments (DOE), and data interpretation to evaluate test chip, E-test, and yield trends.

Preferred Skills and Experience

  • Advanced and Specialty Node Expertise: Architectural experience in advanced-node transistor design and scaling, with deep experience in specialized semiconductor customization for low-power, analog, mixed-signal, and memory technologies.
  • Physical Verification and Mask Flows: High-level familiarity with physical verification flows, Design Rule Checker (DRC) development, and mask generation concepts.
  • Manufacturing and SPC: Extensive experience in a High-Volume Manufacturing (HVM) environment with a focus on statistical process control (SPC) and yield monitoring.
  • Executive Communication: Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to influence executive stakeholders and guide collaborative partners through complex technical trade-offs.

Qualifications:

  • Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Material Science, or a related field. PhD preferred
  • 15+ years of relevant semiconductor device and technology development experience.

title: Senior Manager, Technology and Software Procurement
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

As a Senior Manager, Commercial IP and EDA Procurement, you will lead a team dedicated to optimizing and enabling hardware engineering processes through strategic procurement and management of IP and EDA solutions. You will bridge engineering innovation with business execution, focusing on the acquisition and lifecycle management of critical commercial IP and EDA software/hardware that empower Research and Development, pilot lines, and high-volume manufacturing. Your leadership will inspire productivity, focus on meaningful results, and contribute directly to Intel's cutting-edge advancements in technology by ensuring a robust and strategic supply chain for IP and EDA. Key Responsibilities: Lead a systems and hardware enablement team, ensuring execution of deliverables through clear goal-setting, effective collaboration, and accountability for IP and EDA procurement initiatives. Develop and execute strategic sourcing and supplier development plans for Commercial IP and EDA, aligning with product and process technology roadmaps. Drive competitive negotiations and contract management for IP and EDA, securing optimal technical and commercial terms (e.g., pricing, lead time, IP/confidentiality considerations). Build and maintain robust supplier relationships with IP and EDA providers, fostering continuous improvement in cost, quality, capacity, and innovation. Partner closely with engineering and cross-functional teams to translate technical specifications into procurement strategies and influence design decisions for IP and EDA solutions. Mitigate supply chain risks and ensure continuity of supply for critical IP and EDA assets through proactive strategies. Contribute to cost governance and optimize total cost of ownership for IP and EDA solutions, identifying cost risks and opportunities. Support operational execution and ensure contract compliance for IP and EDA agreements, resolving issues across finance and legal.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:
Bachelor's degree in a relevant field and 10+ years of professional experience in procurement, supply chain, or engineering leadership roles, with significant focus on semiconductor hardware, systems, or manufacturing, and strong experience in Commercial IP and EDA procurement and negotiation.
Proven expertise in hardware engineering, systems enablement, and development processes, combined with experience in strategic sourcing for technical materials and services, specifically relating to IP and EDA.
Strong experience in managing cross-functional teams and driving collaborative engineering and procurement efforts.
Demonstrated ability to set clear goals, maintain accountability, and deliver results, particularly in negotiation, contract management, and supplier performance for technical commodities.
Proficiency in managing and optimizing engineering workflows and procurement processes, including should-cost modeling and risk mitigation for IP and EDA.

Preferred Qualifications:
Experience with product life-cycle development, including feature enhancement and debugging, from a supply chain perspective for IP and EDA.
Strong leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills for team development and fostering collaboration with internal and external partners.
Ability to inspire and motivate teams, driving innovation and growth in supplier technology enablement.
Knowledge of emerging trends in hardware engineering, IP/EDA, and familiarity with industry best practices in procurement and supply chain management.
